items.desc: Company: A leading quantitative proprietary HFT firm expanding into mid-frequency strategies across global equities and futures markets. Location: London The role: The firm is building a specialist machine learning team focused on large-scale sequential modelling for alpha generation. The team develops transformer-based and other deep learning models on market data, from representation learning through to forecasts that feed directly into live, risk-bearing equities and futures strategies. Responsibilities Design, train, and evaluate transformer-based and other sequential deep learning models (e.g. attention architectures, state-space models, recurrent networks) to forecast returns and related market quantities across equities and futures. Build and own the data and feature pipeline: how order book, trade, and bar-level data are tokenised and represented, how cross-asset and cross-sectional context is brought in, and how the models cope with non-stationarity and regime change. Develop rigorous training and validation frameworks for noisy, low signal-to-noise financial data, including leakage-safe cross-validation, walk-forward testing, and robust out-of-sample evaluation. Scale model training and inference on large GPU clusters, optimising for throughput, latency, and stability, working closely with ML infrastructure and engineering teams. Turn model outputs into tradable signals, working with portfolio construction and execution teams on turnover, transaction costs, and capacity. Iterate on live performance: monitor model behaviour and PnL in production, diagnose alpha decay and drift, and retrain and refine models over time. Requirements Advanced degree (PhD or MSc) in a quantitative discipline: Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, or similar. Expertise in modern deep learning, with hands-on experience building and training transformer-based or other sequential models at scale (e.g. attention mechanisms, self-supervised pre-training, state-space models). Demonstrable experience applying ML to financial time series in a systematic trading setting, ideally across equities and/or futures at mid-frequency horizons. Proficiency in Python and a major deep learning framework (PyTorch or JAX). C++ and experience with distributed training or high-performance computing environments are a plus. A track record of taking research into production and generating live PnL is highly valued. Publications at leading ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or experience at a top AI research lab are a plus. Experience with market microstructure or transaction cost modelling is preferred.

items.desc:
ABOUT US

Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.
Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity.
K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners.

Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK, Germany.

Please submit your CV in English




ABOUT THE ROLE:

 We are seeking a driven Research Scientist with hands-on expertise in Foundation Models (FMs) and Multimodal AI to help drive the next phase of our machine learning platform.

In this role, you will bridge cutting-edge AI research and practical application. Rather than training massive base models from scratch, your focus will be on fine-tuning, adapting, and aligning open-weights foundation models across diverse data modalities (e.g. structured tabular data, single-cell scRNA-seq, image representations, and natural language) to build multimodal systems.

 


IN PARTICULAR, YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR:

 - Model adaptation and optimization: Adapt, fine-tune, and evaluate state-of-the-art open-source foundation models (e.g., domain-specific transformers, vision-language models) using fine-tuning and transfer learning strategies.

 - Multimodal integration: Design and implement cross-modal alignment architectures (e.g., contrastive learning, projection heads, unified embedding spaces) to fuse structured, sequential, and text/image data layers.

 - Pipeline and evaluation engineering: Build rigorous, domain-tailored benchmarking frameworks and evaluation pipelines to validate model reliability, generalization, and downstream task performance.

 - Applied R&D collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams (data engineers, domain specialists, and software engineers) to integrate adapted models into scalable production and inference workflows.

 - Low-hanging fruit innovation: Identify high-impact, incremental improvements in data pre-processing, embedding representation, and fine-tuning to maximize model performance without unnecessary computational overhead. 

 


ABOUT YOU

Required qualifications / experience:

 - Education: Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics or a related quantitative field.

 - Experience: 2-4 years of post-degree experience applying deep learning and foundation models to complex datasets.

 - Foundation models: Demonstrated experience adapting and fine-tuning foundation models.

 - Multimodal learning: Proven experience with cross-modal representation learning, joint embedding alignment (e.g., CLIP-style architectures), or vision-language models.

 - Technical stack:
   
   - Advanced proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, Hugging Face ecosystem).
   
   - Hands-on experience with fine-tuning techniques.
   
   - Familiarity with data engineering tools for handling large-scale or multi-modal datasets (Parquet, AnnData, HDF5).

 Preferred qualifications/bonus:

 - Experience working with biological or omics data (e.g., scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, clinical and/or histology data).

 - Experience deploying or scaling models using containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP).

 - Track record of open-source contributions or peer-reviewed publications at top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR) or domain-specific journals.

 

 #LI-HB1


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Flexible work organization

 - Friendly and informal working environment

 - Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds


RECRUITMENT PROCESS & SECURITY

 - Please complete the form and submit your CV.

 - Owkin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status or on the basis of disability.

items.desc:
Company: 
Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. 
 Job Area: 
Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Machine Learning Researcher 
 General Summary: 
 Qualcomm AI Research is seeking world-class researchers to help push the boundaries of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Our team pioneers new algorithms, models, and systems that advance the state of the art while delivering exceptional performance with unprecedented power, memory, and computational efficiency. 
 Our multidisciplinary team brings together expertise across algorithms, software, hardware, and systems. We pursue fundamental and applied research, from foundational theories and novel learning algorithms to efficient AI systems deployed on resource-constrained devices. Working closely with Qualcomm's business and engineering teams, we translate research breakthroughs into technologies deployed worldwide across mobile, compute, automotive, robotics, cloud, XR, and IoT platforms, while publishing at leading AI conferences. 
 Our team has demonstrated world-first research breakthroughs and proof-of-concepts across model efficiency, representation learning, perception and understanding, generative and foundation models, reasoning and agentic intelligence, and embodied and physical AI. Our research contributions have earned numerous best paper awards, major research competition wins, and top rankings on AI and computer vision benchmarks. We also translate these breakthroughs into highly optimized AI models, end-to-end workflows, and developer tools for Qualcomm platforms, making many innovations accessible to all. Explore our research and innovations: 
 Research Breakthroughs and Demonstrations 
 Qualcomm AI Research Publications and Innovations 
 Qualcomm AI Hub: Optimized Models and Workflows 
 Role Responsibilities: 
 Research interns will contribute to fundamental and applied research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, developing novel algorithms, models, and systems that advance the state of the art. Research opportunities span a broad range of areas, including: 
 Generative AI and Foundation Models: Large language models (LLMs), multimodal foundation models, vision-language models (VLMs), vision-language-action models (VLAs), world models, and generative modeling for language, image, video, audio, and 3D content. Research topics include diffusion and autoregressive models, mixture-of-experts, parallel decoding, long-context modeling, and knowledge distillation. 
 Agentic AI and Reasoning: Autonomous agents, multi-agent systems, reasoning, planning, and verification; memory management, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), inference-time optimization, robustness, alignment, AI safety, and hallucination mitigation. 
 Efficient and Scalable AI: Novel neural architectures, efficient attention mechanisms, transformers, state-space models, and recurrent networks; model compression, pruning, quantization, neural architecture search, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and efficient training and inference. Research also includes on-device AI, edge-cloud learning, distributed training, hardware-aware optimization, and compiler and kernel optimizations.

Progettare il preprocessing degli spettri: baseline, allineamento,
items.desc: Chi siamo Siamo una giovane azienda specializzata in intelligenza artificiale per dati scientifici. Sviluppiamo sistemi proprietari e brevettati di AI per analizzare spettri NMR e lavoriamo con clienti industriali e scientifici internazionali, tra cui grandi gruppi dell’energia e della chimica. Siamo un team piccolo e molto qualificato. Ci piacciono il pensiero rigoroso e concreto, l’onestà intellettuale e poca burocrazia. Vogliamo un’azienda con un’alta concentrazione di talento, dove persone capaci possano fare il lavoro migliore della loro carriera. Il ruolo Svilupperai i modelli di deep learning al centro dei nostri prodotti, compresi i foundation model per la spettroscopia NMR. Seguirai tutto il percorso: definizione del problema chimico, dataset, architettura, training, validazione e messa in produzione. Un modello per noi è buono quando funziona su dati reali ed è chimicamente plausibile, non solo quando ha buone metriche. Per questo la sensibilità chimica è importante quanto quella da ML. Cosa farai Progettare, implementare e addestrare reti neurali per spettri e segnali scientifici: transformer, autoencoder, modelli sequenziali e generativi. Contribuire ai foundation model NMR con pretraining, self-supervised learning, fine-tuning e transfer learning. Costruire dataset di grandi dimensioni e pipeline di training riproducibili su GPU. Progettare il preprocessing degli spettri: baseline, allineamento, normalizzazione, riduzione dimensionale. Confrontare i modelli neurali con approcci chemiometrici classici (PCA, PLS, PLS-DA) e scegliere il più adatto. Definire una validazione solida dal punto di vista statistico e chimico, e studiare robustezza, generalizzazione, data leakage e dominio di applicabilità. Portare i modelli in produzione e ottimizzarne l’inferenza. Tradurre i problemi dei clienti in obiettivi computazionali, insieme a chimici, software engineer e partner scientifici. Stack Python, PyTorch (o TensorFlow), NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn, strumenti di experiment tracking e versionamento di modelli e dataset, container, cloud (AWS, GCP o Azure). GPU Nvidia H100 e DGX Spark. Requisiti essenziali Machine learning Almeno 3 anni di esperienza pratica nello sviluppo di modelli di deep learning. Ottima conoscenza di Python e PyTorch o di un framework equivalente. Hai progettato e addestrato reti neurali tu stesso, non ti sei limitato a usare modelli preesistenti o API. Solida comprensione di generalizzazione, regolarizzazione e validazione dei modelli. Chimica Laurea magistrale o dottorato in chimica, chimica fisica, chimica computazionale, chemiometria o in un ambito affine con una forte componente chimica. Esperienza concreta di ML applicato a dati chimici o spettroscopici (NMR, IR, Raman, MS, cromatografia) o a dati molecolari. Capacità di giudicare se il risultato di un modello ha senso chimicamente. Altro Buon inglese scritto e parlato. Autonomia e capacità di affrontare problemi aperti con informazioni incomplete. Costituiscono un plus Esperienza diretta con la spettroscopia NMR. Foundation model, self-supervised learning o apprendimento multimodale. Training distribuito e ottimizzazione su GPU. Cheminformatica (RDKit, rappresentazioni molecolari), elucidazione strutturale o predizione di proprietà. Uncertainty quantification e interpretabilità. MLOps, CI/CD e deployment in produzione. Pubblicazioni, codice open source o esperienza in startup o in contesti internazionali. Questo ruolo non fa per te se… hai una forte formazione chimica o chemiometrica ma non hai mai addestrato una rete neurale in PyTorch o TensorFlow; hai una forte esperienza in ML ma non hai mai lavorato con dati chimici o spettroscopici; cerchi un ruolo solo di ricerca o solo di engineering: qui servono entrambi. Cosa offriamo RAL tra 28.000 € e 36.000 €. Equity Lavoro ibrido. Un giorno di ferie in più per il tuo compleanno. Un ambiente basato su fiducia e flessibilità, con pochissima burocrazia. Problemi scientifici difficili con un impatto diretto su prodotti e clienti.

items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. items.desc:
About Us 
 Huawei is a global leader in information and communications technology (ICT), driving innovation and shaping the future of an intelligent world. With a presence in over 170 countries and a strong commitment to research and development, Huawei continues to push the boundaries of technology. 
 Huawei's European Research Institute (ERI) brings together more than 1,500 researchers across over 20 sites in Europe, including our Research Center in Switzerland. 
 Our Swiss research laboratory focuses on pioneering next-generation computing architectures and systems for the AI era , spanning innovative hardware, software, and algorithms. Working closely with leading universities and academic partners worldwide, we foster an open, collaborative research environment dedicated to fundamental scientific breakthroughs and long-term innovation. 
 Our vision is to become a world-leading research center for computing architectures and systems in the AI era, shaping the future of intelligent computing. 
 About the Team 
 We are a research team based in Europe, working at the intersection of Generative AI, Video and Efficient AI. We collaborate closely with leading universities and research institutions, and with engineering teams, to explore and build the next generation of efficient multimodal AI systems. 
 Our work centres on efficient real-time video generation. We are moving toward mixture-of-experts (MoE) video models, streaming world models, and models that keep learning while they generate. 
 The team has two streams: Architecture and Systems, and Multimodal Efficiency. This position is in the Multimodal Efficiency stream, which makes video and multimodal models faster and cheaper at the model and algorithm level, and works closely with the systems stream to run them in real time on NPU/GPU clusters. 
 The Role 
 We are looking for a Research Scientist who has recently completed a PhD to make large multimodal and video generation models faster and more efficient. You will work hands-on on research projects within the Multimodal Efficiency stream: implementing ideas, running experiments at scale, building working systems and publishing, with mentoring from senior researchers. 
 What You Will Work On 
 Depending on your background, you will work hands-on on one or two of these topics and contribute across the others. 
 · Token efficiency for video: adaptive, content-aware token compression and merging, and positional encodings (e.g. RoPE) designed to work with compressed or multi-resolution tokens 
 · Long-horizon and streaming generation: memory- and KV-cache-efficient autoregressive video, history compression, and few-step and streaming distillation 
 · Sparse and structured attention for long video sequences 
 · Step distillation, caching across denoising steps, and pruning 
 · Quantization and low-precision inference (FP8/FP4, MX formats) for diffusion and flow-matching models 
 · MoE video models: expert routing and MoE-specific acceleration 
 · Efficient end-to-end execution of large multimodal models, including VAE encoding and decoding, and joint audio-video generation 
 · Efficient agentic multimodal pipelines: agents that call LLMs, VLMs and video/speech generators, with KV cache reuse across steps and latency-aware planning 
 · Workload analysis and hardware-aware model design: compute, memory and latency models that guide algorithm choices on NPUs and GPUs, together with the systems stream 
 Your Responsibilities 
 · Drive research projects within the team roadmap: from idea to prototype to results at scale 
 · Implement, train and optimize models yourself, and turn results into working systems and demos 
 · Run careful experiments: strong baselines, ablations, and measurements of quality, latency and memory 
 · Work with the systems stream and engineering teams to profile and accelerate models on NPU/GPU clusters 
 · Publish at top venues (CVPR, ICCV/ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, SIGGRAPH, MLSys) and contribute to open-source projects 
 · Propose new research ideas 
 · Help supervise interns as you grow in the role 
 What We Are Looking For 
 · PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning or a related field, completed recently or to be completed within 6 months 
 · At least one first-author publication at a top venue in generative AI, computer vision, multimodal AI or efficient ML

items.desc: Wanna join the adventure? Loft Orbital flies other people's payloads on standardized satellites, giving our customers a fast, simple, and reliable path to orbit. Our AI for Space team is looking for a motivated intern to explore how fast, lightweight “System 1” models can boost reactivity, performance, and usability across our satellite operational chains. Reactivity use cases are at the heart of Loft's vision, and we are scaling them: from single-satellite reactive loops, to two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue (a detection from one sensor automatically cueing an acquisition by another), and ultimately multi-satellite scenarios. Today we mostly rely on “System 2” models — powerful but slow and heavy at inference — from our partners. “System 1” models (fast, intuitive) are coming back strongly and could add value not only on reactivity, but also on performance and ease of use. This internship will assess that added value and prototype it on our reactivity scenarios. Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station) Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027. About this role: Review the state of the art on System 1 / fast, intuitive models and compare them with the System 2 models used today, including our partners' models Map where System 1 models could bring value in our operational chain for reactivity use cases, from detection to tasking Define benchmark scenarios of increasing complexity with the team: a single-satellite reactive loop, then a two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue loop, and, as a stretch goal, a multi-satellite scenario Set the latency budget, accuracy needs, and execution context for each scenario Build datasets and evaluation sets from Loft data, partner outputs, and open datasets Train or fine-tune System 1 models and benchmark them against System 2 baselines on reactivity (latency), performance (accuracy, compute footprint), and ease of use (integration and operational effort) Prototype an end-to-end reactive loop, possibly as a hybrid design where System 1 triggers and System 2 validates, and assess how it extends to multi-satellite coordination Document results and recommendations for production use, and deliver a final demo Must Haves: Final-year engineering or Master's student specialized in ML / deep learning / computer vision Solid Python and PyTorch skills, and good software engineering practices Strong understanding of the state of the art in LLM / VLM / Reinforcement Learning Practical experience training neural networks (language models or computer vision) and/or LLM manipulation Nice to Haves: Model optimization (quantization, distillation, edge inference) Exposure to satellite or geospatial data Multi-agent or distributed systems experience Genuine interest in space What Can We Offer? You will join the AI for Space team and directly support the scaling of reactivity use cases, a core part of Loft's vision — working toward shorter detection-to-tasking latency on single-satellite and tip & cue scenarios, and a first step towards multi-satellite reactive operations. You'll build new expertise on an emerging class of models, reusable across other detection-like use cases, with a concrete prototype and benchmark the team can build on. With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, USA | Golden, USA | and Toulouse, France. Some of our awesome internship benefits: Gratification: €1,300 gross/month Lunch vouchers (tickets restaurant), because let's be honest, we love food! (we even have a Slack channel about it: #loft-gourmand) Sustainable mobility package (forfait mobilité durable) A genuinely international environment comprising 20+ different nationalities A genuine mentoring program to support you on a daily basis throughout the internship Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions. We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes Who We Are Loft: Space Made Simple. Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit. We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives. items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

items.desc: L'École normale supérieure de Lyon produit une recherche de haut niveau dans ses 25 laboratoires et forme par la recherche quelque 2500 étudiants dont 500 doctorants. Elle compte environ 550 enseignants, enseignants-chercheurs et chercheurs et 600 personnels administratifs et techniques. Dans le classement de Shanghai et QS, elle apparaît parmi les tous premiers établissements français en termes de performance per capita. Son objectif est d'avoir un impact significatif en matière de recherche, d'innovation et de transfert de technologie tout en irriguant la fonction publique et le monde socio-économique de diplômés rompus à la complexité, capables de produire et transmettre des savoirs. L'ENS de Lyon met ses ressources au service d'une vision ouverte de la société et des enjeux contemporains qu'elle veut éclairer. Son budget annuel est d’environ 160 M €. L'ENS de Lyon est une école dynamique, où la qualité de vie au travail, le développement durable et l’égalité professionnelle représentent des dimensions centrales. Le Poste Persée est une Unité d'appui et de recherche, qui numérise, enrichit et diffuse le patrimoine documentaire au bénéfice de la recherche, principalement à travers le portail de publications scientifiques en accès libre. Persée est engagé dans le GIS CollEx-Persée, inscrit sur la feuille de route nationale des infrastructures de recherche, qui regroupe des bibliothèques de recherche et des opérateurs de l’IST dans le but de développer et d’outiller l’usage par les chercheurs des collections des bibliothèques. Le poste est proposé dans le cadre du programme de Numérisation enrichie de CollEx-Persée, qui en assure le financement. MISSIONS La Mission IA est une mission transverse de l’unité. Elle conçoit et met en œuvre l’application de l’intelligence artificielle aux chaînes de traitement documentaire, de l’expérimentation à la production, afin de livrer à grande échelle des métadonnées fiables, interopérables et réutilisables ( corpus as data ). items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices. You will build agentic tools and automation that make our audio ML research dramatically faster and more reproducible. The focus is on orchestrating training, evaluation, experimentation, and reporting across many types of AI models, using on-premise and/or cloud GPU infrastructure. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Design and implement agentic workflows that plan, launch, monitor, diagnose, and summarize audio ML experiments, with appropriate human oversight. Automate data preparation, model training, hyperparameter searches, benchmarking, regression testing, and result comparison across research projects. Build reliable tooling for on-premises GPU scheduling and utilization, experiment tracking, artifact management, and reproducible execution. Connect LLM-powered agents to scripts, repositories, datasets, evaluation suites, and compute resources through well-defined tools and safeguards. Partner with audio researchers to turn repetitive experiments into reusable workflows and clear dashboards or reports. Education Degree in computer science, machine learning, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Skills Strong software engineering and Python skills, with hands-on experience building LLM agents or agentic workflows that invoke tools and execute multi-step tasks. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience with ML training and evaluation pipelines, PyTorch, experiment tracking, and automated testing. Practical experience operating on-premises Linux GPU machines, including CUDA environments, containers, job scheduling, and resource monitoring. Working knowledge of audio ML and DSP, including common datasets, audio metrics, and model development workflows. Experience with orchestration frameworks, distributed training, CI/CD, or MLOps is a plus. Ability to build reliable, observable systems and communicate effectively with research scientists. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! items.desc:
OUR MISSION

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.



TEAM CULTURE

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. 

 - You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

 - No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

 - We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

 - Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

 - Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates. 
   The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

 - Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

 - We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.


REQUIREMENTS

 - At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

 - As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

 - Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:
   
   - Test Driven Development (TDD)
   
   - Trunk based development
   
   - Continuous integration
   
   - Domain Driven Design


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

 - Large parts of our training pipeline are built on top of Kubernetes.

 - We do not hire for skills in a particular technology or language, but rather ability to learn and mindset, yet experience with these technologies is a plus.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Become part of an AI revolution!

 - 30 days of paid vacation

 - Access to a variety of fitness & wellness offerings via Wellhub https://wellhub.com/de-de/

 - Mental health support through nilo.health http://nilo.health/

 - Substantially subsidized company pension plan for your future security

 - Subsidized Germany-wide transportation ticket

 - Budget for additional technical equipment

 - Flexible working hours for better work-life balance and hybrid working model

 - JobRad® https://www.jobrad.org/ Bike Lease

Note: We welcome applicants at every stage of their career. Your drive and willingness to learn are far more important to us than strict experience requirements.

items.desc: Systems Research Engineer - Distributed Systems / OS / AI Infrastructure Join a global technology organisation carrying out ambitious research into the computing infrastructure behind large-scale cloud and AI platforms. Working across operating systems, distributed computing, networking, storage and accelerator-based hardware, the company is exploring fundamental systems problems and turning the strongest ideas into technology used in real deployments. This research engineering role is a chance to combine original systems research with hands-on building. Your work will run from defining the problem and forming hypotheses, through implementation, benchmarking and in-depth performance analysis, to publishing at top-tier venues. Write rigorous, original research for leading systems conferences such as OSDI, SOSP, NSDI, EuroSys, SoCC and MLSys. Work with researchers, architects and engineering teams across the wider organisation to validate ideas and turn successful work into deployable infrastructure. Solid grounding in computer systems, covering one or more of: operating systems, distributed systems, computer architecture or cloud platforms. Strong systems programming skills in C/C++ (or a similar language), plus Python for prototyping and running experiments. Proven ability to build and assess systems through careful experimental design, benchmarking and profiling. An analytical approach to problem solving and a real curiosity about original systems research. Clear communication skills and comfort working within a multidisciplinary research group. Preferred: Papers published at, or the clear potential to publish at, leading systems conferences. Preferred: Experience in areas such as resource scheduling, performance engineering, heterogeneous computing or ML systems. Preferred: Knowledge of AI infrastructure, such as model serving, distributed training, accelerator platforms or inference optimisation. Prenatal medicine is particularly complex, and the scans impose heavy responsibilities on healthcare professionals. They can also be a source of stress for future parents. Based on patented algorithms and a proprietary expert database, Sonio aims to become the reference tool to help practitioners improve screening, reduce diagnostic errors, and optimize pregnant women’s medical path. Sonio's mission is to improve women's and children's health by promoting access and quality of care through technological innovation, medical expertise, and collective intelligence. items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Most agent frameworks are designed for short-lived workflows, best-effort execution, and a narrow set of tools. Callosum is building for a different world: agents that run for weeks, operate across distributed infrastructure, and interact with stateful systems where failures, retries, and side effects must be handled explicitly. Success in this environment requires an agent runtime built entirely from first principles. Sitting at the heart of our technical mission, this position owns the runtime and programming model for long-running agent systems. Your focus will span durable execution, checkpointing and replay, distributed scheduling, secure tool execution, and end-to-end observability. You will develop the core software that makes agent workflows reliable, debuggable, reproducible, and efficient as we expand our model and tool footprint. This is a high-leverage role tackling complex systems challenges across the entire stack. Runtime, observability tooling, and framework design are three separate specialties. We are glad to hire someone with real depth in a combination of them. What You'll Build Design and build stateful, asynchronous agent runtimes across distributed environments Define event histories, checkpoint and resume semantics, deterministic reconstruction, retries, cancellation, timeouts, and recovery from partial failure Build traces and replay, time-travel debugging, and hierarchical tracing across model calls, tools, handoffs, state changes, and runtime decisions Develop clear Python APIs, libraries, and DSLs with stable extension points for tools, backends, and new execution models Design scheduling, placement, backpressure, resource accounting, sandboxing, permissions, and isolation for secure tool execution at scale Develop tooling for trajectory collection and visualisation, performance profiling, experiment comparison, failure attribution, and regression detection across models, prompts, tools, and runtime versions What You'll Bring We are looking for real strength in some of the following rather than coverage of all of it. Strong distributed systems background with hands-on experience in durable workflows, actor systems, schedulers, workflow engines, distributed databases, or stream processors Experience designing a library, framework, runtime, or DSL that other engineers or researchers adopted Deep Python expertise plus proficiency in a systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go - and the instinct to move between abstraction layers when it matters Hands-on debugging skills across APIs, runtimes, and distributed infrastructure - with a practical understanding of nondeterminism, side …

items.desc: We have an exciting opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to investigate how phytoplankton physiology influences ocean carbon cycling. The successful candidate will join a UK-US research project, From Monod to Macromolecules: assessing nutrient-carbon coupling in a hierarchy of ocean-ecosystem models, based at the University of Southampton and working in collaboration with researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). The project will compare different approaches to representing phytoplankton physiology within the MITgcm-Darwin ocean ecosystem model. The successful candidate will implement and evaluate a range of physiological sub-models with the MIT virtual ocean environment, to investigate which aspects of cellular physiology are important for predicting nutrient cycling, primary production and carbon export. The work will involve developing and testing numerical models, running global ocean simulations and analysing model outputs alongside oceanographic observations. There will also be opportunities to investigate how the effects of physiological complexity depend on environmental variability and ecological interactions. We are looking for someone with strong quantitative and programming skills, and experience developing or analysing numerical models. A background in marine ecology, oceanography, biogeochemistry, applied mathematics or a related field would be beneficial. Experience with Fortran, high-performance computing and/or marine ecosystem models would be advantageous, but is not essential. At Southampton, you will work closely with Dr Ben Ward and Professor Mark Moore, in collaboration with Professor Mick Follows, Dr Stephanie Dutkiewicz and colleagues at MIT. You will also have opportunities to work with staff and students across the wider Marine Biogeochemistry research group and the School of Ocean and Earth Science at the University of Southampton. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the publication of research findings in peer-reviewed journals and to present their work at national and international scientific conferences. We welcome applications from all candidates with an interest in the role, and those who are committed to helping us create a diverse and inclusive work environment. We encourage applications from candidates from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, people who identify as LGBTQ+ and people with disabilities. We recognise that employees may wish to have working patterns that fit with their caring responsibilities or work-life balance. Due consideration will be given to applicants who have had career breaks for reasons including maternity, paternity or adoption leave, disability or illness. We offer a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days, subsidised health and fitness facilities and access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS). Applications for Research Fellow positions will be considered from candidates who are working towards or nearing completion of a relevant PhD qualification. The position is full-time and fixed-term for 20 months, with an anticipated start in early 2027. For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Ben Ward (b.a.ward@soton.ac.uk). Working at the University of Southampton Find out more about the staff benefits and working at the University of Southampton.

items.desc:
About Us 
 Huawei is a global leader in information and communications technology (ICT), driving innovation and shaping the future of an intelligent world. With a presence in over 170 countries and a strong commitment to research and development, Huawei continues to push the boundaries of technology. 
 Huawei's European Research Institute (ERI) brings together more than 1,500 researchers across over 20 sites in Europe, including our Research Center in Switzerland. 
 Our Swiss research laboratory focuses on pioneering next-generation computing architectures and systems for the AI era , spanning innovative hardware, software, and algorithms. Working closely with leading universities and academic partners worldwide, we foster an open, collaborative research environment dedicated to fundamental scientific breakthroughs and long-term innovation. 
 Our vision is to become a world-leading research center for computing architectures and systems in the AI era, shaping the future of intelligent computing. 
 About the Team 
 We are a research team based in Europe, working at the intersection of efficient AI, generative models and distributed systems. We collaborate closely with leading universities, research institutions and engineering teams to make advanced AI workloads practical on modern computing platforms. 
 Our work includes large multimodal and video-generation systems, but our research questions span a broader range of AI models and workloads. We focus on performance, scalability and efficiency through advances in inference, compilation, distributed execution and AI-driven optimization. 
 The Role 
 We are looking for a hands-on Research Scientist with a strong background in AI performance optimization. items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. For more information, visit: www.interdigital.com. Summary The objective of this internship is to design a deep learning model for generating energy-aware images. Methods for producing energy-aware images — that is, images that consume less energy than their original versions when displayed on a screen — already exist in the literature. These approaches typically aim to achieve a trade-off between reducing energy consumption and preserving the visual quality of the resulting images. However, Several Research Directions Remain To Be Explored Existing approaches mainly focus on reducing the luminance component of images, while we would also like to investigate the colour dimension. We would like to explore perceptual loss functions, i.e., losses designed to better reflect the characteristics of the human visual perception system. Current methods struggle to maintain a satisfactory quality-energy trade-off at high power reduction ratios. We would therefore like to investigate how the research directions above could improve performance in this more challenging range. The objective is to develop a model that combines these different aspects to improve both visual quality and energy efficiency compared with state-of-the-art approaches. This work represents a further step towards a more sustainable video streaming chain. In the context of climate change, reducing the environmental footprint of video streaming is an important part of the broader effort to reduce carbon emissions. The internship will first involve reviewing existing approaches for perceptual quality assessment and colour modelling of images. In a second stage, a deep learning-based model will be designed and implemented to generate energy-aware images using these new features. The performance of the proposed model will then be evaluated in terms of both image quality and energy consumption. The internship will take place within the Media Services research group at the InterDigital Video Lab. The intern will be mentored by research scientists and will contribute to a research project focused on developing solutions to reduce energy consumption across the video streaming ecosystem.  Help shape the future of healthcare AI, where innovation meets trust.

items.desc: Reasonable is the applied AI research company building formal verification for super-human software development. Join us to develop the next frontier of formal reasoning and software engineering. Proof follows function. We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Member of Technical Staff specialized in Post-Training and Evaluations to join our Reinforcement Learning & Formal Methods team. items.desc: At the Faculty of Medicine, Department of Health Science and Technology, a PhD stipend in AI and Medical Imaging for Stroke Prediction and Personalised Care is available for appointment from 1 February 2027 or soon thereafter. The advertised position is one of several PhD and postdoctoral positions established as part of the Centre for AI in Health at Aalborg University. The appointment is for a period of three years. The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD programme in Biomedical Engineering and Neuroscience at the Faculty of Medicine. Who we are: The Department of Health Science and Technology (HST) at Aalborg University is an interdisciplinary research and teaching environment where engineering, medicine and health sciences come together to improve people's lives. As a PhD fellow at HST, you will become part of an international research community with access to experienced supervisors, modern research facilities and strong interdisciplinary collaboration. You will work alongside researchers from a wide range of disciplines and engage with hospitals, industry and public-sector partners to address some of society's most important health challenges. We offer a stimulating research environment that encourages scientific curiosity, collaboration and professional development. The Faculty of Medicine is committed to preparing PhD graduates for diverse career paths. Throughout your PhD, you will develop advanced research competencies alongside transferable skills that prepare you for careers in academia, industry and the public sector. Towards the end of your PhD, you will be offered dedicated career development support to help you plan your next career step. At HST, our values – Share. Care. Dare. – shape the way we collaborate, support one another and create knowledge with societal impact. Learn more about the department on our website and in our research portal. About the Centre for AI in Health: The Centre for AI in Health is a strategic initiative by the Faculty of Medicine that brings together researchers from the Department of Clinical Medicine and the Department of Health Science and Technology. The centre combines clinical, technical and methodological expertise to advance the development, evaluation and implementation of AI in healthcare. The successful candidate will become part of this interdisciplinary research community. Learn more about the Centre for AI in Health and the centre’s signature projects website. About the Project: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide. While many patients who experience a transient ischaemic attack (TIA) or minor stroke subsequently recover well, a substantial subgroup is at high risk of recurrent stroke and adverse outcomes. Identifying these patients early and ensuring timely intervention remains a major clinical challenge. At the same time, increasing amounts of data are becoming available across the patient pathway. These include prehospital assessments, neuroimaging, vascular imaging, clinical records and longitudinal follow-up data. The challenge is, how to integrate these heterogeneous data sources into clinically meaningful prediction and decision-support tools. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal learning and foundation models create new opportunities to address this challenge. The overall goal of this PhD project is to develop novel AI methods that support early risk stratification, clinical decision-making and personalised care for patients with TIA and minor stroke. The project is part of the Centre for AI in Health signature project AI for Cardiovascular and Stroke Care , which aims to develop AI solutions supporting prevention, prediction and time-critical clinical decisions across the care continuum. The project will leverage multimodal data collected across the patient pathway, including prehospital data, neuroimaging, vascular imaging, clinical records and longitudinal patient data. Particular emphasis will be placed on developing methods that are clinically relevant, robust, explainable and transferable across healthcare settings. Potential research directions include: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Neurovascular Imaging Learning clinically meaningful imaging representations from large-scale neuroimaging data. Multimodal Foundation Models for Risk Prediction in TIA and Minor Stroke Integrating prehospital, imaging, clinical and longitudinal patient data for personalised risk prediction. Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware AI for Neurovascular Decision Support Developing trustworthy AI methods for transparent and reliable clinical decision-making. items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. For more information, visit: www.interdigital.com. Summary This internship will explore neural-network-based representations for the encoding, representation, generation, and manipulation of haptic data. It will build on previous work on Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) for haptics and on probabilistic haptic rendering, with the objective of investigating learned representations that support both compact encoding and controllable transformation of haptic effects. The work will compare architectures such as autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and INRs for sample-based and/or parametric haptic data. Beyond reconstruction, the intern will investigate selected manipulation and generation tasks relevant to haptic authoring, including filtering, interpolation, completion/inpainting, temporal extension, and real-time procedural generation. Candidate methods will be assessed in terms of reconstruction quality, controllability, generalization, and computational cost. The internship may build on recent internal work on haptic effect analysis and temporal extension to explore data-driven approaches for generating missing or extended haptic content. Target use cases may include gaming and haptic authoring tools. The work may lead to prototype software, internal demonstrators, and potentially publication and/or patent contributions. Responsibilities The intern will join the haptics research team within the New Media Codec group at InterDigital (Rennes). The work will consist in: Studying the state of the art on neural representations and generative models for haptic and temporal signals, including autoencoders, GANs, and INRs Designing and implementing neural representations for encoding, reconstruction, and controllable manipulation of sample-based and/or parametric haptic effects Exploring selected authoring and generation tasks such as filtering, interpolation, inpainting/completion, temporal extension, and real-time procedural generation Evaluating the proposed methods and developing demonstrators for haptic authoring or gaming, with potential contributions to publications and patents Qualifications Master’s student (or 4th year engineering school) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Robotics, or related field Strong Python programming skills and experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow Good knowledge of neural networks, representation learning, and signal processing Nice To Have Experience with autoencoders, GANs, INRs, or generative models for temporal data Knowledge of haptics, audio, time-series processing, or interactive systems Experience with C++, real-time systems, or game engines Keywords Haptics, Neural Networks, Generative Models, Autoencoders, GANs, INR, Representation Learning, Procedural Generation Expected Outcomes Prototype software, demos, potentially publications and patents Location Cesson-Sévigné, France InterDigital is an equal employment opportunity employer. items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. For more information, visit: www.interdigital.com. Summary Hybrid implicit neural representations (INR) compress images by combining learnable feature grids with lightweight neural networks. The grids capture spatial information at multiple resolutions, while a compact network transforms these features into pixel values. Both components are jointly optimized for each image to balance bitrate and reconstruction quality. The resulting latent features and network parameters are quantized and encoded into a compressed bitstream. During decoding, the features are recovered and processed by the network to reconstruct the image. This approach enables efficient image reconstruction with low decoding complexity, at the cost of more computationally intensive encoding. The objective of this internship is to investigate underlying architectures used by hybrid INR. Starting from an existing framework, the intern will explore how to adapt and tailor entropy, up sampler and synthesis networks to the specific image to encode. The proposed methods will be evaluated in terms of rate-distortion performance, rendering quality, retraining complexity, and encoding time. You will be working in the SympAI team, in the New Media Codecs Group of the Video Lab. Responsibilities In collaboration with the InterDigital research team, the candidate will be expected to: Analyze existing technologies and identify core challenges related to Hybrid INR compression. Contribute to the design and development of software solutions addressing these challenges Perform rigorous testing and validation, including simulation-based evaluations, to ensure functional correctness and performance in line with established protocols. Implement, test, and validate the proposed components and algorithms. Communicate technical outcomes effectively, contributing to documentation, internal reports, and potentially to publications or intellectual property filings. Qualifications Master’s student in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Strong proficiency in C/C++ and Python is required. Familiarity with one or more of the following areas is a plus: 3D geometry, compression, computer vision, or computer graphics. Fluent in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrates strong collaboration abilities and a team-oriented mindset. Keywords Hybrid INR, image compression, model fine-tuning, rate-distortion optimization, neural rendering, quality enhancement. The resulting latent features and network parameters are quantized and encoded into a compressed bitstream. During decoding, the features are recovered and processed by the network to reconstruct the image. This approach enables efficient image reconstruction with low decoding complexity, at the cost of more computationally intensive encoding. The objective of this internship is to investigate warmup phases that are used prior the real encoding. This phase aims to start the encoding in the best condition. Starting from an existing framework, the intern will explore how to adapt and tailor the warmup phases to the specific image to encode. The proposed methods will be evaluated in terms of rate-distortion performance, rendering quality, retraining complexity, and encoding time. You will be working in the SympAI team, in the New Media Codecs Group of the Video Lab. Responsibilities In collaboration with the InterDigital research team, the candidate will be expected to: Analyze existing technologies and identify core challenges related to Hybrid INR compression. Contribute to the design and development of software solutions addressing these challenges Perform rigorous testing and validation, including simulation-based evaluations, to ensure functional correctness and performance in line with established protocols. Implement, test, and validate the proposed components and algorithms. Communicate technical outcomes effectively, contributing to documentation, internal reports, and potentially to publications or intellectual property filings. The role Frontier robotics and embodied AI live or die by the quality of their training data, yet the infrastructure to curate, evaluate, and scale multimodal real-world inputs remains largely broken. Backed by over $100M from top-tier venture funds and serving more than 300 AI and robotics teams globally, this company builds the foundational data layer for Physical AI. With continuous access to massive, proprietary multimodal streams, their dedicated frontier research lab operates on real-world edge cases that academic benchmarks cannot replicate. As a Research Engineer, you will lead original research directly driven by open problems from leading robotics labs. This is not ivory-tower benchmarking on synthetic toys, nor is it standard ML operations; you will formulate hypotheses, run experiments end to end, build working prototypes, and ship your methods straight into a core platform while retaining the mandate to publish. Your scope covers agentic multimodal workflows, automated data curation, and pushing the boundary on egocentric video and 3D scene understanding. The work Formulate hypotheses, design rigorous experiments, and drive original research targeting open challenges in multimodal data curation, model evaluation, and automated quality control. Prototype agentic workflows that leverage modern vision-language models to interpret complex real-world ontologies and unstructured sensor inputs. Tackle frontier video problems, advancing models from egocentric dense captioning toward deep 3D spatial and temporal scene understanding. Build end-to-end prototypes in PyTorch and partner with ML systems engineers to transition proven architectures directly into production. Publish novel methodologies and represent the research lab at major computer vision and machine learning conferences. items.desc:
Research Scientist in Scientific AI and Geotechnical Engineering 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Research Scientist in Scientific AI and Geotechnical Engineering
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The Chair of Geotechnical Engineering at ETH Zurich, part of the Institute for Geotechnical Engineering (IGT), focuses its teaching and research on foundation engineering, soil mechanics and natural hazards. Our objective is to combine theoretical knowledge with experiments and numerical simulations to develop new methods for understanding and predicting the behaviour of soils, foundations and infrastructure. 
 We are opening a position in our research group at ETH Zurich, focusing on developing and integrating modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods into geotechnical engineering research, while maintaining a strong connection to the underlying physics and mechanics. We do not aim to develop a new AI model or replace physics-based engineering with purely data-driven AI. Instead, we want to use AI to transform the way research itself is performed—from numerical model generation and experimental data acquisition to analysis, visualization and communication.
 For this purpose, we are looking for a Research Scientist in Scientific AI and Geotechnical Engineering, who will work across the research group, collaborating with PhD students, postdoctoral researchers and senior scientists.
 The role combines scientific research, computational engineering, research automation, data science and the development of reusable AI-enabled tools. A central objective is to identify new opportunities where AI can enable research that would otherwise be difficult or impossible, and to develop capabilities that can be used across the entire group.
 Job description
 The job will interconnect several different areas of our activity:
 Scientific AI and physics-informed modelling 
 Develop and apply AI and machine-learning approaches to challenging problems in geotechnical engineering and computational mechanics, with particular emphasis on approaches that combine data with physical knowledge, rather than relying exclusively on black-box, data-driven models.
 Explore topics including physics-informed and physics-guided machine learning, hybrid physics–ML constitutive modelling, surrogate and reduced-order models, inverse problems and parameter identification, uncertainty quantification, and AI-assisted scientific discovery.
 Apply these methods to problems involving soil behaviour, soil–structure interaction, liquefaction, natural hazards, foundations and infrastructure resilience.
 AI-enabled numerical modelling 
 Develop tools for automating and accelerating numerical modelling workflows, including finite element (FE) and potentially discrete element (DEM) and material point method (MPM) simulations.
 Automate tasks, such as model generation, geometry and mesh creation, assignment of materials and boundary conditions, parameter studies, high-performance computing (HPC) execution, model verification, extraction of results and standardised post-processing.
 Create robust and reusable tools that enable researchers throughout the group to build and analyse numerical models more efficiently while retaining appropriate engineering control and verification.
 Automation of experimental research 
 Develop AI-enabled methods for the acquisition, processing and interpretation of experimental data from laboratory and centrifuge testing.
 Automate sensor-data processing, synchronization of different measurement systems, computer-vision analysis of experiments, extraction of deformation and failure mechanisms from images and videos, identification of experimental parameters, and integration of experimental and numerical results.
 Geotechnical data intelligence 
 Develop methods to exploit the growing volume of geotechnical data available within the group and through external repositories.
 Organize and extract information from historical laboratory and centrifuge experiments and numerical analyses, and exploit large external datasets and research repositories such as DesignSafe and databases containing geotechnical and geological properties.
 Contribute to the longer-term development of structured, physics-aware geotechnical datasets to support parameter inference, model calibration, uncertainty quantification, identification of model deficiencies and the development of new physics-informed AI approaches.
 Scientific visualisation and communication 
 Develop automated approaches for transforming research results into high-quality visualisations, animations and videos.
 Develop tools that support scientific publications and presentations while facilitating effective communication of research through websites, teaching materials, professional audiences and social-media platforms.
 Group-wide AI capability 
 Help establish AI as a broadly accessible research capability within the group.
