items.desc: As a public expert in weather and climate, Météo-France is here to help keep you safe every day and assist you in making the best decisions in a changing climate. With dangerous weather events becoming even more intense and frequent due to climate change, our mission to keep you safe is crucial. We mobilize our expertise and scientific and technological excellence to enable you to anticipate and adapt to challenging weather and climate events. Find us online:https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france The position will be at CRNM in Toulouse, in the GMAP group. (GMAP is responsible for operational models at Météo-France), with collaborations on this theme with the ECMWF and with others ACCORD country. The DESR brings together the research entities of Météo-France (mainly CNRM, SAFIRE and LACy), the Ecole Nationale de la Météorologie and the shared administrative and IT support services (PGA). The CNRM is a Joint Research Unit (UMR 3589) under the joint supervision of Météo-France and CNRS. The CNRM conducts research in the field of meteorology and climate, from the observation, understanding and modelling of processes to the development of weather forecasting and climate projection systems that can be transferred to Météo-France's operational services. The GMAP (Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision - Modelling and Assimilation Group for Forecasting), based in Toulouse, is one of the CNRM's 6 research groups or centres. Its mission is to maintain and develop Météo-France's operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems and to conduct research in preparation for future versions. Why join us? Embark on a stimulating adventure that serves everyone, alongside men and women who are committed every day to tackling the challenges posed to our society by weather and climate. And enjoy the following benefits: flexible working hours, RTT (reduced working time), teleworking, staff restaurant or meal vouchers, 75% contribution to public transport costs, contribution to mutual insurance, sports and cultural associations depending on the site concerned (climbing, gym, pottery, theater, etc.). Other benefits await you, come and discover them! Responsibilities The aim of the position is to develop and evaluate a short-range regional weather forecasting model using artificial intelligence for the Indian Ocean region. The successful candidate will have the following responsibilities: Adapt the Météo-France AI model, currently being developed for forecasting over Western Europe, to run over the Indian Ocean region; evaluate the model’s performance and compare it, in particular, with that of the Arome-Indien operational model; implement and evaluate fine-tuning strategies to adapt the AI model to the specific challenges of the French overseas territories : it is expected to propose innovative solutions to significantly improve the prediction of extreme events, including tropical cyclones; work as part of a team: the position is based at the CNRM in Toulouse but requires regular interaction via videoconference with a research team in La Réunion island. Additional Information Position open to people with disabilities, Position in office hours Remote work (1 day per week) An engineering degree is desired as well as confirmed experience in a similar position. To fill this position, you will mobilize the following skills : Know-How A master degree in atmospheric sciences, statistics or artificial intelligence ; a PhD is an advantage A strong background in deep learning algorithms, in particular graphe networks Experience in geophysical problems would be appreciated, at least a strong interest for applied research in atmospheric physics is highly recommended Expert proficiency with Python programming and AI librairies (PyTorch) Some experience with the Anemoi software environment is highly desirable Experience with processing large volumes of data (distributed dataloading and computing frameworks) Experience of working in a Linux-based environment Social Skills Ability to carry out scientific work, and to communicate in writing and orally in English A scientific curiosity, independance and rigourr Application deadline: 11/30/2026 Emails from people to contact for any further information : laure.raynaud@meteo.fr , thomas.rieutord@meteo.fr

ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



The Role

Mistral AI is looking for AI Scientists with deep machine learning expertise and hands-on engineering experience to expand what Mistral's agentic tools can do across the engineering lifecycle across CAE (CFD, FEA etc) and EDA/Semi.. 

Within AI4Engineering Science, your core work is building the pre and post-training data for Mistral's LLMs to reason about and execute real engineering tasks. Alongside this, you'll help shape the agent architectures and harness that let these models operate reliably inside multi-step engineering workflows, not just answer isolated questions.

You'll work closely with domain experts across CAE and EDA to ground this work in how engineers actually work, and with the broader research team to translate that domain grounding into training signal and evaluation benchmarks that measure genuine task competence.

What You Will Do

 - Design pretraining, SFT, and RL data for engineering tasks across CAD, CAE, and semiconductor/EDA

 - Define verifiers and evaluation criteria that capture what "correct" and "high-quality" actually mean for each engineering task, beyond surface-level plausibility

 - Design and improve agent architectures and harnesses: how models plan, call tools, recover from errors, and chain steps together across long-horizon engineering workflows

 - Build evaluation benchmarks and diagnostic tooling to identify where models fail on engineering tasks, and trace those failures back to gaps in data, reward design, or agent scaffolding

 - Collaborate with domain experts across CAEand EDA (and the science and solutions teams more broadly) to identify which engineering workflows are highest-value to target next

 - Contribute to Mistral's broader pre and post-training research, sharing findings and methodology across the science organization

What We're Looking For

 - Fluent English with excellent communication skills, able to explain technical ML and engineering concepts to both engineering and non-technical audiences

 - Deep, hands-on machine learning expertise, particularly LLM development

 - Demonstrated experience running, debugging, and validating real engineering workflows in at least one of CAD, CAE, semiconductor simulation, or EDA. 

 - You write clean, readable Python code and are comfortable in Linux/HPC environments

 - Self-directed, you don't need detailed roadmaps to make progress

 - Low-ego, collaborative, and eager to learn at the intersection of engineering and ML

It would be great if you

 - Have experience building or fine-tuning agentic systems (tool use, multi-step planning, agent orchestration frameworks)

 - Have experience with reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF/RLVR, or preference-based training

 - Have industrial or academic experience with CAE, or EDA tools (e.g. SolidWorks, CATIA, Fluent, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, STAR-CCM+, Cadence/Synopsys/Siemens EDA tools)

 - Have contributed to a large open-source or industry codebase

 - Have publications in engineering and ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, JFM, AIAA, etc.)

 




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.desc: Research Scientist in Provenance Research and Forest Tree Breeding (f/m/d) Location: Großhansdorf Start date: At the earliest possible date Organization: Institut für Forstgenetik (FG) Working hours: Full-time / part-time possible Application deadline: 10.12.2026 The Institute of Forest Genetics of the Johann Heinrich von Thünen Institute, Federal Research Institute for Rural Areas, Forestry and Fisheries, is seeking to fill a full-time position (currently 39 hours per week) as a Research Scientist in Provenance Research and Forest Tree Breeding (f/m/d) at its Großhansdorf location, starting as soon as possible. The position combines long-term employment prospects with opportunities for scientific development: 50% of the position is permanent and involves the management and further development of forest genetic field trials, as well as data analysis and data management. The remaining 50% is offered on a fixed-term basis for up to four years and is dedicated to scientific qualification, providing opportunities for independent research, externally funded projects, policy advice, and knowledge transfer. Our research group has a clear mission: to conserve genetic diversity, maintain the growth performance and stress tolerance of broadleaved and coniferous trees, and identify climate-adapted provenances, thereby making an important contribution to securing the future of Germany's forests. At the Thünen Institute of Forest Genetics, we maintain a nationwide network of field trials to assess genetic and phenotypic variation within native and non-native tree species and evaluate the suitability of different provenances under varying site conditions. Our research focuses on adaptive capacity and phenotypic plasticity under current and future climatic conditions. Breeding programmes for selected tree species aim to increase biomass production and the yield of high-quality timber while maintaining wood quality, vitality, and disease resistance. State-of-the-art phenotyping and genomic technologies enable the targeted selection of traits that enhance the economic viability and sustainability of forest management. The position is partly intended to support the successful candidate's scientific qualification and offers, among other opportunities, the possibility of pursuing a PhD. The Thünen Institute collaborates with several universities for this purpose. The fixed-term component of the employment contract is governed by the maximum permissible duration under Section 2(1) of the German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz, WissZeitVG). Employment is governed by the Collective Agreement for the German Federal Public Service (TVöD Bund). Subject to meeting the relevant collective agreement and personal requirements, remuneration will be based on pay grade E13 TVöD Bund , corresponding to an annual gross salary of €62,489.15 to €89,579.84 for full-time employment. items.desc: Who we are Resonance is an Applied AI company, founded by a team of seasoned operators and engineers from Europe's leading software investor and a leading AI consultancy. Collectively we've shipped 30+ AI products, embedded AI into 50+ businesses and created $250m of value for them. AI models are improving faster than companies can use them. The models are good enough today. What's missing is building AI into how a company actually works, and that's what we do. We work with ambitious companies to help fundamentally rewire how they work with AI, and accelerate their growth. Our mission is to help companies reinvent themselves for the AI era and cross the emerging AI productivity gap. The role We are looking for graduates to join Resonance as Applied AI Engineers. You'll join our first graduate cohort in London or Berlin. What you'll do Build and ship Ship production code on client teams: agents, integrations, data pipelines and evals Work across the stack, from the AI layer to the client's core systems and the interfaces people use Contribute to Resonance's own AI products and shared platform Learn the business Sit with the people who do the work today and see how AI changes it Help client teams run and extend what we build Grow at pace Coaching from senior engineers who have worked at some of the top AI companies globally Take on more ownership as you grow, and help shape our company as a key member of our team Your first year Training: Comprehensive training when you join, covering AI engineering, our platform and how we work with clients Your first project: On a client team from your first month, with a Senior Applied AI Engineer who reviews your code and coaches you Progression: You'll start as a Junior Engineer and typically become an Engineer within 18–24 months How we work A small team: You'll know everyone by name, founders included, and work closely with people across London and Berlin Questions welcome: Nobody expects you to know it all when you start. items.desc: Mission Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives. items.desc: Are you passionate about uncertainty and explainability of large language models in healthcare? We invite applications for two PhD positions on language model reasoning for uncertainty communication and explanation in healthcare. Working at the UvA Join Us! We invite applications for two PhD positions within a new Horizon Europe project ‘Bringing Explainability, Verifiability and Trustworthiness into Multimodal LLMs in the Clinical Practice’. Our team is researching how uncertainty, interpretability and explanations work together to help users judge when to rely on automated decisions. The two successful candidates will join us in advancing the state-of-the-art of techniques for explainability and uncertainty representation in LLM-based reasoning agents, with a particular focus on challenging healthcare data. The research will explore how to best represent and communicate the state of uncertainty of a generative model, as well as how to best extract, organise and communicate supporting explanations of a model’s response. As healthcare data are composed of long, multimodal, structured and unstructured clinical documents, the project will also involve research into long-context reasoning and tool use. The two positions will contribute to these shared research themes, with room to develop distinct questions and approaches. We welcome applicants with a broad range of interests, including natural language processing, explainable AI, machine learning, human-computer interaction, and related fields. Possible directions include, but are not limited to: PhD 1: Structured and explainable representations of uncertainty (e.g., hierarchical Bayesian models, graph-based representations, structure prediction). Mathematical tools for uncertainty representation beyond probability (e.g., possibility measures, belief functions, ranking functions). Cognitively plausible approaches (e.g., from psychology and psycholinguistics) to uncertainty representation and communication. Evaluation of uncertainty quantification usefulness. PhD 2: Conversational and configurable evidence-grounded, uncertainty-aware explanations (e.g., informed by input/data/causal attribution). Explanation methods for long and multimodal clinical records, including how to locate, organise, and cite relevant evidence across documents. Developing XAI tool-using agents. Evaluation of explanation reliability and usefulness (incl., human-centred studies of how explanations support understanding and decision-making) The successful candidates will work in a team together with Wilker Aziz and Vlad Niculae, and two postdocs, within several larger collaboration networks: A Horizon Europe consortium with more than a dozen partner institutes from Europe, UK and Canada The Language Technology lab at the Informatics Institute at UvA The Natural Language Processing unit at the Institute for, Logic, Language, and Computation at UvA Potentially, the ELLIS international doctoral network. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do Each of the two PhD positions is expected to carry out the following tasks in support of the corresponding project described above. Tasks and responsibilities: leading state-of-the art research on the project described; collaborating with researchers in the network and beyond; publishing academic papers in peer-reviewed international conferences and journals in NLP, ML, and related fields; presenting your work in national and international venues; assisting in teaching duties, for example as teaching assistant for bachelor and master’s courses, and supervising bachelor and master’s final projects; engaging in lab, institute, and research center activities, such as seminars and various rotating organizational roles; completing your PhD thesis within the appointment duration of four years. items.desc: Position description Category Engineering science Contract Internship Job title Internship in Artificial Intelligence-Saclay- H/F Subject Active Learning for Continual Category Discovery Contract duration (months) 6 mois Job Description As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Context : Most image-recognition systems are trained with labeled examples and a fixed list of categories. After deployment, however, new images continue to arrive. Their visual appearance may change because of a different style, camera, or environment, and the system may also encounter categories absent from its initial training data. In continual category discovery a model first receives labeled images from known categories, then successive collections of unlabeled images containing both known and genuinely new categories. It must recognize known categories, form groups for new ones, and retain what it has learned over time. The main challenge is that visual similarity does not always mean that two images show the same category. A known vehicle represented as a sketch may look less similar to photographs of the same vehicle than to a visually close but new vehicle category. The internship will investigate methods to resolve these ambiguities with limited expert feedback. What do we expect from you ? The intern will work on the following tasks : Conduct a literature review on methods for category discovery, visual domain adaptation and active learning Analyze when changed appearances of known categories are confused with genuinely new categories Select informative images for expert feedback under a limited query budget Use this feedback to improve category discovery and maintain categories over time Evaluate the approach against fully automatic and randomly queried baselines This internship offers an introduction to research in machine learning and computer vision. Depending on the results, it may lead to a scientific publication and may be pursued with a PhD focused on a similar topic. # Cea-List Methods / Means Python, PyTorch Applicant Profile Students in their final year of studies (M2 or last year of engineering school) Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning and computer vision Interest in visual representation learning, continual discovery, or active learning Python proficiency in a deep learning framework Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France, Essonne (91) Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Master 2 Recommended training Informatique avec spécialisation en intelligence artificielle PhD opportunity Oui Requester Position start date 01/03/2027

items.desc: Job number MED06074 Faculties Faculty of Medicine Departments Department of Infectious Disease Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Hammersmith Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 4 Jan 2027 About the role Supported by BBSRC funding, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join the group of Dr Rachel Lai at Imperial College London. This 48-month position, available from January 2027, will investigate how metabolic rewiring and cellular ion fluxes govern innate immune responses and inflammation. Macrophages are essential sentinels of innate immunity, but their dysregulated activation drives severe inflammatory diseases. Macrophage activation requires the convergence of biophysical and biochemical inputs, including acute metabolic shifts, ionic fluxes and oxidative stress. Working within a dynamic, multi-institutional team, you will employ biological and analytical assays and tools to define the physiological checkpoints that determine how macrophages integrate these stress signals and transition from homeostasis to a proinflammatory state. What you would be doing You will lead studies investigating how metabolic and ionic shifts govern macrophage activation, taking responsibility for experimental planning and execution, data analysis and manuscript preparation. Working closely with members of the Lai group and collaborators across the multi-institutional team, you will develop and apply experimental approaches to deliver the project’s scientific aims. You will also supervise and train students, share expertise with colleagues and contribute to the day-to-day running of the laboratory. You will present findings at scientific conferences, prepare reports for research funders and contribute to future grant applications. What we are looking for We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with: A PhD in Immunology, Physiology, Cell Biology or a closely related discipline. Practical experience with primary macrophages or relevant cell-culture models, with strong knowledge of innate immunity and macrophage biology. Experience studying immunometabolism or cellular physiology, including functional immunology and biochemical assays. Ability to lead independent research and work collaboratively, with experience in experimental planning, data analysis and scientific writing. Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable but not essential: measuring cellular ion fluxes or transporter/channel activity, mass spectrometry-based proteomics or metabolomics, bioinformatics or computational analysis of omics datasets, or working with small-animal models. Holding a relevant UK personal licence would also be advantageous. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term post for 48 months. items.desc: Graduate Research/Algorithm Engineer (DSP, Sensor Systems) Whiteley, Fareham (3 days per week in office) Up to £38,000, or up to £42,000 with a relevant PhD Your new company You'll be joining the European headquarters of a high-growth, innovation-led semiconductor business developing next-generation human-machine interface technology. The Research team focuses primarily on capacitive touch sensing, helping to shape advanced touch ICs used within OLED display panels and other future-facing products. This is a highly collaborative R&D environment where ideas move from initial research and modelling through to system validation. Engineers work hands-on across hardware, firmware, software, data analysis and system modelling, using agile methods to solve complex technical problems and turn early concepts into robust product technology. The role is hybrid and you'll be required to work three days per week onsite in Whiteley. You must have a relevant Degree to apply, ideally at PhD level. Your new role This is a graduate or early-career opportunity to build specialist expertise in algorithm engineering, working on RISC-V-based capacitive touch controllers and the physical sensing technology behind them. The position is designed for someone with up to one year of relevant experience who enjoys combining mathematical problem-solving with hands-on experimentation. Working alongside experienced engineers, you'll investigate how physical sensors behave and turn measured signals into reliable algorithms. You'll contribute to touch-detection and signal-processing work involving filtering, calibration and noise rejection, while learning how sensor physics, mixed-signal electronics and digital processing interact in real products. Using MATLAB, Simulink and/or Python, you'll help build models of capacitive sensors, analogue front ends, ADCs and digital signal-processing chains. You'll collect and analyse measurements from prototypes and IC evaluation platforms, compare experimental results with model predictions, and create repeatable simulations and tests to quantify performance improvements. You'll also support algorithm verification, basic fixed-point evaluation and the handover of research into firmware or digital hardware implementation, collaborating with IC design, firmware and system-validation engineers throughout the process. What you'll need to succeed You'll hold a BEng/BSc, MEng/MSc or PhD in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Physics or Applied Physics, Signal Processing or a closely related subject. You'll have sound fundamentals in signals and systems, including sampling, filtering and time and frequency-domain analysis, supported by good numerical and mathematical reasoning. You'll also understand electronic circuits, sensors or physical measurement systems and be interested in how noise, interference and other real-world effects influence performance. Experience gained through university research, projects, placements or personal development involving MATLAB, Simulink or Python will be valuable. Exposure to FIR or IIR filters, FFTs, fixed-point arithmetic, analogue or mixed-signal electronics, ADCs, laboratory instrumentation, SPICE, FPGA or HDL development, Embedded C/C++, microcontrollers or RISC-V would be advantageous rather than expected in depth. Projects involving physical sensors, signal acquisition, sensor fusion or machine learning applied to measured data would be particularly relevant. Above all, you'll be curious, methodical and able to explain your technical reasoning clearly. What you'll get in return You'll join a technically ambitious R&D team where you'll learn directly from experienced algorithm, IC, firmware and validation engineers while applying your academic knowledge to real physical systems and semiconductor products. The base salary is up to £38,000 for a graduate or postgraduate candidate, rising to up to £42,000 for someone holding a relevant PhD. The benefits package also includes private health and dental cover, an EV car salary sacrifice scheme, mental health assistance programmes and wider wellbeing support, alongside hybrid working from modern offices in Whiteley. What you need to do now To find out more or to be considered, please apply directly or get in touch for a confidential discussion with Max Wilcock, Senior Business Director, on 0333 010 5724. As demand for specialist engineering talent continues to grow, we work closely with organisations and individuals to create opportunities where people can make a real impact.

items.desc: As a researcher at Flanders Make, you will help develop next-generation operational intelligence platforms for manufacturing ecosystems. You will research and implement interoperable software frameworks that enable companies to securely exchange and operationalize data, knowledge, and manufacturing capabilities across organizational boundaries. You translate cutting-edge concepts such as data spaces, semantic interoperability, and AI-driven reasoning into real industrial applications, contributing to resilient, sustainable, and flexible manufacturing ecosystems. Your work will support advanced industrial use cases such as Manufacturing-as-a-Service, resilient supply chains, circular value chains, and cross-company operational coordination throughout the product lifecycle. You will contribute to European ecosystem initiatives and frameworks such as Gaia-X, Manufacturing-X, Catena-X, and emerging Digital Product Passport ecosystems. Your role You will join an interdisciplinary research environment where experts in software engineering, AI, systems engineering, optimization, and manufacturing technologies collaborate on real industrial challenges. Together with industrial and academic partners, you will design and validate software frameworks for federated operational intelligence across manufacturing ecosystems. These frameworks enable semantic interoperability, capability matchmaking, distributed decision-making, and operational coordination between companies in complex manufacturing value chains . FUNCTION You will: Design and develop operational intelligence platforms for cross-company collaboration; Translate manufacturing data and knowledge management challenges into reference architectures and semantic models; Implement solutions based on Data spaces, Knowledge graphs, Digital twins and/or Distributed architectures; Develop decision-support and coordination mechanisms (e.g. capability matchmaking, distributed optimization); Contribute to emerging European initiatives such as Gaia-X, Manufacturing-X and Catena-X; Collaborate with industrial and academic partners across Europe; Share results through demonstrators, publications, and presentations. PROFILE You combine strong technical expertise with systems thinking and a passion for applied research. Required: A Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI or related field; Minimum 3 years of industrial experience or research experience; Strong skills in software engineering and modelling; Experience in one or more of the following: Semantic web technologies (RDF, OWL, SPARQL, SHACL, ...) Knowledge graphs / graph-based reasoning (GraphDB, Neo4j, N3, Apache Jena, ...) Data space technologies (EDC-Eclipse Dataspace Components, Solid, ...) Distributed systems and interoperability. Nice to have: Knowledge of Gaia-X, Catena-X, Manufacturing-X or IDS; Experience with digital twins, Asset Administration Shell, or AI reasoning; Experience with industrial data exchange. You are: Passionate about applied research and innovation; Able to bridge research and industry; Proactive and curious in fast-evolving domains; A strong collaborator in international teams. items.desc: The Role We are seeking an outstanding computational biologist to join the BioFAIR Pathfinder project to develop computational framework for gene regulatory network (GRN) inference methods in single-cell genomics. The project involves curating, harmonising single-cell and multimodal datasets, containerising and running, comparing GRN inference tools as a community resource. The role includes contributing to peer-reviewed publications and developing community, training and engagement opportunities with BioFAIR and ELIXIR-UK Southampton node. You will join the collaborative interdisciplinary environment within the School of Biological Sciences, working alongside a growing computational genomics community at Southampton. You will have access to IRIDIS HPC, with support from RSEs, and also collaborate nationally through BioFAIR project and ELIXIR-UK Southampton Node. About You You will have a quantitative or RSE background and an interest in applying computational and data-driven methods to single-cell genomics and gene regulation. We are looking for someone who can work confidently with large and varied single-cell datasets, and who enjoys developing, benchmarking, and testing new analytical approaches. Experience in single-cell bioinformatics, containerisation, and workflow development will be critical to the role, and we are interested in your ability to think clearly, learn new methods, and work well with others. The Pathfinder project has a community engagement aspect and will require someone who is comfortable engaging with researchers from different disciplines and institutions across UK and FAIR data community. Alongside the project, the role comes with benefits that will make your life easier, such as a generous holiday allowance and additional university closure days. As a university employee, you will have access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS)*, subsidised health and fitness facilities, and a range of discounts. This post is offered on a fixed-term basis for 12 months. For additional information or informal enquiries before submitting your application, please contact knn1y25@soton.ac.uk.

items.desc: About InterDigital InterDigital is a global research and development company focused primarily on wireless, video, artificial intelligence (“AI”), and related technologies. We design and develop foundational technologies that enable connected, immersive experiences in a broad range of communications and entertainment products and services. We license our innovations worldwide to companies providing such products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, cars and other motor vehicles, and providers of cloud-based services such as video streaming. As a leader in wireless technology, our engineers have designed and developed a wide range of innovations that are used in wireless products and networks, from the earliest digital cellular systems to 5G and today’s most advanced Wi-Fi technologies. We are also a leader in video processing and video encoding/decoding technology, with a significant AI research effort that intersects with both wireless and video technologies. Founded in 1972, InterDigital is listed on Nasdaq. InterDigital is a registered trademark of InterDigital, Inc. For more information, visit: www.interdigital.com. Summary Context Neural Video Codecs (NVCs) use learned representations and neural-network-based transforms to compress video. Recent codecs such as Microsoft’s DCVC-RT [1] demonstrate that neural video compression is approaching the performance required for real-time applications. These codecs differ from conventional video codecs in their compressed representations, prediction dependencies, model requirements, and decoder state. Their bitstreams therefore do not naturally fit existing media containers and packetization formats. Media over QUIC Transport (MOQT) [2] is being developed within the IETF to support low-latency media distribution over QUIC. The NMSF Internet-Draft [3] proposes an initial method for packaging neural video frames as MoQ Groups and Objects. This proposal requires implementation and experimental evaluation against realistic codec behavior and network conditions. Objective The internship will investigate how an existing real-time neural video codec, such as Microsoft DCVC-RT, can be packaged and transported over MOQT. The student will study the state of the art, implement and evaluate an NVC proposal, identify its limitations, and propose improvements or an alternative packetization approach where justified. Responsibilities Review the state of the art in neural video compression, real-time media transport, QUIC, MOQT, and media packetization. Keywords Neural video coding, NVC, DCVC-RT, Media over QUIC, MOQT, NMSF, QUIC, real-time media, video packetization, low-latency streaming. Expected Outcomes A state-of-the-art analysis of NVC transport over QUIC and MOQT. A functional NVC-over-MOQT evaluation testbed. An implementation and experimental evaluation of NMSF. items.desc: Location: Europe (Remote) Company: US-headquartered life sciences and AI company Engagement: Full-time international contractor arrangement Compensation: Competitive Performance-based earnings The Opportunity Are you a gene therapy scientist who enjoys solving complex biological problems, interpreting experimental data, and challenging scientific assumptions? We are recruiting on behalf of a rapidly growing US-based life sciences technology company working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and biomedical research. The company develops scientific evaluations that test whether advanced AI systems can accurately interpret biological data, solve complex research problems, and make scientifically defensible decisions. We are looking for an experienced scientist in gene therapy, gene delivery, or genome editing who can translate their specialist expertise into rigorous scientific challenges for AI systems. This is not a traditional wet-lab or AI software engineering position. Your value lies in your scientific judgment, understanding of experimental methods, and ability to distinguish genuine biological findings from misleading results. What You Will Do Design challenging scientific evaluation tasks based on real gene therapy research, experimental datasets, and published studies. Develop scientifically correct reference answers and assessment criteria to evaluate AI-generated conclusions. Investigate complex biological questions related to vector design, delivery efficiency, functional potency, specificity, biodistribution, and therapeutic safety. Evaluate experimental and preclinical results, identifying biological signals, technical artifacts, confounding factors, and limitations in the available evidence. Identify where AI systems make plausible but scientifically incorrect assumptions, and explain what a knowledgeable researcher would conclude instead. Collaborate remotely with scientists and software engineers to develop increasingly sophisticated AI evaluation methods. You will primarily work within your own scientific area of expertise. You are not expected to be an expert across every gene therapy technology or development stage. Your Background We are particularly interested in candidates who have: A PhD, or equivalent relevant experience in gene therapy or gene delivery . At least 3 years of hands-on research or development experience in gene therapy or gene delivery . Recent, first-hand experience designing experiments, analysing biological data, or making research decisions based on experimental evidence. Deep expertise in at least one relevant area, such as: AAV or lentiviral vector development and characterization. In vivo or ex vivo gene therapy. Viral or non-viral gene delivery. CRISPR-based genome editing and analysis of editing outcomes. Gene therapy potency, efficacy, safety, or preclinical development. Strong experimental design, critical thinking, and scientific problem-solving skills. The ability to explain why a particular scientific method was chosen, what its limitations are, and how to interpret potentially conflicting results. Strong written scientific communication skills and professional English proficiency. Additional Qualifications Experience with Python, R, bioinformatics, or quantitative analysis would be an advantage, particularly if you have personally developed analytical workflows. Familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, or scientific coding assistants is beneficial, but a software engineering or machine learning background is not required. We welcome applicants from both academia and industry, including experienced postdoctoral researchers with substantial ownership of their scientific work. What Makes This Role Different? Rather than conducting experiments at the bench, you will apply your scientific knowledge to evaluate how well AI systems can solve real biological problems. You will have the opportunity to work on diverse scientific questions, collaborate with an international interdisciplinary team, and contribute to a rapidly developing application of AI in biomedical research. Your success will depend on the quality of your scientific reasoning, your ability to identify subtle errors, and your capacity to turn complex research problems into clear, verifiable scientific evaluations. Working Arrangement & Compensation Remote collaboration from Europe with a US-based international team. Working hours are flexible, with an emphasis on scientific output rather than fixed office hours. Some collaboration and scheduled meetings with US-based colleagues will be required. Introduction to the role At a moment when our information environment is under significant strain, this is an exciting opportunity: a role with real autonomy, meaningful mission, and genuine influence at the intersection of AI and web scale engineering. As a Data Scientist at Full Fact, you will make sure those who make false claims in public can't get away with it. This is a rare opportunity to work for a non-profit tackling internet-scale misinformation problems with a global user base. The fact checks our users publish are seen hundreds of millions of times each year and embedded in many of the most well-known internet services. Every day, 100s of people around the world find, check, archive and challenge false claims identified by AI-enabled products produced by Full Fact. Your job will be to help us improve and expand this software for our growing user base. You’ll be working at the intersection of software engineering, machine learning, and real-world impact. Whether you're responding to a new feature request from users in Nigeria covering a general election, helping fact checkers in Australia verify politicians' claims in real time, or enabling health-focused charities to identify and reduce harmful content spreading online, you will be working at pace on projects that make a substantial difference in the world. In this role that means prototyping and developing features with robust APIs, writing clean Python, and working closely with engineers and other data scientists to bring AI-powered features into production. It is an exciting time to join Full Fact. You will be joining a team of technical, data, and product specialists working on genuinely novel problems in applied AI, from natural language processing and claim detection to trust benchmarks and harm detection. We will support you to keep learning, and if you are interested in applying but not sure you have all the skills, please do apply. We are open both to supporting learning on the job and to rearranging tasks within the team to suit the skillsets of the best applicant Job Definition As an experienced Data Scientist, you will be a key contributor to a number of new and ongoing projects. You will use your technical skills to design and develop software that identifies and counters misinformation. You will develop and use a variety of datasets to train and evaluate machine learning models. You will work with non-technical colleagues and other users of our tools. You will participate in code review, both of your own and of others' code. Outcomes Some of the projects you will be contributing to include: Extending our new “Public Interest AI Trust Benchmark” to provide a deeper analysis of how reliably AI chatbots answer everyday questions. Spotting potentially misleading and harmful claims across a broad range of media Identifying and characterising potentially harmful narratives as they spread Helping to integrate the technologies you build into products that will have an immediate use, for both fact checkers and journalists Identifying sightings of previously checked claims at real-time speed Measuring and improving the quality of the system What we are looking for from you Political impartiality and sensitivity: You are committed to the political neutrality of our work and have a good understanding of impartiality (please see the rules on our website). You can design, code, test, correct and document moderate to complex programs and scripts from agreed specifications with or without AI coding tools. You can use agreed standards and tools. Collaborate with others to review and refine specifications where appropriate. AI and data science innovation. You are broadly familiar with recent advances in AI including LLMs. You proactively research and explore areas of innovation in our industry. items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Contrat renouvelable : Oui Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Niveau d'expérience souhaité : De 3 à 5 ans A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Le centre Inria de l’université de Bordeaux est un des neuf centres d’Inria en France et compte une vingtaine d’équipes de recherche. Le centre Inria est un acteur majeur et reconnu dans le domaine des sciences numériques. Il est au cœur d'un riche écosystème de R&D et d’innovation : PME fortement innovantes, grands groupes industriels, pôles de compétitivité, acteurs de la recherche et de l’enseignement supérieur, laboratoires d'excellence, institut de recherche technologique… Contexte et atouts du poste L'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle dans les activités scientifiques entraîne de nouveaux besoins en matière de traitement, de gestion et d'exploitation des données. Les chercheurs souhaitent pouvoir mobiliser des modèles d'intelligence artificielle pour analyser leurs données expérimentales, sans nécessairement disposer des compétences ou des infrastructures nécessaires pour déployer et administrer eux-mêmes ces technologies. Le projet AI2F (AI for Science) vise notamment à faciliter l'accès à ces capacités de traitement au sein des infrastructures de calcul scientifique, en permettant aux utilisateurs de combiner données, modèles d'intelligence artificielle et traitements dans des chaînes de traitement adaptées à leurs besoins. Dans ce contexte, le poste s'appuie sur UMRS (Unified Multimodal Retriever Service) , une plateforme logicielle développée pour orchestrer des traitements d'intelligence artificielle, gérer des données et leurs représentations vectorielles, et mettre à disposition des modèles de traitement. UMRS permet notamment de construire des workflows, c'est-à-dire des chaînes de traitement représentées sous forme de graphes, combinant différentes sources de données, modèles et opérations. L'objectif est d'étudier et d'expérimenter l'intégration de UMRS dans l'environnement de SLICES-FR ( en particulier sur la plateforme expérimentale Grid'5000). Ce travail sera réalisé en collaboration avec l'équipe technique de SLICES-FR. Il prendra notamment la forme d'une preuve de concept (POC, Proof of Concept ) permettant d'évaluer la faisabilité de cette intégration, d'identifier les limites de l'infrastructure actuelle et de déterminer les adaptations nécessaires, notamment en matière de gestion des ressources, d'authentification et de droits d'accès. Ce poste offre ainsi l'opportunité de travailler à l'interface du génie logiciel, de l'intelligence artificielle et du calcul haute performance, en interaction avec les équipes techniques de SLICES-FR et les communautés scientifiques impliquées dans le projet AI2F. La personne recrutée participera également aux réunions et aux activités collectives du projet AI2F, et contribuera aux échanges techniques et scientifiques avec ses différents partenaires. Mission confiée La personne recrutée aura pour mission principale de contribuer au développement et à l'évolution de la plateforme UMRS, ainsi que d'étudier et d'expérimenter son intégration dans l'environnement de SLICES-FR, en collaboration avec l'équipe technique de l'infrastructure et dans le cadre du projet AI2F. Elle prendra notamment en charge l'appropriation et l'adaptation du moteur de gestion et d'exécution de workflows de UMRS, afin de permettre aux utilisateurs de construire et d'exécuter des graphes de traitements combinant données, modèles d'intelligence artificielle et opérations de traitement dans un environnement de calcul partagé. Elle contribuera à la réalisation d'une preuve de concept permettant d'évaluer les possibilités d'intégration de UMRS dans SLICES-FR, d'en identifier les limites techniques et de proposer les évolutions nécessaires. Elle accompagnera également les chercheurs dans la définition et la mise en œuvre de cas d'usage et participera aux activités collectives du projet AI2F. Principales activités Appropriation de l'architecture logicielle et des fonctionnalités de la plateforme UMRS. Appropriation, portage et évolution du moteur de gestion et d'exécution de workflows de UMRS. Étude et expérimentation de l'intégration de UMRS dans l'environnement de SLICES-FR, en collaboration avec son équipe technique, notamment à travers la réalisation d'une preuve de concept. Étude des interfaces entre UMRS et les services de l'infrastructure : ordonnancement des tâches, stockage, authentification et gestion des ressources. Analyse des limitations éventuelles de l'infrastructure actuelle, notamment concernant la gestion des droits d'accès, et identification des adaptations nécessaires. Développement et évolution des composants logiciels de UMRS. Prise en compte des contraintes du calcul haute performance : allocation des ressources, ordonnancement, exécution distribuée et gestion des dépendances entre traitements. Développement et …

items.desc: Ref Number B04-08095 Professional Expertise Research and Research Support Department UCL BEAMS (B04) Location London Working Pattern Full time Salary See advert text Contract Type Fixed-term Working Type On site Available for Secondment No Closing Date 29-Nov-2026 About us UCL’s Faculty of Engineering Sciences comprises ten academic departments that undertake research and teaching across a wide range of disciplines. Our scientists and engineers take discoveries from fundamentals to practice, producing innovative technological solutions to challenging problems. It is a dynamic and growing faculty, with a strong vision and desire to use our talents to ‘Change the world. UCL Mechanical Engineering has been pioneering the development of engineering education, having taught the core discipline for over 165 years. UCL was home to the UK’s first ever Professor of the Mechanical Principles of Engineering, Eaton Hodgkinson, in 1847. It was also where Sir Alexander Blackie William Kennedy introduced organized laboratory practicals in university education training; a world-leading educational innovation at the time. UCL Mechanical Engineering, we develop and apply core competencies to produce world-class research into a wider range of engineering challenges than most would imagine. Amongst many other avenues we are: Leading research into low carbon shipping Designing the greenest engines and novel sustainable fuels Studying the flow of red blood cells in channels thinner than a human hair Using ‘lighter than air’ building materials to develop the solar power stations of the future. Developing the most advanced brain models for dementia Designing propulsion systems for advanced multihull ships. The Department of Mechanical Engineering at UCL undertakes multidisciplinary research at the interface of engineering, imaging and orthopaedic surgery. The Orthopaedic Engineering group develops quantitative methods for understanding anatomical variation, improving three-dimensional surgical planning and evaluating implant design and performance. The group works with surgeons, researchers and industrial collaborators on complex joint reconstruction. The principal focus of this post is hip surgery, spanning primary OA, acetabular bone defects, reconstruction of missing pelvic anatomy, proximal femoral morphology and femoral stem positioning. Related applications include shoulder and knee arthroplasty, and the assessment of off-the-shelf and custom additively manufactured implants. About the role We are looking to recruit a Research Fellow to undertake high-quality research in statistical shape modelling (SSM), CT-based three-dimensional analysis and patient-specific surgical planning for complex hip reconstruction, bringing together acetabular and femoral approaches. The postholder will extend these established methods into validated implant-design and fixation assessments and develop expertise in finite element analysis (FEA) through supported training and collaborative projects. The postholder will contribute a defined programme of implant metrology, particularly for off-the-shelf and custom additively manufactured reconstruction devices; provide technical mentoring to a PhD student working on acetabular defect classification and reconstruction planning; and participate in publications, conferences and research career development. About you The successful candidate will hold a PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Physics, or a closely related discipline, with research experience in statistical shape modelling, three-dimensional anatomical analysis, computational orthopaedic engineering, or related fields. You will have experience working with CT-based imaging data, including anatomical segmentation, registration, or surgical planning workflows, and possess knowledge of hip anatomy, joint reconstruction, and orthopaedic implant positioning, including acetabular and femoral applications. You will have demonstrated scientific writing skills through your doctoral research and contributions to publications or conference submissions. You will be capable of independently developing, validating, and documenting reproducible computational or medical-image analysis workflows, with a strong commitment to research integrity and responsible data management. You will be proficient in medical-image processing, three-dimensional CAD, or related analytical software, and able to organise research activities effectively to deliver high-quality outputs to agreed milestones. Strong communication skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively with engineering, research, and clinical colleagues are essential. We particularly welcome applicants who are committed to advancing equality, diversity, and inclusion. Experience in finite element analysis, additive-manufacturing metrology, or custom orthopaedic implant assessment would be advantageous. What we offer As well as the exciting opportunities this …

It has
items.desc: Job number MED06066 Faculties Faculty of Medicine Departments Institute of Clinical Sciences Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Hammersmith Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 29 Nov 2026 About the role We invite applications for a 3-year postdoctoral position in the Computational Regulatory Genomics group at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences (LMS) / Institute of Clinical Sciences. The successful candidate will play a central role in the analysis and interpretation of diverse omics data within the cis-ARC consortium that studies cis-regulatory mechanisms governing vertebrate development. It has been established that long-range promoter-enhancer interactions are indispensable for the normal transcription of key developmental regulatory genes, including transcription factors. These interactions occur within landscapes of extremely conserved noncoding elements – genomic regulatory blocks (GRBs). However, neither the source, nor the functional importance, of this extreme evolutionary conservation has been elucidated. The successful applicant will perform statistical modelling and develop computational methods to analyse publicly available and consortium-generated omics data with the aim to provide mechanistic hypotheses about transcription regulation within GRBs during zebrafish development. What you would be doing You will perform whole-genome alignment and identification of conserved non-coding elements and their clusters in the zebrafish genome. Using statistical methods, you will integrate the sequence conservation signal, 3D-genome sequencing datasets and data on chromatin accessibility and gene expression to delineate genomic regulatory blocks, find regulated genes and predict their long-range interactions with cis-regulatory elements. Using the obtained comprehensive view of transcription regulation in selected GRBs in normal development, you will help prioritise regulatory loci for perturbations to observe and interpret emerging phenotypes. For this, you will be working closely with experimental groups of the cis-ARC consortium. You will also have an opportunity to collaborate with other members of the Computational Regulatory Genomics group. What we are looking for A PhD (or equivalent) in a relevant field of biology, such as computational biology, bioinformatics, molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry. First author publication in relevant and refereed journals. Experience and expertise in more than one of the following areas: analysis and interpretation of bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing or ATAC data, Hi-C-type data, ChIP-seq / CUT&RUN or similar data, CAGE-seq data. Experience in at least one of the following areas: whole-genome alignment, single nucleotide polymorphism or indel calling and annotation, analysis of evolutionary sequence conservation. Experience in the analysis or modelling of functional promoter-enhancer associations; or experience in statistical modelling or bioinformatics software/database development. Excellent communication skills and experience of collaborative work within a research group. What we can offer you Opportunity to do cutting-edge research on a topic important for both fundamental and translational molecular biology The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity Excellent opportunities for professional development through collaborations within and outside the group Access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information This is a full-time, fixed term post for 3 years. Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . items.desc: Position Details School of Biosciences Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £33,662 to £36,320 with potential progression once in post to £40,704 Grade: 6 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to 12 months Closing date: 6 th December 2026 Background We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic Research Associate to join our research team at the University of Birmingham to work on an exciting project funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA). The project aims to develop innovative technologies for delivering molecular cargos into mitochondria, with the long-term goal of enabling mitochondrial genome engineering and advancing therapeutic approaches for mitochondrial diseases. The successful candidate will have a strong interest in mitochondrial biology and a passion for developing new experimental approaches. They will contribute to the design, optimisation and validation of strategies for delivering molecular cargo into mitochondria, using a combination of mammalian cell culture, molecular biology, mitochondrial functional assays and advanced imaging techniques. The successful candidate will join a collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment, working alongside researchers with expertise in mitochondrial genetics, cell biology in the School of Biosciences, University of Birmingham. This position is initially offered for a fixed term of 12 months. Role Summary Work on a research project aimed at developing technologies for delivering molecular cargos into mitochondria. Apply expertise in mitochondrial biology, mammalian cell culture, molecular biology and imaging to develop, optimise and evaluate mitochondrial delivery strategies. Design and conduct experiments, analyse and interpret research data, and contribute to the development of new methodologies. Collaborate with interdisciplinary research teams and contribute to project reports, scientific publications and research presentation. Main Duties Conduct research within an ARIA-funded project focused on developing and optimising technologies for delivering molecular cargos into mitochondria. Establish and maintain mammalian cell cultures, including genetically modified cell lines, for experimental studies. Design and perform experiments to evaluate mitochondrial cargo delivery efficiency, localisation and functional outcomes. Perform mitochondrial functional assays, including measurements of mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration and ATP production. Apply molecular biology techniques, including molecular cloning and CRISPR–Cas9-mediated genome editing, to develop and validate experimental systems. Use fluorescence microscopy and advanced imaging techniques to investigate mitochondrial morphology, dynamics and sub compartment localisation of delivered cargo. Analyse and interpret experimental data, maintain accurate research records and contribute to the development and optimisation of experimental protocols. Collaborate with project partners and other members of the research team, contributing to scientific discussions, progress reports, presentations and publications. Provide guidance as required to support staff and any students who may be assisting with research Deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines Carry out administrative tasks related directly to the delivery of the research Fosters a fair and equitable workplace for all staff Identify and respond to equality and diversity issues in line with relevant university policies and procedures Other relevant criteria from our equality and diversity duties document. Person Specification Essential skills and experience: An Undergraduate degree in biological sciences, biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience in mammalian cell culture and associated experimental techniques. Previous experience in mitochondrial research and mitochondrial functional assays, such as measurements of mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP production or other indicators of mitochondrial activity. Experience in fluorescence microscopy and imaging-based analysis of mitochondrial morphology, organisation or sub-compartment localisation. Strong experimental, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. items.desc: The Role The Rosalind Franklin Institute (the Franklin) is a technology institute established by the UK Government as a unique centre committed to advancing tools that are needed to transform healthcare in the future. The Institute brings together researchers in life and physical sciences, and engineering, to develop a spectrum of tools which we will use to image, interpret and intervene in biological systems. These insights will speed up the discovery of new medicines, help find new diagnostics and contribute to a deeper understanding of human health and disease. Our Science Strategy seeks to focus the Franklin’s research and unite our researchers around our Technology Innovation Challenges and Life Science Challenges. For more information on the Franklin’s Challenges click here . This research opportunity within the Virtual Cell project will advance molecular mapping of cells by expanding the range of proteins and macromolecular complexes that can be reliably detected and characterised in cryo-electron tomograms and develop methods to track how these change over time and in response to cellular perturbation. The Research Associate will develop machine-learning methods for particle localisation, detection and classification in crowded cellular volumes. The work will emphasise learning from limited annotations, generalisation to additional molecular species and experimental datasets, and discovery of candidate particle populations beyond existing labelled classes. Methods will address low signal-to-noise ratios, missing-wedge artefacts, and variation in particle orientation, abundance and conformation. The role will explore integration of complementary structural, molecular and imaging data, such as predicted or experimental protein structures, proteomics, molecular interaction data, and fluorescence or correlative microscopy. These sources will guide detection, constrain candidate molecular identities and support validation, with explicit consideration of their uncertainty, spatial resolution and potential biases. Working closely with experimental and computational researchers, the role-holder will establish robust benchmarks, develop reproducible software, and validate detections and candidate identities through subtomogram analysis and complementary evidence. The role offers opportunities to develop scientific independence within an interdisciplinary team. Key Responsibilities As a Research Associate you will: Develop and apply machine-learning methods to broaden the range of proteins and macromolecular complexes that can be detected and characterised in cryo-electron tomograms. Explore how complementary structural, molecular and imaging data can improve analysis and support interpretation of molecular organisation in cells. Work with experimental and computational colleagues to prepare datasets, evaluate methods and validate biological findings. Develop reproducible analysis workflows and research software, and share methods and findings through documentation, publications and presentations. Plan data acquisitions with experimentalists who conduct them, analyse and interpret results and supervised delivery of outputs (e.g. research report, patent application) in a scientific/technology area of interest. Work within a project team, contributing to wider projects around Franklin's key Challenges. Lead major contributions to outputs from research including papers, patents and both internal and external presentations. Support and develop others including day-to-day supervision of students or visitors in areas related to own research. Have supervised, staged progression to first stages of scientific independence with opportunities to further develop science and skills/experience. Enhance your research through collaboration with other researchers and make active contributions to exchanging of ideas through your own network. items.desc: À propos de nous Nantes Université est un établissement public d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche qui propose un modèle d’université inédit en France unissant une université, un hôpital universitaire (CHU de Nantes), un institut de recherche technologique (IRT Jules Verne), un organisme national de recherche (Inserm) ainsi que Centrale Nantes, l’école des Beaux-Arts Nantes Saint-Nazaire et l’École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Nantes. Ces acteurs concentrent leurs forces pour développer l’excellence de la recherche nantaise et offrir de nouvelles opportunités de formations , dans tous les domaines de la connaissance. Durable et ouverte sur le monde , Nantes Université veille à la qualité des conditions d'études et de travail offertes à ses étudiantes, étudiants et personnels, pour favoriser leur épanouissement sur tous ses campus de Nantes, Saint-Nazaire et La Roche-sur-Yon. Mission Ce poste vise à développer de nouvelles méthodes de vérification formelle pour les systèmes temporisés paramétrés soumis à des contraintes énergétiques , en s’appuyant sur les avancées récentes en model checking et en automates temporisés paramétrés. Il s’agit d’ identifier les limites des approches existantes, concevoir de nouvelles techniques théoriques et algorithmiques, puis les implémenter et les évaluer expérimentalement , afin de contribuer à l’avancement de l’état de l’art et à l’amélioration des capacités de vérification de systèmes complexes. Mission Analyser l’état de l’art en vérification formelle de systèmes temporisés paramétrés à énergie Réaliser une veille scientifique approfondie sur les méthodes existantes de vérification de systèmes temporisés, paramétrés et soumis à des contraintes énergétiques. Étudier les travaux récents, identifier les verrous scientifiques, les limites des approches existantes et les problèmes encore ouverts. Comparer les différents formalismes et techniques de vérification afin d’identifier les pistes les plus pertinentes pour les développements du projet. Concevoir de nouvelles méthodes théoriques pour la vérification de systèmes complexes Étudier et faire évoluer des formalismes fondés notamment sur les automates temporisés paramétrés afin de prendre en compte les contraintes liées à l’énergie. Proposer de nouvelles techniques de raisonnement et de vérification permettant de mieux exploiter la structure des systèmes étudiés. Formaliser les méthodes développées et analyser leurs propriétés théoriques, notamment en matière de correction, de complétude, de décidabilité et de complexité. Développer et améliorer les algorithmes de vérification Concevoir et implémenter des algorithmes permettant de mettre en œuvre les méthodes théoriques proposées. Explorer différentes stratégies d’exploration, d’optimisation et d’heuristiques afin d’améliorer les performances des méthodes de vérification. Adapter les algorithmes aux caractéristiques des systèmes temporisés paramétrés à énergie et étudier les compromis entre précision, complexité et temps de calcul. Évaluer expérimentalement les méthodes développées Mettre en place des expérimentations reproductibles permettant de mesurer l’efficacité des approches proposées. Construire, sélectionner et exploiter des jeux de tests et des bancs d’essai représentatifs de différents cas d’utilisation. Comparer les différentes variantes algorithmiques et heuristiques, ainsi que les méthodes proposées avec les approches existantes, en s’appuyant sur des critères tels que le temps de calcul, la consommation mémoire et la capacité à traiter des instances de taille croissante. Identifier, à partir des résultats expérimentaux, les configurations et stratégies les plus efficaces et orienter les développements en conséquence. Valoriser et diffuser les résultats de recherche Documenter les méthodes, algorithmes et résultats expérimentaux afin de garantir leur compréhension et leur reproductibilité. Contribuer à la diffusion des résultats sous la forme de publications scientifiques, de présentations dans des conférences ou séminaires et, lorsque cela est pertinent, de prototypes ou d’outils logiciels. Participer aux échanges scientifiques avec les membres de l’équipe et avec la communauté de recherche afin de confronter les résultats obtenus aux travaux existants et d’identifier de nouvelles perspectives de recherche. Retrouvez notre offre complète ici : https://www.univ-nantes.fr/universite/recrutement/nantes-universite-recrute-un-e-ingenieur-e-detude-en-informatique-iut-nantes Profil Formation de niveau Bac + 3 ou 4 en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe, avec une spécialisation ou un intérêt marqué pour la vérification formelle, l’algorithmique, l’intelligence artificielle, les systèmes distribués, les systèmes embarqués ou les méthodes formelles. items.desc: Expert public de la météo et du climat, Météo-France est à vos côtés pour contribuer à votre sécurité au quotidien et vous aider à prendre les meilleures décisions, dans un climat qui change. Face à des épisodes météo dangereux encore plus intenses et plus fréquents sous l’effet du changement climatique, nos missions au service de votre sécurité sont cruciales. Nous mobilisons notre expertise, notre excellence scientifique et technologique pour vous permettre d’anticiper les phénomènes météorologiques et climatiques à enjeux, et de vous y adapter. Retrouvez-nous en ligne : https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france Rejoindre Météo France, C'est Intégrer Une Organisation Multi-sites, Situés En Hexagone, En Outre-mer, Etc. L'organisation De Météo-France S'appuie Sur Des Directions Centrales Et Des Directions Interrégionales. Ci-dessous, La Présentation De La Direction Que Vous Pourriez Rejoindre La Direction de l'Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche (DESR) rassemble les entités de recherche de Météo-France (principalement CNRM, SAFIRE, LACy), l'Ecole Nationale de la Météorologie, et les services partagés de soutien administratif et informatique (PGA). Le CNRM est une Unité Mixte de Recherche (UMR 3589) avec la double tutelle Météo-France et CNRS. Le CNRM conduit des recherches dans le domaine de la météorologie et du climat, de l'observation, la compréhension et la modélisation des processus jusqu'à la mise au point de systèmes de prévision météorologique et de projection climatique pouvant être transférés aux services opérationnels de Météo-France. Le GMAP (Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision), basé à Toulouse, est l'un des 6 groupes ou centres de recherche du CNRM. Sa mission est de maintenir et développer les systèmes de prévision numérique du temps (PNT) opérationnels de Météo-France et de conduire des recherches qui préparent les futures versions. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?
