items.desc: Job Description This is an Atlantic portfolio company. About Marentis Marentis develops AI-supported software for manufacturing, robotics and complex automated machinery. We turn machine data and operational information into useful knowledge for troubleshooting, decision-making and automation. Our work connects sensor measurements, machine and robot states, quality data, alarms and expert knowledge. These problems require understanding both the data and its context: a fault may originate elsewhere in a production line, and similar symptoms can have different causes. We are a small, early-stage startup where individual contributions directly shape the product. We value curiosity, initiative and people who enjoy understanding difficult problems and making things work. The Role We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Software Engineer with strong Python skills and sound technical judgment. You will own backend features from problem definition through implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance. After onboarding, you should be able to investigate unfamiliar production code and independently review Python/backend pull requests: understand intended behavior, question assumptions, assess tests and failure paths, and identify effects on the wider system. We actively encourage AI-assisted development. You remain responsible for understanding, verifying and maintaining the resulting software. We value demonstrated delivery, ownership and learning ability more than a fixed number of years in the industry. What You Will Do Build backend services, APIs and SQL-backed data pipelines for industrial analytics, knowledge retrieval and agent workflows. Read and improve existing code, review pull requests, and make informed decisions about interfaces, data models, state and failure handling. Design meaningful unit, integration and end-to-end tests, supported by continuous integration. Test with representative machine data, recorded streams and simulated device inputs, including missing measurements, duplicate or out-of-order events, invalid values and connection failures. Reproduce bugs, inspect whether test assertions verify the intended behavior, and add useful regression coverage. Understand manufacturing users and equipment, contribute across integration and deployment, and communicate trade-offs and blockers early. What You Bring Strong practical Python and backend engineering skills, supported by software you personally shipped and maintained. Independent code-review ability: you can investigate a change, assess correctness, maintainability and security, and justify whether it is ready to merge. Practical system-design judgment across APIs, SQL, database design, data validation, state management and concurrency where relevant. Strong testing and debugging skills: you choose useful test boundaries, construct representative data and investigate failures. Experience making imperfect operational, machine, sensor or similarly complex data trustworthy, with an interest in its industrial meaning and consequences. Resourcefulness: you learn unfamiliar code and technologies through documentation, small experiments, focused questions and feedback. Clear written and spoken English, constructive collaboration and reliable follow-through. We welcome different educational and professional paths. Direct manufacturing experience is especially useful; equivalent engineering depth from adjacent domains is also relevant. Particularly Relevant Experience Bring depth in one or more of these areas; expertise in all of them is not expected. Machine data, analytics and machine learning: Time-series or sensor-data processing, curation, feature engineering, anomaly detection, condition monitoring or quality prediction. Explain how you handled timestamps, units, asset identity and data quality, and evaluated whether the result was useful. Knowledge graphs and retrieval: Entity and relationship modeling, graph or relational database design, provenance, versioning and conflicting information. Experience combining identifiers, aliases, lexical search and semantic retrieval, with evaluations of relevance and applicability. Agent systems and workflows: LLM tools, multi-agent coordination, orchestration, context and memory management, validation and failure recovery. Show how you evaluated quality, cost and latency, enforced permissions and chose appropriate execution boundaries. Industrial integration, robotics and automation: Connecting software with production equipment, robot cells or automated machinery through telemetry, device interfaces or protocols such as MQTT and OPC UA. Experience with simulators, physical-device testing and equipment-specific behavior is valuable. Cloud deployment, containerization, observability and operating software across customer environments are also useful.

items.desc:
Amazon Ads Brand Safety & Suitability protects advertisers from exposure to unsafe, unsuitable, or policy-violating content across web, mobile app, CTV, and audio advertising inventory. Our mission is to ensure that every ad impression delivered through Amazon's demand-side platform appears adjacent to content that meets advertiser trust expectations while giving brands granular controls to define suitability on their own terms. We operate at the intersection of advertiser trust, publisher quality, and supply integrity.
AI is fundamentally changing the content landscape. Content is now generated at unprecedented scale, faster, cheaper, and increasingly sophisticated. Low-quality, deceptive, AI-generated, and synthetic content evolves in real time, constantly adapting to evade detection. The volume and velocity of new content entering the advertising system has outpaced traditional classification approaches.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist to work on the next generation of AI-powered Brand Safety and Content Classification systems designed to protect advertisers and elevate supply quality at internet scale. This is not a traditional classification problem. You will build systems that make millisecond-level decisions across billions of content signals while continuously adapting to emerging content risks driven by generative AI. You will own the science strategy for LLM-powered classification and semantic understanding, real-time multimodal content evaluation, adversarial ML and adaptive model resilience, proactive risk intelligence and content risk hunting, AI-generated and synthetic content detection, and large-scale abusive content system identification and disruption.
You will define how modern AI separates high-quality advertising inventory from unsafe, unsuitable, and policy-violating content, across web, mobile app, CTV, and audio surfaces.
What Makes This Role Unique
Generative AI has dramatically lowered the cost of producing deceptive, policy-evasive content, and the adversary evolves daily. Your detection systems must reason contextually, adapt rapidly, and generalize beyond previously seen content risk patterns. Static models fail here; you will build living systems that learn and respond in real time. You will do this at internet scale, developing low-latency ML and LLM-powered systems evaluating content safety, brand suitability, misinformation risk, and emerging content risk vectors across massive real-time traffic streams, making billions of decisions per day with single-digit millisecond latency constraints. This role sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and large-scale production engineering, combining deep science, system-wide impact, and business-critical outcomes. The models your team ships directly influence billions of dollars in advertising spend and the trust of the world's largest brands in Amazon DSP.
The Science Problems Are Genuinely Hard
You will tackle challenges including detecting sophisticated AI-generated and synthetic content, understanding nuanced contextual brand risk, identifying coordinated MFA space before they scale, balancing precision, recall, latency, explainability, and fairness, designing adaptive models resilient to adversarial evolution, and leveraging LLMs for semantic understanding in real-time, latency-constrained environments.
Why This Matters
Few roles offer the opportunity to work at the intersection of frontier AI, internet-scale production systems, adversarial environments, and business-critical impact, while tackling open-ended scientific challenges with real-world societal relevance. As AI reshapes the internet, the systems your team builds will define what trustworthy, high-quality digital systems look like for the next decade.
Key job responsibilities
 - Own the science strategy for AI-powered brand safety classification.
 - Build LLM-powered content classification systems making billions of decisions/day at single-digit millisecond latency
 - Develop multimodal evaluation pipelines reasoning across text, images, audio, and video in real time
 - Design adaptive ML systems resilient to adversarial evolution, semantic understanding for nuanced contextual brand risk.
 - Define measurement frameworks and drive continuous improvement
 - Translate research into production, own the path from prototype to deployed model
 - Publish at peer-reviewed venues; contribute to the scientific community in adversarial ML, NLP, and content safety
- Collaborate with software engineering teams to integrate successful experiments into large-scale, highly complex Amazon production systems.
- PhD, or a Master's degree and experience in CS, CE, ML or related field
- Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and …

items.desc: Job number NAT02328 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 14 Dec 2026 About the role How does a compact nervous system combine different sensory cues to make a life-changing decision? We are seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to join the Chatzigeorgiou Laboratory at Imperial College London and work on a Leverhulme Trust-funded project investigating multisensory decision-making in the larval tunicate Ciona intestinalis. You will examine how mechanical and chemical cues are integrated to control settlement, combining quantitative behaviour, controlled stimulus delivery, whole-brain calcium imaging, neural perturbation and computational analysis. With only 231 neurons and a synaptic-resolution connectome, Ciona offers a powerful opportunity to uncover general principles of sensory integration in a minimal chordate nervous system. What you would be doing Lead experiments defining how mechanical and chemical cues interact to regulate larval swimming, settlement and metamorphic commitment in Ciona intestinalis. Develop high-throughput behavioural assays using millifluidic or microfluidic arenas and quantitative tracking. Perform whole-brain calcium imaging during precisely controlled unimodal and multimodal stimulation. Analyse behavioural and imaging datasets to identify nonlinear integration, cue hierarchy and temporal decision dynamics. Use targeted optogenetic and/or chemogenetic perturbations to test causal circuit mechanisms. Generate transient transgenic Ciona larvae and contribute to animal culture and experimental workflows. Publish findings in high-quality international journals and share data and code through open, reproducible workflows. Present work at national and international conferences and workshops. Work closely with the PI, students and project collaborators across experimental and modelling work packages. Help supervise students and contribute to the growth of the Chatzigeorgiou Laboratory at Imperial. What we are looking for We are looking for a scientist who has: A PhD in neuroscience, neurobiology, animal behaviour, physiology, quantitative biology or a closely related discipline. Evidence of high-quality research and strong publication potential or a publication record appropriate to career stage. Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in rigorous experimental design and statistical analysis. Practical experience in fluorescence microscopy, functional imaging and/or calcium imaging. Practical experience working with an experimental model organism. Experience in quantitative behavioural analysis and handling complex datasets. Enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research spanning behaviour, neurobiology, imaging and computation. Strong communication, organisational and collaborative skills. Desirable experience includes: Experience with microfluidics or controlled mechanical and chemical stimulation. Experience in transgenesis and genetically encoded calcium indicators. Experience working with Ciona, marine organisms or other non-traditional model systems. Experience in computer vision or machine learning, such as DeepLabCut, and analysis of calcium-imaging data. What we can offer you Opportunity to work on an ambitious Leverhulme Trust-funded project addressing fundamental questions in sensory neuroscience, behaviour and evolution. Access to a uniquely tractable chordate model, whole-brain imaging, controlled-stimulus platforms and connectomic resources, with close interaction between experimental and modelling researchers. The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . This is a full-time post (35 hours per week). This role is for a fixed-term contract for 3 years from 1 March 2027 If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr. Marios Chatzigeorgiou – m.chatzigeorgiou@imperial.ac.uk . items.desc: Hours of work: Full-time Tenure: Permanent A Research Coordinator position is available in the group of Professor. Andrew Cooper at the University of Liverpool. The Research Coordinator will bring their expertise to strengthen the relevant areas of our research programme, particularly by providing specialist advice and leadership in artificial intelligence and machine learning for functional materials discovery . This will include managing the teams working on the development and application of advanced AI methods for scientific research, including machine learning, large language models, machine reasoning, knowledge representation, and optimisation algorithms. A PhD in Chemistry, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Physics or Materials Science and expertise in AI and machine learning as applied to scientific problems are essential, together with the ability to lead a team of researchers working on projects in this area. You will oversee and coordinate the AI and machine learning aspects of our research programme, while also ensuring integration with the other research areas in the Cooper Group (i.e., chemistry, robotics, automation and materials discovery). You will also help manage the computational resources and software infrastructure associated with this research area, ensuring that projects are delivered to the highest standards and that research findings are disseminated effectively and in a timely manner. items.desc: Internship – Time Series Foundation Models for Forecasting Duration: 6 months Start date: April 2027 (flexible) Location: Paris 7e ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. Your Role How Much History Does an LLM Need? Memory-Augmented Language Models for Financial Text Financial text about a company accumulates continuously over years. Today's language models typically process this history either by feeding in as much as fits in their context window, or by splitting it into independent chunks. Both approaches have well-known limitations, especially as history grows long and needs to stay historically consistent. This internship explores an alternative: building a compact, incrementally updated memory of a company's disclosure history, one that is updated as new documents arrive rather than fully re-read each time. The central question is twofold: Does a long disclosure history help understand or predict a company's future, compared to only recent information? If so, what is the best way to represent and maintain that history over time in a language model? Key Responsibilities Design and compare strategies for incrementally updating a compact memory representation as new documents arrive. Build comparison baselines, including a retrieval-based system. Evaluate the resulting representations both for faithfulness to the source documents and for usefulness on a downstream financial prediction task. Read and implement research papers (a significant part of the work). Your Skills Required Final-year engineering or Master's student in NLP, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, or Computer Science. Strong Python skills, including PyTorch. Solid understanding of LLMs and sequence modeling. Ability to read and implement research papers. Fluent English Appreciated Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, agent memory systems, or reinforcement learning for LLMs. Interest in financial applications (a bonus). Prior knowledge of finance is not required. French is a bonus. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT We are continuously striving to be an equal opportunity employer and we prohibit any discrimination based on sex, disability, origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, or religion. We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success. CFM is a signatory of the Women Empowerment Principles.

items.desc: CMP Phar.ma Srl, nata nel 1969, produce macchine per l'ispezione farmaceutica e l'industria veterinaria. Nel 1982 diventa la prima società al mondo a lanciare sul mercato una macchina automatica per l'ispezione a raggi laser di fiale; in breve tempo, grazie ad una costante attività di ricerca e sviluppo, si consolida sul mercato internazionale perfezionando l’offerta con una vasta gamma di ispezionatrici automatiche e semi-automatiche per il controllo di fiale, flaconi, siringhe pre-riempite, sacche infusionali e liofilizzati. Nel 2018 Marchesini Group firma l’acquisizione della maggioranza di CMP Phar.ma, grazie alla quale arricchisce ulteriormente il suo già amplissimo portafoglio prodotti. L’obiettivo è di rispondere a 360 gradi alle più diversificate richieste della clientela anche nell’ambito dell’ispezione e del controllo e di consolidarsi come produttore di linee complete in grado di realizzare e monitorare tutto il processo di confezionamento dei farmaci. L’acquisizione di CMP Phar.ma è stata resa possibile anche grazie all’importante contributo del partner SEA Vision, che ha compartecipato all’operazione. Posizione: Per il nostro stabilimento di Costabissara siamo alla ricerca di un* AI / Computer Vision Engineer da inserire all'interno dell'area Pharma. La risorsa si occuperà della progettazione, dello sviluppo, dell'addestramento e dell'ottimizzazione di modelli di Deep Learning applicati a sistemi di visione artificiale, contribuendo alla realizzazione di soluzioni innovative e alla loro integrazione in ambienti produttivi. Cerchiamo un professionista con almeno 3-5 anni di esperienza nello sviluppo di soluzioni di Computer Vision e Deep Learning, con solide competenze di programmazione e una concreta esperienza nella gestione di progetti dalla fase di ricerca e sviluppo fino al rilascio in produzione. La persona lavorerà su progetti applicativi, affrontando problematiche legate all'analisi di immagini, all'addestramento dei modelli, alle prestazioni e all'ottimizzazione dei sistemi di inferenza. Requisiti: Esperienza in Deep Learning e Computer Vision Solida esperienza di almeno 3 anni nello sviluppo e nell'addestramento di modelli di Deep Learning per applicazioni di visione artificiale. Capacità di lavorare con dataset reali, anche limitati o scarsamente annotati. Conoscenza delle tecniche di Data Augmentation e delle metodologie per migliorare le prestazioni dei modelli in presenza di dati non ideali. Esperienza nella valutazione delle prestazioni dei modelli attraverso metriche specifiche e metodologie di validazione. Sviluppo e integrazione in produzione Esperienza concreta nell'integrazione e nel deployment di modelli di Intelligenza Artificiale in ambiente produttivo, sia per la fase di training sia per quella di inferenza. Capacità di ottimizzare i modelli con particolare attenzione alla riduzione della latenza e al miglioramento delle prestazioni computazionali. Esperienza nello sviluppo e nel deployment di applicazioni cross-platform in ambiente Windows e Linux. Capacità di redigere report tecnici dettagliati per ciascun caso d'uso, documentando metodologia adottata, caratteristiche dei dataset, processo di training, risultati e metriche di valutazione. Linguaggi e tecnologie Ottima conoscenza di C++ (standard C++14/17 o superiori). Ottima conoscenza di Python. Ottima padronanza delle librerie e dei framework: PyTorch OpenCV TensorRT LibTorch Preferibile conoscenza della programmazione CUDA e degli strumenti e framework dell'ecosistema NVIDIA. Completano il profilo Approccio analitico e orientamento alla risoluzione di problemi complessi. Laurea in scienze informatiche/ingegneria informatica, matematica o fisica. Autonomia nella gestione delle attività di sviluppo e ricerca. Capacità di lavorare in team multidisciplinari. Precisione, metodo e attenzione alla qualità del codice e della documentazione tecnica. Attitudine alla sperimentazione e all'aggiornamento continuo sulle tecnologie di Intelligenza Artificiale. Altre informazioni: Entrerai a far parte di una realtà internazionale e tecnologicamente avanzata, in continua evoluzione, dove potrai contribuire concretamente allo sviluppo di progetti complessi per importanti clienti del settore farmaceutico. Offriamo: Inserimento in un contesto tecnologicamente stimolante e orientato all'innovazione. Opportunità di lavorare su progetti concreti di Intelligenza Artificiale e Visione Artificiale. Contratto a tempo indeterminato. Orario full time: dal lunedì al venerdì, 08:00–12:30 / 13:30-17.00. Ticket restaurant giornalieri. Inquadramento e trattamento economico commisurati all'esperienza e alle competenze maturate. Il presente annuncio è rivolto ad entrambi i sessi, ai sensi delle leggi 903/77 e 125/91 e a persone di tutte le età e tutte le nazionalità, ai sensi dei decreti legislativi 215/03 e 216/03.

items.desc: Bristol, London, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, York Job Summary The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) works on issues that affect daily life across England. Our work covers the environment, farming, food production, rural communities, animal health and protection from natural risks such as flooding. The Farming Directorate is responsible for delivering a major part of the UK Governments programme of restoring nature, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving animal health and welfare as well as maintaining sustainable food production. By changing how government works and the offers we make available to farmers, we are: Improving productivity across the farming sector Re-purposing funding to focus on the environment Working with farmers to deliver the targets set out in the Climate Change and Environment Acts We have an opportunity to join the Metrics and Reporting team within the Evidence and Analysis function. This position would be suited to analytically-minded candidates interested in deriving robust, impactful analysis on directorate and environmental outcomes from real-world information. items.desc: Machine Learning Engineer - Spiking Neural Networks Salary: £50,000 to £100,000 Location: West London Working arrangement: Predominantly office and customer-site based, with some remote working available Employment: Permanent, full-time MFK Recruitment is seeking a specialist Machine Learning Engineer to help develop an engineering-grade Spiking Neural Network engine for practical machine vision applications. Commercial software development alongside academic or research experience. An MSc, PhD or postdoctoral background involving SNNs, Computer Vision, AI or Machine Learning. items.card: About The Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. items.desc: Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones) Start Date: ASAP Languages: English Team: Engineering About The Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand. We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines — protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents. This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation. This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70–80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. What You'll Do Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case. Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods. Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation. Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts. Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields. Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards. What We're Looking For Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems. Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content. Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility. An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data — and when each is appropriate. High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes. Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap. Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones. Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production. Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above. Why This Role Matters for You Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets. Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need. From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation. Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets. San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70–80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. items.desc:
We are looking for a passionate, talented, and inventive Applied Scientist with a strong machine learning background to help build industry-leading language technology powering Alexa for Shopping, our AI-driven search and shopping assistant, helping customers with their shopping tasks at every step of their shopping journey.
This innovative role focuses on developing and optimizing language model-powered (LLM/SLM) conversational experiences. The core emphasis is to get the best performance out LLMs/SLMs via careful and methodical instruction design, contextual grounding, informed choices of MCP tools and agent/multi-agent systems, context engineering, model fine-tuning, evaluation frameworks, and experimentation to systematically improve quality, robustness, and customer impact. The work combines scientific rigor with product intuition to systematically raise the bar for conversational AI performance at Amazon scale.
Our mission in conversational shopping is to make it easy for customers to find and discover the best products to meet their needs by helping with their product research, providing comparisons and recommendations, answering product questions, enabling shopping directly from images or videos, providing visual inspiration, and more. We do this by leveraging advanced analytics, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), A/B testing, causal inference, and data-driven insights to continuously improve our systems.
Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Scientist on our team, you will develop and maintain LLM agents, including automated eval pipelines, LLM-as-a-judge methodologies, rubric design, and dataset curation to measure nuanced aspects of response quality.
You will partner with the wider org to experiment with techniques such as retrieval augmentation, context enrichment, prompt decomposition, and model fine-tuning or post-training strategies, if and when applicable. Where latency and cost constraints demand it, you will lead post-training of small language models (SLMs) — including supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation, and distillation — to deliver low-latency conversational and shopping experiences.
You will apply applied machine learning and deep learning techniques as last-mile improvements to shopping experiences, that might span ranking, relevance, personalisation, and multimodal understanding. You will design and evaluate agentic architectures that balance the needs of diverse shopping use cases, making principled choices across paradigms such as single-agent and multi-agent systems, memory management strategies, and tool orchestration to optimise for quality, latency, and reliability at scale. You will leverage petabytes of data and identify opportunities to leverage machine learning models aimed at making conversational systems more performant.
A day in the life
Perform hands-on analysis of large-scale multimodal interaction datasets to develop insights into how customers engage with conversational AI systems and how to improve response quality and customer experience.
Use statistical methods, experimentation, and data-driven analysis to develop scalable approaches for measuring, evaluating, and optimizing large language model (LLM)-based shopping assistant systems, leveraging structured and unstructured contextual signals.
Conduct deep-dive analyses to identify opportunities for improving conversational relevance, grounding, customer satisfaction, and downstream business impact.
Collaborate with Product management and Engineers to translate analytical insights into production systems, working closely on model evaluation and deployment.
Communicate results and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences, including through presentations, written reports, and data visualizations.
About the team
The Alexa for Shopping Science team, based in London, works alongside ~150 engineers, designers and product managers, shaping the future of AI-driven shopping experiences at Amazon. The team works on every aspect of the conversational AI system, from making it agentic, enabling customers to set price alerts or empower the assistant to act on their behalf and automatically purchase products when the price is right, to understanding multimodal user queries and generating answers that combine text, image, audio and video, including deep research reports that scour the web and the Amazon catalog to provide detailed and personalised shopping guidance. We utilize and advance state-of-art techniques in the fields of Natural Language Processing, gen AI, Information Retrieval, Machine/Deep Learning, and Data Mining. We validate our work by actively participating in the internal and external scientific communities.
- Master's degree or above in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

items.desc:
Research Assistant - FCLG Operationalisation Project 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Research Assistant - FCLG Operationalisation Project
 100%, Singapore, fixed-term 
 Drucken 
 The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.
 Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .
 The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.
 Project background
 The “Mind the density - Quantifying design scenarios that soften high-density living” project is a multi institutional and multi disciplinary project with researchers from the Singapore-ETH Centre, National University of Singapore, and the Singapore Management University.
 Previous projects at the Singapore-ETH Centre targeted the lack of data convergence in urban planning and the application of the latest developments in geospatial data science to urban design and planning. Data commonly reside in silos (across different fields, agencies, and stakeholders), and analytical and AI methods do not fully exploit these multimodal datasets. Their research outputs tackled this problem directly by releasing open, converged datasets and developing methods that leverage different dimensions such as text, subjective indicators and imagery. In addition, work on design data semantics enhanced the meaning of data science applications for particular urban design solutions and actions. Moreover, they also investigated how the built environment affects people's behaviour, cognition, perception and emotion. They focused on the human and building scale, examining how indoor and outdoor environments influence experience.
 This project integrates these expertise to operationalise evidence on human responses to high-density environments in Singapore. The project will generate large-scale preference data across controlled design conditions, and will conduct focused empirical studies of behavioural, cognitive, physiological and subjective responses. This combined evidence will support agency decision-making on design interventions that improve experience in high-density environments, identify thresholds, compare interventions, and produce decision-support evidence, planning parameters and implementation guidance.
 Lead PI: Filip Biljecki (NUS) and Zdravko Trivic (NUS)
 Job description
 As a research assistant, you will be involved in a multidisciplinary and collaborative research study to operationalise human-centred urban analytics and cognition methods as evidence-backed decision support and implementation guidance for high-density urban form and design interventions. You will integrate analytical methods to quantify how urban form and design interventions affect perception, cognition and behaviour, producing URA-relevant guidance for high-density environments. You will also be involved in large scale field data collection through online surveys and lab-based physiological studies, and collaborations with researchers from various disciplines and government agencies stakeholders. You will do this under the guidance of Assoc. Prof. Filip Biljecki (National University of Singapore) and Asst. Prof. Matias Quintana (Singapore Management University).
 Your key responsibilities will be:

 Developing deep learning models for the project’s research (e.g., geo-spatial data science, street view imagery segmentations).
 Co-developing applications, features, datasets, and use cases on public datasets of street-view imagery and longitudinal cohort studies.
 Co-developing and publishing journal and/or conference articles.
 Presenting your research to international audiences and visitors.

 Participating in and contributing to team meetings.

 Presenting the project internally and externally, and preparing material for such presentations.

items.desc: Baximus AB söker nu en driven och lösningsorienterad AI-ingenjör för ett uppdrag inom nästa generations fordonsutveckling. I rollen kommer du att arbeta med tidig konceptutveckling, prototyper och genomförbarhetsstudier (feasibility assessments) i gränslandet mellan maskininlärning och fordonsdynamik, energisystem och intelligenta cockpit-funktioner. Du arbetar nära domänexperter för att identifiera tillämpningsområden där AI kan skapa mätbart affärsvärde, bygga och utvärdera tidiga konceptmodeller baserade på verklig och simulerad fordonsdata samt dokumentera tekniska beslutsunderlag (go/no-go). Huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter Utveckla, träna och testa tidiga AI/ML-prototyper med hjälp av verklig och syntetisk/simulerad data. Definiera och utvärdera tekniska nyckeltal (KPI: er) avseende prestanda, beräkningskostnad, redundans och robusthet. Genomföra förstudier gällande beräkningsbegränsningar (compute/latency), integration och datatillgång. Samarbeta med domänspecialister inom fordonsutveckling för att omsätta tekniska frågeställningar i tillämpbara modeller. Bidra till återanvändbara kodbibliotek, testmiljöer och ramverk för snabb konceptvalidering. Internationella resor kan förekomma vid behov (upp till 1–2 veckor per år). Kvalifikationer och skall-krav För att matcha rollen uppfyller du följande krav: Utbildning: Civilingenjörs- eller masterexamen inom datateknik, artificiell intelligens, robotik, nätverksteknik eller likvärdig teknisk utbildningsbakgrund. Erfarenhet: 0–3 års erfarenhet inom tillämpad maskininlärning eller mjukvaruutveckling (inklusive examensarbete, forskningsprojekt och relevant praktik). Programmering: Mycket goda kunskaper i Python samt erfarenhet av bibliotek som NumPy och Pandas. Maskininlärningsramverk: Praktisk vana av PyTorch, TensorFlow eller Keras. Verktyg: Erfarenhet av versionshantering i Git samt containerisering med Docker. Språk: Mycket goda kunskaper i engelska i tal och skrift (då detta är det dagliga koncernspråket). Meriterande erfarenheter Vi ser det som ett stort plus om du har: Erfarenhet av LLM-agentarkitekturer, Text-to-SQL eller applikationsutveckling med FastAPI. Kännedom om simuleringsverktyg eller CAD-geometri (t.ex. STEP/STL-hantering, IPS eller pythonOCC). Praktisk erfarenhet av förstärkningsinlärning (Reinforcement Learning) eller datorseende (Computer Vision). Erfarenhet från forsknings- eller utvecklingsprojekt inom fordonsindustrin. Vi erbjuder Marknadsmässig fast månadslön (enligt överenskommelse baserat på branschpraxis och utbildning). Kollektivavtalsliknande villkor med fullt tjänstepensions- och försäkringspaket (tjänstepension, sjukförsäkring, TFA och TGL). Möjlighet att arbeta i teknikens framkant tillsammans med ledande ingenjörsteam i Göteborg.

items.desc: The Role The Rosalind Franklin Institute (the Franklin) is a technology institute established by the UK Government as a unique centre committed to advancing tools that are needed to transform healthcare in the future. The Institute brings together researchers in life and physical sciences, and engineering, to develop a spectrum of tools which we will use to image, interpret and intervene in biological systems. These insights will speed up the discovery of new medicines, help find new diagnostics and contribute to a deeper understanding of human health and disease. Our Science Strategy seeks to focus the Franklin’s research and unite our researchers around our Technology Innovation Challenges and Life Science Challenges. For more information on the Franklin’s Challenges click here. This research opportunity within the Virtual Cell project will advance molecular mapping of cells by expanding the range of proteins and macromolecular complexes that can be reliably detected and characterised in cryo-electron tomograms and develop methods to track how these change over time and in response to cellular perturbation. The Research Associate will develop machine-learning methods for particle localisation, detection and classification in crowded cellular volumes. The work will emphasise learning from limited annotations, generalisation to additional molecular species and experimental datasets, and discovery of candidate particle populations beyond existing labelled classes. Methods will address low signal-to-noise ratios, missing-wedge artefacts, and variation in particle orientation, abundance and conformation. The role will explore integration of complementary structural, molecular and imaging data, such as predicted or experimental protein structures, proteomics, molecular interaction data, and fluorescence or correlative microscopy. These sources will guide detection, constrain candidate molecular identities and support validation, with explicit consideration of their uncertainty, spatial resolution and potential biases. Working closely with experimental and computational researchers, the role-holder will establish robust benchmarks, develop reproducible software, and validate detections and candidate identities through subtomogram analysis and complementary evidence. The role offers opportunities to develop scientific independence within an interdisciplinary team. Key Responsibilities As a Research Associate you will: Develop and apply machine-learning methods to broaden the range of proteins and macromolecular complexes that can be detected and characterised in cryo-electron tomograms. Explore how complementary structural, molecular and imaging data can improve analysis and support interpretation of molecular organisation in cells. Work with experimental and computational colleagues to prepare datasets, evaluate methods and validate biological findings. Develop reproducible analysis workflows and research software, and share methods and findings through documentation, publications and presentations. Plan data acquisitions with experimentalists who conduct them, analyse and interpret results and supervised delivery of outputs (e.g. research report, patent application) in a scientific/technology area of interest. Work within a project team, contributing to wider projects around Franklin's key Challenges. Lead major contributions to outputs from research including papers, patents and both internal and external presentations. Support and develop others including day-to-day supervision of students or visitors in areas related to own research. Have supervised, staged progression to first stages of scientific independence with opportunities to further develop science and skills/experience. Enhance your research through collaboration with other researchers and make active contributions to exchanging of ideas through your own network. Be able to understand, interpret, create and communicate appropriately within a research context. Develop search and discovery skills and techniques. Be supervised by a Scientist/Senior Scientist in delivery of research outputs, either in the context of a project or Challenge or as an early career development fellow. Before submitting your application please ensure you read the Job Information Pack for full details of this role. This can be found at the bottom of the page. items.desc: Department: Detection Location: Remote Description Who are we? Hi! 👋 We are Ravelin! We're a fraud detection company using advanced machine learning and network analysis technology to solve big problems. Our goal is to make online transactions safer and help our clients feel confident serving their customers. And we have fun in the meantime! We are a friendly bunch and pride ourselves in having a strong culture and adhering to our values of empathy, ambition, unity and integrity. We really value work/life balance and we embrace a flat hierarchy structure company-wide. Join us and you’ll learn fast about cutting-edge tech and work with some of the brightest and nicest people around - check out our Glassdoor reviews. If this sounds like your cup of tea, we would love to hear from you! For more information check out our blog to see if you would like to help us prevent crime and protect the world's biggest online businesses. The Team You will be joining the Detection team. The Detection team is responsible for keeping fraud rates low – and clients happy – by continuously training and deploying machine learning models. We aim to make model deployments as easy and error free as code deployments. Google’s Best Practices for ML Engineering is our bible. Our models are trained to spot multiple types of fraud, using a variety of data sources and techniques in real time. The prediction pipelines are under strict SLAs, every prediction must be returned in under 300ms. When models are not performing as expected, it’s down to the Detection team to investigate why. The Detection team is core to Ravelin’s success. They work closely with the Data Engineering Team who build infrastructure and the Intelligence & Investigations Team who liaise with clients. The Role We are currently looking for a Data Scientist to help train, deploy, debug and evaluate our fraud detection models. Our ideal candidate is pragmatic, approachable and filled with knowledge tempered by past failures. Evaluating fraud models is hard; often times we do not even get labels for 3 months. You’ll need to use your judgement when investigating cases of ambiguous fraud and when you’re investigating the veracity of the model itself. We have to build robust models that are capable of updating their beliefs when they encounter new methods of fraud: our clients expect us to be one step ahead of fraud, not behind. You will be given the equipment, space and guidance you need to build world class fraud detection models. The work is not all green field research. The everyday work is about making safe incremental progress towards better models for our clients. The ideal candidate is willing to get involved in both aspects of the job – and understand why both are important. Key Responsibilities Build out our model evaluation and training infrastructure. Develop and deploy new models to detect fraud whilst maintaining SLAs Write new features in our production infrastructure Research new techniques to disrupt fraudulent behaviour Investigate model performance issues (using your experience of debugging models). Requirements Around 1 year's experience building and deploying ML models using the Python data stack (numpy, pandas, sklearn or pytorch). Strong analytical skills. Being a strong collaborator with colleagues outside of your immediate team, for example with client support teams or engineering. Being skilled at communicating complex technical ideas to a range of audiences. The ability to prioritise and to manage your workload. In this role, you will focus on developing and scaling agentic infrastructure and systems for robot autonomy. items.desc: Ready for a challenge? Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience. Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe. About This Role In this role, you will join the User Behaviour Analytics (UBA) team, the group responsible for building the data foundations that power all customer experiences at Just Eat Takeaway. We work collaboratively across CRM, Product, and Marketing to lead with data, deliver trusted insights, and care about the quality and impact of what we build. As a Data Scientist in the User Behavioural Analytics team, you will own machine learning products that predict customer behaviour and directly inform marketing decisions across Just Eat Takeaway's marketplace. Your models will power use cases such as Customer Lifetime Value, Inactivity and Order Frequency Segment predictions, enabling campaign targeting and value-based bidding. You will be responsible for the full ML lifecycle, from data analysis and model development through to productionisation and monitoring of predictive performance. This includes writing production-grade Python code and efficient SQL pipelines, deploying models to cloud-based ML infrastructure for both batch and near real-time predictions, and continuously monitoring model quality to ensure reliable, scalable outputs. You will also be involved in measuring model impact on business metrics through experiments, helping the team understand how predictions translate into tangible business performance. These are some of the key components to the position : Model Development & Assessment: Lead well-defined assignments to develop, maintain, and improve machine learning models that predict customer behaviour. Select appropriate techniques for each problem, validate rigorously, and track performance against business objectives. Data Analysis & Engineering: Use SQL and Python to acquire, transform, and clean large-scale datasets. Apply appropriate techniques for handling outliers, missing values, and exploratory data analysis to create data structures relevant to customer behaviour prediction problems. Production Standards & Model Monitoring: Write production-quality Python code and efficient SQL for data and ML model pipelines that can scale across our marketplace. Be mindful of production environment rules, deploy models to cloud-based infrastructure, and help monitor predictive performance of models in production — identifying and responding to degradation, or data quality issues. Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to automate or improve existing processes; recommend solutions based on established best practices. Actionable Insights: Translate analytics output into clear, actionable insights for decision-making. Assist in presenting these to stakeholders in easy-to-understand language, using data visualisation where appropriate. Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with Data, ML Engineers, and Marketing stakeholders; participate in cross-functional projects, building business acumen and domain knowledge from collaborating colleagues. Team Ways of Working: Contribute to sprint planning, technical prioritisation, and knowledge-sharing to help the team collaborate effectively and deliver together. What will you bring to the team? Practical ML experience: hands-on experience building and validating ML models, comfortable working independently under general supervision while knowing when to seek guidance from more senior colleagues. ML technique fluency: familiarity with statistical and machine learning techniques (classification, regression, boosted trees, uplift modelling, forecasting, hyperparameter tuning) and how to select the right approach for a given problem. Production-grade Python: coding abilities that go beyond notebooks, writing clean, testable code suitable for engineering workflows and collaboration with technical teams. Proficient SQL: across complex data warehouses, including partitioning, window functions, and large-table joins, with focus on query efficiency and data quality. AI-assisted workflows: comfortable using AI tools and building skills to automate and accelerate day-to-day work, including writing, debugging, and optimising code, and analysing data. Version control: familiarity with Git for collaborative development and code management. Problem-framing and communication: translate ambiguous business questions into modelling approaches and explain technical results to non-technical stakeholders with respect and mutual support. Self-starter attitude: comfortable with autonomy and ambiguity, thriving in fast-paced environments where you can build rapidly, test rigorously, and roll out successes at scale. items.desc: Job Description Are you passionate about robotics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies? Join AVL and gain hands-on experience in developing and testing applications for humanoid robots. Work alongside experienced engineers, explore cutting-edge technologies, and contribute to innovative projects in robotics and Physical AI. Support the development of applications and skills for humanoid robots. Implement and test robot behaviors including perception, grasping, pick-and-place, and material handling. Set up and operate robotic hardware, sensors, simulation environments, and AI development toolchains. Support robot training, simulation, testing, validation, and performance analysis. Research and evaluate new technologies in humanoid robotics, Physical AI, and robot learning. Document results and collaborate with AVL engineers and technology partners. Profile Description Ongoing university studies in Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. This position is designed for students who can commit to working 20 hours per week alongside their studies. Strong interest in humanoid robotics, AI, and innovative technologies. Programming skills in Python and/or C++. Familiarity with Linux and Git; experience with ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac, MuJoCo, Gazebo, or PyTorch is an advantage. Good command of English. Strong communication skills. A curious, proactive mindset, a structured approach to problem-solving, and the ability to work both independently and as part of an international team. Able to think beyond boundaries. Strong driver of change and innovation. Passionate about AI and digital technologies. Ready to turn your interest in robotics and AI into practical experience? Join our team and help shape the future of intelligent robotics! We Offer AVL contract, long-term opportunity Group accident insurance, private medical insurance Flexible working time, home office possibility (60%) International projects, business trips Travel reimbursement Relaxation and fitness room Cafe and restaurant in the office building ABOUT AVL HUNGARY KFT. AVL Hungary Kft., founded in 2002, has become a leading research and development center in almost all areas of powertrain systems in recent years by combining the 100-year tradition of the Hungarian vehicle industry and the innovative activities of the global company. The Hungarian company's team of more than 500 professionals works in a high-tech development environment not only in the headquarters in Érd, but in Budapest, Zalaegerszeg and Kecskemét. The team is operating primarily in the fields of R&D - planning, simulation, testing, software development, calibration, and production planning. The results of the work of our colleagues and the technical innovations created by AVL are used in passenger cars, heavy vehicles, construction machinery and ship industries of five continents: AVL Hungary participates in national and international projects, works with the most modern tools, and develops the powertrains of the future.

items.desc: Program Summary - Data Science & Technology Internship Company Overview: Castleton Commodities International is a leading global energy commodities merchant and infrastructure asset investor. As a trader, CCI deploys capital on a proprietary basis in the physical and financial commodity markets, providing the Company with market insights and access. As a strategic investor and developer, CCI leverages its market expertise, operations capabilities, and industry knowledge to invest in, and develop, select commodity infrastructure assets. Our strategically integrated platform has generated strong risk-adjusted returns for our investors since our formation. Position Overview: CCI is developing a leading-edge Data Science platform, as staying at the forefront of data management and analytics is essential to our investment strategy. We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented Machine Learning Intern with a strong interest in quantitative analysis, particularly time series forecasting to join our Global Data Science team in our London office. Our Machine Learning Internship provides a unique opportunity to work with fundamental market data, generating insights that support our commercial trading business. You will be responsible for analyzing time series data related to market fundamentals in the Power, Natural Gas, and Oil sectors, helping to identify key supply and demand drivers. These insights will play a vital role in forecasting price movements and supporting risk management decisions. Responsibilities: Apply mathematical and statistical knowledge to enhance existing machine learning applications and explore new solutions. Work closely with Data Scientists, Analysts, and Traders to design, implement, and optimize machine learning models for time series forecasting, including ARIMA/SARIMA, gradient boosting methods (e.g., XGBoost), LSTM networks, and linear regression-based approaches. Assist in designing and implementing end-to-end data ingestion processes, ensuring seamless data flow to investing teams. Work with desk heads, traders, and analysts to understand current data architecture, investment processes, and functional requirements for data science analysis. Contribute to identifying and back-testing new data sets, leveraging machine learning techniques to drive insights. Conduct ad hoc research on emerging project topics, including energy fundamental data, analytics trends, and best practices in big data and artificial intelligence. Qualifications: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's Degree or higher in Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Computer Science or related technical field with a focus in Machine Learning. Expected graduation date of Winter 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028. Experience applying machine learning techniques such as regression, time series forecasting, deep learning, reinforcement learning, or predictive modeling to solve problems involving complex data patterns and market dynamics. Strong programming experience in Python (preferred libraries: Pandas, NumPy, etc.) Ability to communicate and interact with a wide range of users, from very technical to non-technical backgrounds. Strong analytical skills with demonstrated attention to detail.

items.title: AI Fellow, Regulatory Policy, AI for Health
items.card: You will research the current state of medical device regulatory systems across the region, support our Wellcome-funded work with the Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ) to operationalise a regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled mental health products, and work with the Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation in AI & Digital Health Technologies (CERSI-AI) at the University of Birmingham to
items.desc: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year. PATH’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative is our flagship technical team working across divisions to deliver best-in-class evaluation and implementation of AI in health, spanning model evaluation to product development and service innovation. We aim to use AI to address the world’s largest health inequities. We’re looking for a researcher to help PATH understand how national regulators in sub-Saharan Africa can be more effectively supported to assess and oversee software and AI as medical devices, and to turn that understanding into practical capacity strengthening. You will research the current state of medical device regulatory systems across the region, support our Wellcome-funded work with the Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ) to operationalise a regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled mental health products, and work with the Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation in AI & Digital Health Technologies (CERSI-AI) at the University of Birmingham to develop a course that strengthens regulators’ understanding of software as a medical device (SaMD), AI as a medical device (AIaMD), and frontier AI in healthcare settings. You will have the option of registering for a PhD at University College London (UCL), co-supervised by PATH and UCL, built from this work (assuming you don’t already have a PhD). The role is a strong fit for an early-career researcher with a grounding in regulation, governance, or quality management who wants to shape how AI-enabled health products are regulated in low- and middle-income countries. Please apply by Monday, November 23, 2026 end of day for priority consideration. Responsibilities Design and Deliver Research on Regulatory Systems in Sub-Saharan Africa (50%) A core element of the role will be figuring out how to formally study the regulatory sandboxes we’re running and post-market oversight arrangements, document lessons learned, and prepare those insights for dissemination (both in the academic literature, to policymakers, and more broadly). In parallel to the core task, this role will undertake additional research: An example of our current work: we’re mapping the current state of medical device regulation across sub-Saharan Africa, spanning which national regulatory authorities have a legal mandate and an operational pathway for medical devices, SaMD, and AIaMD; how they are staffed and resourced; where they sit against the World Health Organisation (WHO) Global Benchmarking Tool; and how far they rely on reliance, recognition, and regional harmonisation mechanisms. Future research could include: Desk research: Build on the aforementioned survey’s findings to examine the legislative reforms needed to drive national and continental action, and whether there is value in mental health-specific instruments being developed. Qualitative research: Engage with medical device leads in national regulatory authorities, as well as device manufacturers (and specifically those developing mental health-relevant tools), to better characterise challenges to progress and what interventions need to be prioritised. Quantitative/simulation: Leverage our ongoing portfolio of patient simulation and benchmarking projects to test certain assumptions that current legislation or regulatory approaches appear to take for granted. Thought leadership: Work with the technical experts in the team to think out loud about what frontier AI (general-purpose and generative models) means for existing medical device frameworks, quality management system requirements, and the practical limits of what a regulator can verify. A key part of the role is ensuring we follow best practices for research. You will work with PATH’s Office of Research Affairs to keep our studies compliant with institutional and funder requirements, prepare protocols, and shepherd them through ethics review and the associated approvals (at PATH, and with the relevant national committees in the countries where we work), maintain the records that allow us to account for what was done and why, and contribute to the donor reports, read-outs, and progress updates that keep our funders and partners informed. Convene and Support Delivery of Our Regulatory System Strengthening Programme (50%) Across this part of the role, you will serve as the primary partner for PATH’s Chief AI Officer, working together to draw on the expertise of CERSI-AI, PATH’s internal specialists, as well as our wider network of consultants, to ensure that the right people are brought together at the right time, with the agenda agreed and the preparation done, so that the programme keeps moving and what is decided is written down …

A fully funded 39 month position is available at the University of Sheffield in the field of Surface engineering & tribology for silicone-free consumer products, funded by EPSRC. The project aims to decode the fundamental polymer physics/chemistry of lubrication and slip planes across complex, heterogeneous surfaces, using explainable machine learning and materials informatics to rationally design sustainable, high-performance formulations. You will be responsible for developing explainable machine learning models (symbolic regression, Bayesian optimisation, and genetic algorithms) to decode polymer-solvent thermodynamics and map soft-matter physics to real world applications. The position involves featurizing complex polymer architectures, analysing multi-modal experimental datasets, and creating open-source cheminformatics tools in Python/Julia for sustainable inverse formulation design and AI-driven materials discovery. The work is a highly collaborative project between Dr Grant Hill and colleagues within the School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences, and an industrial partner. The project requires a high degree of independence, strong computational skills, and the initiative to bridge theoretical polymer chemistry with experimental data. Main Duties And Responsibilities Algorithm development: Develop and benchmark explainable machine learning models to predict how polymers interact with solvents. Data integration & featurization: Process and featurize complex polymer architectures to link molecular structure with bulk properties. items.desc: Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today. The Faculty of Health, Innovation, Technology and Science is a pioneering Faculty, dedicated to creating and communicating knowledge and opportunities to ensure that all our students can excel within their chosen discipline. The School of Computer Science and Mathematics is dedicated to producing research that has real-world application, boasting specialisms in immersive technologies, applications of artificial intelligence, trustworthy computing technologies and data science. We are seeking to appoint a Research Associate in Artificial Intelligence to join the Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies Research Institute (AIDTRI). AIDTRI brings together multidisciplinary expertise in AI and advanced digital technologies, with research spanning fundamental methodological development through to real-world application and evaluation. Key areas include AI, data science, trustworthy and explainable AI, causal AI, digital twins, immersive technologies, data visualisation and advanced computational modelling. You will contribute to current AI and data science research programmes and to the development of new externally funded research. Key activities will include: conducting high-quality research in AI and Data Science; organising, harmonising and analysing large, multimodal and multi-source datasets; developing and evaluating AI methods; collaborating with internal and external research partners; preparing research papers and conference contributions; contributing to external research funding applications; and supporting research management and activities within AIDTRI. You should hold a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a related discipline, or have submitted your thesis and be awaiting viva. Essential criteria include experience of conducting and publishing high-quality AI research, strong knowledge of AI algorithms, programming experience in Python, R or similar, excellent communication and organisational skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Experience with large and complex AI problems, novel AI or computational methods, advanced Python programming, and research funding proposals would be advantageous. You should clearly demonstrate in your supporting statement how you meet all essential criteria in the person specification, providing specific evidence and examples for each criterion. Evidence against the desirable criteria should also be provided where applicable. We anticipate holding interviews the second week of December 2026. Further information about AIDTRI is available at: https://www.ljmu.ac.uk/research/centres-and-institutes/artificial-intelligence-and-digital-technologies-research-institute For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Professor Ivan Olier, Head of AIDTRI, at I.Olier@ljmu.ac.uk . In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies. This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. Find out more about working at LJMU here . If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. The Faculty of Health, Innovation, Technology and Science is committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Gender Equality charter for promoting the career of Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) in higher education. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post and all appointments will be made on merit. Please let us know if you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process. Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated. LJMU are committed to adhering to the Principles set out in the Researcher Development Concordat; in line with this all fixed-term researchers will be supported to complete 10 days professional development activities per year (pro-rata).

items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire d'analyse et d'architecture des systèmes Type de Contrat Convention de stage Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 31031 TOULOUSE Durée du contrat 5 mois Date d'Embauche 01/02/2027 Date limite de candidature : samedi 5 décembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions Title: Master 2 Internship - Runtime Monitors of Neural Network in Aerospace Supervisors: Jérémie Guiochet (https://homepages.laas.fr/guiochet) Profile: Computer Science, AI Level: Master 2 (MSc) Duration: 5–6 months Location: LAAS-CNRS, Toulouse, France (https://www.laas.fr) Salary: ~€600/month Keywords: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Generation, Safety Monitoring Technologies: Python, AI Frameworks Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in safety-critical applications, such as autonomous vehicles and surgical robotics. In these systems, perception tasks largely rely on deep neural networks (DNNs). However, the use of these components remains challenging because their behavior cannot be fully guaranteed, raising concerns about reliability and safety. Runtime monitoring mechanisms are among the promising approaches to address these limitations. Their purpose is to continuously monitor neural network behavior in order to detect or prevent potential errors. Two main families of monitors can be distinguished: rule-based monitors, which verify whether predefined safety properties are satisfied, and data-driven monitors, which are themselves developed through machine learning, often using neural networks. Evaluating the performance of these monitors is essential, particularly in situations where the main neural network produces incorrect predictions. This raises several important questions: What data should be used to evaluate these monitors? How should such data be collected, generated, and selected? How can the dataset cover both nominal and abnormal operating conditions? The objective of this internship is to investigate data generation and selection strategies for monitor evaluation and to develop a framework for testing and evaluating one or more monitoring mechanisms proposed by the AI research community. The internship will be conducted as part of an aviation-related case study, focusing on runway detection during aircraft landing approaches. It builds on the LARD (Landing Approach for Runway Detection) tool and dataset, which we have extended into Lardon-x, a tool currently under development at ANITI and LAAS-CNRS.
