items.desc: Over Rensa Family Rensa Family is een toonaangevend technisch handelsbureau in de Nederlandse installatiebranche. Met circa 1600 medewerkers levert de organisatie dagelijks installatiematerialen aan installateurs. De stage wordt uitgevoerd bij Rensa Family Company, waar de centrale diensten worden verzorgd voor alle bedrijven binnen de Rensa Family. Wat ga je doen? Data vormt een belangrijke pijler binnen de organisatie en wordt intensief gebruikt voor rapportages en stuurinformatie via Power BI. Binnen het BI‑team wordt continu gewerkt aan het verbeteren van datakwaliteit, datamodellen en inzichten. In voorbereiding op toekomstige ontwikkelingen wil Rensa Family haar data‑omgeving geschikt maken voor het verantwoord en effectief inzetten van AI‑toepassingen binnen Business Intelligence. Tijdens Deze Afstudeerstage Werk Je Aan De AI Readiness Van De BI‑omgeving, Met Focus Op Het Gebruik Van Data Door Het BI‑team En Power BI‑gebruikers. De Nadruk Ligt Niet Alleen Op Het Onderzoeken, Maar Vooral Op Het Voorbereiden, Analyseren En Verbeteren Van Data Zodat Deze Geschikt Wordt Voor Toekomstige AI‑toepassingen. Jij Gaat Dit Verder Uitwerken Door Datakwaliteit, structuur en consistentie te analyseren Te beoordelen in hoeverre de huidige datasets, modellen en definities AI‑geschikt zijn Concrete verbeteringen en richtlijnen uit te werken voor AI‑ready data Daarnaast onderzoek je hoe BI-specialisten en Power BI-gebruikers AI-functionaliteiten kunnen benutten om vragen te stellen over data, datatransformatie, analyse en visualisatie, en hoe AI het ontwikkelproces kan versnellen. Wat is het doel? Inzicht krijgen in de huidige mate van AI‑readiness van de BI‑data Het identificeren van concrete verbeterpunten op het gebied van datakwaliteit, modellering en standaardisatie Het voorbereiden van datasets en datamodellen zodat deze geschikt zijn voor AI‑gedreven analyses Het opleveren van praktische richtlijnen, aanbevelingen en eventuele proof‑of‑concepts voor AI‑gebruik binnen Power BI Wat is je profiel? Je volgt een HBO‑opleiding in de richting van IT, Data, BI of Analytics Je hebt interesse in datakwaliteit, datamodellering en de toepassing van AI binnen BI Je kunt zelfstandig analyseren en werkt gestructureerd toe naar concrete verbeteringen en adviezen Wat bieden wij jou? Swipe om de arbeidsvoorwaarden te bekijken Werken binnen het Microsoft Azure‑landschap, onder andere met Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse, Azure Data Warehouse en Power BI. Programmeren met T-SQL, Python en DAX. Begeleiding door een ervaren BI‑professional uit het BI‑team. Samenwerken in een betrokken en multidisciplinair team van zes collega’s (vier developers, een product owner en een business analyst). Werken volgens de SCRUM‑methodiek. Een kijkje achter de schermen bij een moderne, datagedreven familieorganisatie. Ruimte om inhoudelijk impact te maken op de datavolwassenheid van de organisatie Waarom jij moet solliciteren! Je werkt aan een toekomstgericht onderwerp met directe impact op hoe de organisatie met data en AI omgaat. De verbeteringen die jij doorvoert zorgen ervoor dat de BI‑omgeving daadwerkelijk klaar wordt gemaakt voor AI‑toepassingen. Daarmee lever je een zichtbare en structurele bijdrage aan de verdere professionalisering van datagedreven werken binnen Rensa Family.

Olink panels provide innovative, high-quality solutions for human protein biomarker discovery, enabling researchers to measure thousands of proteins simultaneously from just a few microliters of blood. Using highly specific and thoroughly validated assays with a wide dynamic range, Olink’s technology overcomes traditional limitations in protein analysis and supports deeper insights into human biology and disease. We are currently seeking a Data Scientist to join our Data Science Development team. As part of the Data Science Development team in Uppsala R&D, you will contribute to advancing data analysis capabilities for both external and internal use. This role offers the opportunity to work across the full product lifecycle, from concept development through post-launch support, applying cutting-edge data science and bioinformatics expertise. A Day in the Life: Develop methods and tools for data analysis for external and internal use. Participate in the development of new products through all phases from concept development to post product launch. Participate in research and development of concept design, product ideas and products in accordance with project plans and work schedules. Develop and improve quality control methods. Assist in quality control and troubleshooting of data issues. Develop solutions for monitoring and analysis of QC parameters to ensure quality in products and processes. Participate in the development of future bioinformatic and data analytics solutions for internal use. Organize internal training in programming, data analysis, and QC of data. Provide study design and advanced data analysis expertise and support to other departments. Requirements: MSc or PhD in Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Computer Science, Molecular Biology or similar. Advanced degree plus 2 years of relevant experience, or Bachelor’s degree plus 4 years, in data science or a related field. Experience integrating, harmonizing, and analyzing complex data in life sciences, biotechnology, biopharma, healthcare, clinical research, diagnostics, or laboratory environments. Advanced proficiency in R, Python, and SQL, for data processing, transformation, analysis, and automation. Moderate experience in applying statistical methods in medical or biological research, especially with data from high throughput technologies in proteomics and genomics Experience with cloud and scalable analytics platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, Spark, Databricks) and DevOps/version control (Git). Demonstrated strong communication skills, both oral and written in English. To succeed in this role, you need to have a strong analytical mind and an interest in modern statistical and data analysis methods including machine learning. It is also important to have the ability to translate complex scientific and business problems into analytical solutions and communicate technical concepts effectively to scientific, technical, and non-technical stakeholders. If you enjoy solving challenging problems, don't mind working both independently and in collaboration with others and stay current with emerging technologies, we are looking forward to meeting you! Why Join Us? At Olink, Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will be part of a nurturing team that values integrity, innovation, and involvement. We offer an encouraging environment where your diverse experiences and perspectives are appreciated, enabling you to thrive and excel in your career. Come aboard and contribute significantly to global health and safety! The last day for applications is on the 6th of December.

Overstromingen, grote stormen, bosbranden) op kort, middellange en lange termijn in kaart kunnen brengen. Daarnaast wordt gekeken in hoeverre deze beschikbaarheid, bruikbaarheid en toepasbaarheid verschilt tussen Europese landen en dus in hoeverre deze technieken bruikbaar zijn voor universele Europese modellen. Ben je geïnteresseerd in de klimaatgerelateerde rampen, gezondheidseffecten hiervan en de toepasbaarheid van AI voor maatschappelijk relevante vraagstukken? Lijkt het je leuk om mee te draaien in een internationaal team? Zie je jezelf meedraaien in een team bij het RIVM? Stuur ons dan een reactie! Ook voor vragen kan je bij ons terecht. Dit krijg je €800 Arbeidsovereenkomst voor bepaalde tijd 36 uur Dit bieden we nog meer Naast het salaris ontvang je een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,50% van je bruto jaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaal vriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Tot de secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden behoren onder meer verschillende studiefaciliteiten, bedrijfsfitness, volledige vergoeding van je OV-reiskosten woon-werkverkeer en gedeeltelijk betaald ouderschapsverlof. Als kennisinstituut van de overheid op het gebied van volksgezondheid, voeding, milieu en veiligheid vervult het RIVM de rol van betrouwbare adviseur. In deze rol ondersteunt het RIVM burgers, professionals en overheden bij de uitdaging onszelf en onze leefomgeving gezond te houden. Het RIVM voert kennisintensieve taken uit zoals het Rijksvaccinatieprogramma, de Bevolkingsonderzoeken en CBRN (Chemische, Biologische, Radiologische, Nucleaire) crises en verricht daartoe zelf onderzoek, maar verzamelt ook wereldwijd kennis en past die toe. Het RIVM brengt jaarlijks een groot aantal kennisproducten uit: publicaties, adviezen, rapporten en factsheets. Het RIVM kiest positie midden in de maatschappij, om zo iets te betekenen voor anderen – voor opdrachtgevers, voor netwerk- en ketenpartners en voor de maatschappij als geheel. Deskundig, betrouwbaar en waakzaam zijn belangrijke kernwaarden, naast onafhankelijk, omgevingsbewust, dienend en verbindend. Over de afdeling binnen het RIVM De afdeling Gezondheid Leefomgeving en Nazorg (GLN) beoordeelt het risico op fysieke en mentale gezondheidseffecten als gevolg van (langslepende) crises en rampen. Tevens adviseert de afdeling over de wenselijkheid en invulling van gezondheidsonderzoek en psychosociaal crisismanagement bij (langslepende) crises en rampen, in nauw overleg met lokale partners en met VWS. Over RIVM RIVM: deskundig, betrouwbaar en onafhankelijk Als Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM) zijn we een deskundige, betrouwbare en onafhankelijke adviseur voor overheid, professionals en burgers. Ons doel: een gezonde bevolking en een duurzame, veilige en gezonde leefomgeving. We bewaken gezondheid, ziekten, de kwaliteit van de leefomgeving én het milieu. Daarvoor doen we onderzoek en we verzamelen kennis voor toegankelijke informatie en toepasbare adviezen. Het RIVM zorgt voor een goede geboortescreening, het bestrijden van infectieziekten en heeft een centrale rol bij het Rijksvaccinatieprogramma en de bevolkingsonderzoeken. items.desc: Role Purpose The Team The AI Team, part of Front Office Technology, builds the AI tools and platforms used across the front office: assistants and agents for investment teams, secure access to firm data and knowledge, and the controls that let AI be used safely in a regulated trading environment. We build central capabilities for the whole firm and support teams across the business as they build their own, bringing the most successful into Technology ownership as they grow in importance. The Role As an AI Engineer with a focused on optimisation, you will build and run the AI tools and platforms used across the front office, and make sure the firm gets the most value from its AI spend. You will design and deliver central AI services, assistants and agents for PMs, traders and researchers, while making AI usage more efficient across providers and teams. A key area is moving suitable workloads onto open-weight models served on our own GPUs, fine-tuned where needed, at a fraction of the cost of external APIs. The team is small and priorities shift as the firm’s use of AI grows. You will be expected to pick up other priorities across the team as they arise, so this role will not be dedicated solely to cost optimisation. Why Join Build AI tools used in live investment workflows, and help the firm run its own models on its own GPUs. Join an AI function with a real mandate and the backing to shape how AI is built across the firm. Work with current frontier AI tooling in a team that values engineering discipline over hype. Key Responsibilities Building front office AI tools Build central platform capabilities such as model access, an AI gateway, MCP services and knowledge retrieval, with entitlements, audit and monitoring built in. Design, build and run AI assistants, agents and services used by PMs, traders, quants and researchers. Self-hosted models Stand up and run production inference for open-weight models on our own GPUs, using engines such as vLLM or SGLang behind OpenAI-compatible APIs. Fine-tune models for specific front office tasks with LoRA and QLoRA, and serve multiple adapters efficiently on shared base models. Apply quantisation (e.g. FP8, AWQ, GPTQ) and serving optimisations such as prefix caching, continuous batching, speculative decoding and tensor parallelism to get the most from each GPU. Benchmark latency and throughput (time to first token, inter-token latency, tokens per second) with tools such as GuideLLM, and plan GPU capacity against service levels. Run inference on Kubernetes with GPU scheduling, autoscaling, and monitoring of GPU utilisation and health. Cost optimisation Route traffic across hosted and self-hosted models through a central gateway such as LiteLLM, sending each workload to the cheapest model that meets its quality bar. Apply cost levers: model right-sizing, prompt caching, batching and context efficiency. Compare the cost and quality of self-hosted and API models per task, and support provider and hardware decisions with evidence. Centralising and reuse Identify AI applications built in the business with real usage or value, and bring them onto central platforms. Turn repeated requirements into shared services, MCP servers, skills and agent templates, reducing duplication across teams and providers. Wider AI engineering Pick up other priorities across the team as they arise, from new front office tools to knowledge services, MCP integrations and data access. Contribute to shared engineering standards, code review and production support. Business outcomes Provide usage, performance and cost metrics from the models and services you run to the colleague responsible for AI spend reporting, so decisions to scale, consolidate or retire AI tools are based on data. items.desc: About Nominal Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them. Nominal is building the Hardware Intelligence Platform that gives engineers increased visibility into complex physical systems, helps them make better decisions, and ultimately gets their products into the real world faster. It brings together the systems, data, intelligence, and applications hardware engineering requires to meet the AI moment. Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics. Our customers span aerospace, defense, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and robotics. They include Anduril, Shield AI, Wisk Aero, Pratt Miller Motorsports, Antares, and Shinkei Systems, amongst others, alongside programs within the U.S. Air Force and Navy. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Tesla, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software. Some of the world’s leading technology investors, including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, and Insight Partners, are backing Nominal’s ambition to change how machines are built and operated. We’re looking for engineers who want to take on hard problems and help make a new generation of world-changing hardware possible. London is our newest office, and we're building the team that will grow Nominal across the UK and Europe. Mission Operations We’re looking for students with solid engineering fundamentals on track to graduate in Summer 2027 or sooner. As a Mission Ops Engineer, you'll be the person on the ground helping customers deploy Nominal's platform into their test and operations environments — propulsion test stands, satellite mission ops, flight test, and similar high-stakes settings. You'll train users, troubleshoot issues in real time, and build the relationships that turn a deployment into a long-term partnership. 🚀 What you’ll do Own the outcome for a set of customer accounts: run discovery to understand their test problems, align internal and external stakeholders, and deliver solutions that stick, on time and on target Deploy and integrate: write code to ingest and normalize customer data from test stands, DAQs, telemetry streams, and other hardware sources, and build the pipelines and automations that turn that data into decisions Build custom apps, dashboards, and workflows on Nominal's platform for each customer's specific needs Build trusted relationships with everyone from front line engineers and operators to senior executives, and train their teams as they bring Nominal into daily use Debug issues across the stack in real time, and know when to solve something yourself versus pull in the broader team Be the bridge between customers and Nominal's product and engineering teams: translate customer needs and critical dependencies into solutions, and turn patterns you see across customers into clear product input 🎯 We'd love to hear from you if... You're graduating in Summer 2027 or sooner and are interested in a full-time graduate role. You have hands-on experience with hardware systems — test stands, robotics, aerospace, automotive, medical devices, energy systems, or similar — through internships, personal projects, research, or coursework You can write code (Python or similar) to work with real-world data, whether that's parsing sensor logs, building data pipelines, or automating analysis to turn data into decisions You're intellectually curious and think in systems: you see the big picture, still sweat the details, and have a strong intuition for the math and physics behind the hardware You communicate clearly and honestly, in writing and in person, and can explain technical ideas to everyone from front line engineers to senior executives, including people who aren't engineers You bring humility, eagerness to learn, and empathy, and you lift the people around you. You don't just spot problems; you solve them You're comfortable working through open-ended problems in unfamiliar environments, and you can take a technical concept from planning through deployment You're willing to travel occasionally to be on-site with customers You have a genuine interest in hardware testing and the industries Nominal serves ⚡ Bonus Experience with data acquisition or hardware tools (DAQs, LabVIEW, MATLAB/Simulink) or data tools (SQL, Python, Pandas, Grafana) Experience deploying technical software or data products into real-world workflows, whether through an internship, co-op, or capstone project Prior customer-facing, account management, technical …

items.desc: A GK Capital está a recrutar um Quantitative Analyst – Algorithmic Trading (FX) para integrar a SIWA , empresa do portefólio do G-Lock First Fund dedicada à negociação automatizada no mercado cambial. A função tem como objetivo avaliar o desempenho dos algoritmos com dados reais de sinais, ordens e posições, explicar os fatores que afetam a rentabilidade e o risco e testar melhorias às regras de negociação. Principais responsabilidades Avaliar a qualidade dos sinais e o resultado líquido das operações por algoritmo, versão e par cambial. Quantificar o impacto de spreads, comissões, slippage e swaps. Investigar posições que evoluem contra o sinal inicial ou permanecem abertas além do horizonte previsto. Medir as perdas, a duração e a margem utilizada e testar o efeito de fechar mais cedo ou reduzir a posição. Avaliar a exposição agregada por moeda e estratégia, testar cenários de stress e propor limites e alertas operacionais. Analisar o impacto do aumento do volume negociado nos custos de execução. Propor e testar alterações às regras de entrada, saída e dimensionamento das posições. Comparar as propostas com a versão em produção, com custos realistas e validação fora da amostra, e acompanhar o desempenho das alterações aprovadas. A função incide sobre o desempenho dos algoritmos da SIWA. A análise geral de mercado, a elaboração de previsões cambiais próprias e a formulação de uma visão macroeconómica ficam fora do âmbito. Perfil pretendido Formação em Matemática, Estatística, Engenharia, Física, Informática, Finanças Quantitativas ou área equivalente. Domínio de Python e SQL, com experiência em séries temporais e análise de dados de mercado, ordens ou execuções. Conhecimento de custos de negociação e métricas de risco, com capacidade para produzir análises reproduzíveis e recomendações concretas. Será valorizada experiência em FX, backtesting e avaliação de estratégias em produção . Primeiros 90 dias Espera-se a entrega de um painel de desempenho por algoritmo, de um diagnóstico das posições problemáticas e da exposição agregada, e de uma primeira lista de melhorias sustentada por testes. Candidaturas As candidaturas deverão ser submetidas através do LinkedIn, com o respetivo CV.

About the Role Join Ipsos' growing Synthetic Data team and help build the next generation of AI-powered research solutions. Working alongside data scientists, researchers and engineers, you'll explore how synthetic data and digital twins can transform the way insights are generated and delivered. This is a unique opportunity to work at the cutting edge of generative AI, applying deep learning and LLM technologies to solve genuine business challenges. You'll be involved in designing and evaluating synthetic datasets, building digital twin applications, developing experimentation frameworks and helping turn emerging technologies into practical tools that can be used across Ipsos. Your application will be reviewed by someone from our Talent Team who will be in touch either way to let you know the outcome. Ready to have an impact? Apply now!

items.desc: About The Role What if your curiosity and creative thinking could make AI safer for millions of people? items.desc: Sea Sentinel AI · Munich · Full-Time What we do Sea Sentinel AI is a risk intelligence platform with a focus on the maritime shipping industry. We monitor ports, vessels, and shipping routes worldwide, detecting disruptions before anyone else does. When a vessel crashes, we detect it from a local newspaper hours or days before major media picks it up. When a typhoon is still days away from hitting a port, we warn customers before the chaos starts. This way, we enable our customers to be ahead of crises, rather than reacting to them at the last minute. We sell our intelligence primarily via API, which means our customers integrate it directly into their own systems and workflows. Our rigorous focus has allowed us to build the leading product in this niche. It shows: we consistently win deals with global customers, large and small. We grow because customers pay for what we build. The role Our core data infrastructure, PRISM, is built and proven. Every day it analyzes more than 800,000 news articles alongside weather and other data to find the disruptions that matter to our customers. Owning PRISM. This is your first priority. Keeping PRISM sharp takes two things: solid traditional engineering, and serious prompt tuning backed by evaluations and test harnesses. You'll own this together with the team. Taking PRISM into new verticals. We're ambitious. Next up are other verticals such as air cargo and energy risk intelligence (LNG, oil, gas). You'll identify the master data each vertical needs, benchmark data providers, and make the case for what to integrate and how to integrate it into PRISM. You'll work with structured and unstructured data and form your own views. This is where the role becomes product work: you care whether what you build solves the right problem. Working on a system that’s still moving. PRISM runs on messy, real-world data, and new models change what’s possible every few months. You are encouraged to test your ideas against ambiguous inputs and production conditions where things break, and you’ll decide which new model capabilities are worth adopting. Then you’ll prove it with evals. You won't have a backlog handed to you on Monday morning. You'll be expected to understand the system well enough to know what the most important problems are and go solve them. What we're looking for Must haves: You've run something in production and dealt with it breaking. You know what silent failure looks like and how to find it, using sensible monitoring and alerting. Good coding standards and the judgment to know when to apply them and when to move fast. You drive your own work: you identify problems, prioritize, and see them through without someone telling you what's important. Analytical curiosity. You're comfortable sitting with ambiguous questions, forming hypotheses, and making a case for your conclusions. Real experience tuning LLM systems. You know from experience that a prompt which works well on one model can fall apart on another, or on the same model with slightly different input or settings. You treat model behavior as something to measure, never something to assume. An evaluation mindset. Fixing one case often breaks another, so you build eval sets and regression tests, measure before and after, and only ship a change you can show is a net improvement. Experience monitoring and tracing LLM pipelines in production. The question you should be able to reason about: if the input changes, or we turn this knob up or down, how does the pipeline behave, and what does that mean for our customers and analysts? Experience with AWS, Pulumi or SST. Bonus points for experience in: News data analysis (!), logistics, or energy TypeScript Web scraping (proxies, crawlers, etc.) Structuring or maintaining enterprise-grade APIs We don't expect you to arrive knowing everything. We do expect you to arrive with strong fundamentals, good instincts, and the drive to figure out what you don't yet know. We care more about the right person than the right CV. A sharp, motivated junior and a seasoned engineer can both be the right fit for this role. What we're looking for is curiosity, ownership, and the ability to operate with minimal hand-holding. Compensation reflects experience. What we offer Full ownership from day one. You'll work directly with the founders. When you make a decision, it ships. You'll be a core part of how we expand into new areas, from the research phase through to production. We go where the opportunity actually is. We have strong revenue and we're growing in the areas where we know we can win. We don't chase trends or move into spaces because someone else thinks we should. The roadmap is driven by what our customers need and what the data tells us. A domain worth caring about. Our customers reroute shipments around typhoons, prevent factory shutdowns, and pull cargo out of war zones because we gave them the intelligence to act in time. The work you do will have consequences you can actually …

items.desc: Über uns Die DEUTSCHE FACHPFLEGE deckt in ganz Deutschland das gesamte Spektrum der Pflege ab. Unsere Leistungen reichen von der Alten-, Kranken-, Intensiv- und Beatmungspflege bis hin zur Palliativpflege. Unser Ziel seit dem ersten Schritt: den Zustand der uns anvertrauten Menschen zu verbessern, im Idealfall bis hin zur vollständigen Genesung. Dein Arbeitsplatz Hannover | Vollzeit | Home Office-Möglichkeit Wie lässt sich künstliche Intelligenz sinnvoll in Pflege, Verwaltung und Steuerung einsetzen? Welche Idee hilft im Alltag wirklich – und wie wird daraus eine Lösung, die in bestehende Systeme passt und verantwortungsvoll genutzt werden kann? Als KI-Entwickler (m/w/d) bei der DEUTSCHEN FACHPFLEGE begleitest Du diesen Weg: von der ersten Fragestellung gemeinsam mit den Fachbereichen bis zur Entwicklung, Integration und Überwachung der Anwendung. Als Arbeitsort sind sowohl unsere Verwaltungsstandorte in Herford als auch in Hannover möglich. Deine Aufgaben KI-gestützte Anwendungen entwickeln und betreiben, die Pflege, Verwaltung und Steuerung im Alltag entlasten sollen. Gemeinsam mit den Fachbereichen geeignete Anwendungsfälle identifizieren und deren Nutzen, Aufwand und Risiken bewerten. KI-Lösungen sicher in die bestehende Systemlandschaft einbinden. Lösungen testen und evaluieren sowie deren Qualität im Betrieb überwachen. Auf einen datenschutz- und regelkonformen Einsatz achten – von der DSGVO bis zur EU-KI-Verordnung. Kolleginnen und Kollegen beraten und sie dabei unterstützen, KI-Anwendungen zu verstehen und zu nutzen. Dein Profil Du hast ein Studium der Informatik, Data Science oder Wirtschaftsinformatik abgeschlossen oder vergleichbare Kenntnisse durch Berufserfahrung erworben. Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von Software- oder KI-/ML-Lösungen; idealerweise Erfahrung mit Large Language Models und vorzugsweise Kenntnisse im Microsoft-Azure-Umfeld. Sehr gute Python-Kenntnisse sowie ein sicherer Umgang mit Daten und Schnittstellen. Datenschutz und IT-Sicherheit sind Dir vertraut. Du hast ein Gespür für den verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit sensiblen Daten. Freude daran, technische Themen verständlich zu erklären und mit anderen zusammenzuarbeiten. Sehr gute Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse. Von Vorteil: Erfahrung im Gesundheitswesen oder in regulierten Umfeldern sowie Kenntnisse in MLOps und Cloud-Plattformen.

items.desc: Help build and evolve our platforms that powers Data, Analytics and AI across PostNL. Develop cloud-native platform services, developer tooling and automation that enable teams to innovate faster. As a Software Engineer within our Data, Analytics & AI Platform team, you build the software, tooling and cloud platform that enable our data scientists, analytics engineers and software developers to deliver solutions faster and more reliably. Using modern software engineering practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and cloud technologies, you help create a scalable platform that accelerates innovation across PostNL. Visible work : Your work and our platform is used every day by all PostNL data specialists. You develop reusable platform services, internal developer tooling and automation that simplify how data teams provision environments, deploy applications and manage cloud resources. By improving developer experience and reducing operational complexity, you help teams move from experimentation to production more efficiently to support analytics, machine learning and AI applications across logistics, sorting, customer contact and planning. Challenge : You help develop PostNL’s new Databricks platform while keeping existing AWS-based solutions running. The challenge is to evolve platform capabilities while enabling AI and data teams to develop, deploy and operate their solutions consistently and at scale. Drawing on your understanding of the software lifecycle, you translate platform users’ needs into reusable software, platform services and automation, and explore and integrate new capabilities. Good atmosphere : You work with colleagues who are eager to improve, help each other and enjoy trying new things. You can bring your ideas, learn from others and grow in a supportive team. Flexibility : You work hybrid: partly from home and partly from our modern office in the historic Stationspostgebouw next to The Hague Hollands Spoor. This gives you freedom to organise your week in a way that works for you. Development opportunities : Technology evolves quickly—and so do we. You'll work with modern cloud technologies, Infrastructure as Code, Databricks, AWS, GitHub Actions, AI development tooling and developer platform engineering practices. Through the PostNL Academy, conferences and collaboration with experienced colleagues, you'll continue developing both your technical and engineering skills. Your role As a Software Engineer within the Data, Analytics & AI Platform team, you build and maintain the software platform that enables Data Science & AI Engineering teams across PostNL. You develop platform services, internal tooling and automation that make it easier for teams to build, deploy and operate reusable data and AI components. Your focus is on writing high-quality software, improving developer experience and creating reusable platform capabilities. Infrastructure as Code is a key part of your work. Using AWS CDK with typescript you automate the provisioning of cloud infrastructure and platform resources. You contribute to deployment pipelines, project templates and platform components that enable engineers to work consistently and efficiently. Using those insights, you translate engineering best practices into reusable platform capabilities, templates and automation. While you are not responsible for building AI and machine learning models yourself, you understand the lifecycle of Data Science & AI solutions and continuously improve the platform that supports them. Using (IaC) technologies such as AWS CDK and Terraform, you help create the platforms (on AWS and Databricks) that allow engineers to focus on solving business problems instead of managing infrastructure. You work closely with the users of the platform to understand their needs and translate them into scalable platform capabilities. Your colleagues You join the Data Analytics Services team within the Data Center of Excellence. The team includes Platform Software Engineers and Solution Consultants. You work closely with them, as well as with the data scientists and AI engineers who use your platforms every day. The team works in an open, collaborative and innovative way. Wednesday is our office day, when the team comes together in person to collaborate, share knowledge, and connect. Together, we combine engineering excellence, data expertise, and collaboration to make data and AI innovation accessible across PostNL. What we'll deliver A role full of innovation and work that you see reflected throughout the Netherlands. You help shape the logistics e‑commerce platform of the future. You can count on a strong package of employment benefits. Salary between €4,588.87 and €6,498.75 gross per month based on 37 hours (32 hours is also possible). Hybrid working and flexibility in organising your time. If you work from home two or more days a week, you receive a €45 net monthly allowance. 8% holiday allowance and 25 vacation days based on full‑time …

items.desc: Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones) Start Date: ASAP Languages: English Team: Engineering About The Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand. We are looking for a Research Engineer, Synthetic Data to build the synthetic data pipeline. You will turn domain-specific workflows into synthetic training tasks that are realistic enough to teach useful behaviour, structured enough to generate at scale, and difficult enough to expand model capabilities. This is a hands-on research engineering seat, not a commercial or privacy-systems role. You will design how synthetic tasks are created, mutated and validated, and you will analyse what those tasks actually teach models and agents. This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70–80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. What You'll Do Work with subject-matter experts to create synthetic tasks for training AI agents across a range of professional and technical domains. Design synthetic task-generation methods that produce diverse, realistic and learnable tasks. Build systems and tooling to mutate, validate and improve synthetic tasks. Analyse model and agent performance on synthetic tasks to understand what the tasks are teaching and where they fail. Develop metrics to quantify and understand synthetic task diversity, realism, learnability and related qualities. Take synthetic data pipelines from early research through to reliable systems, including in areas where the roadmap is not fully prescribed. What We're Looking For Proficiency in Python, Docker and Linux environments. Experience with synthetic data research methods — please be ready to describe this in your application. A strong understanding of what “good synthetic data” means, and of its limitations. Experience building synthetic data pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap. Experience working on environments, evals or benchmarks. Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating remotely across time zones. Strong candidates may also be detail-oriented enough to catch subtle inconsistencies or edge cases in synthetic data; able to reason from first principles about task design, scoring and failure modes; and comfortable in unstructured problem spaces or early-stage environments. Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above. Why This Role Matters for You Build the synthetic data pipeline: You will design the tasks and systems that generate training data at scale, not only run experiments on someone else's pipeline. Research that has to work in production: Turn messy, domain-specific workflows into tasks that are realistic, measurable and usable for training agents. See what the data actually teaches: Analyse model and agent performance, and improve the tasks when they fail. High ownership, unstructured problems: You will build without a fully prescribed roadmap, from method design through tooling and metrics. San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70–80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. items.desc: Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones) Start Date: ASAP Languages: English Team: Engineering About The Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand. We are looking for a Research Engineer, Synthetic Data to build the synthetic data pipeline. You will turn domain-specific workflows into synthetic training tasks that are realistic enough to teach useful behaviour, structured enough to generate at scale, and difficult enough to expand model capabilities. This is a hands-on research engineering seat, not a commercial or privacy-systems role. You will design how synthetic tasks are created, mutated and validated, and you will analyse what those tasks actually teach models and agents. This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70–80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. What You'll Do Work with subject-matter experts to create synthetic tasks for training AI agents across a range of professional and technical domains. Design synthetic task-generation methods that produce diverse, realistic and learnable tasks. Build systems and tooling to mutate, validate and improve synthetic tasks. Analyse model and agent performance on synthetic tasks to understand what the tasks are teaching and where they fail. Develop metrics to quantify and understand synthetic task diversity, realism, learnability and related qualities. Take synthetic data pipelines from early research through to reliable systems, including in areas where the roadmap is not fully prescribed. What We're Looking For Proficiency in Python, Docker and Linux environments. Experience with synthetic data research methods — please be ready to describe this in your application. A strong understanding of what “good synthetic data” means, and of its limitations. Experience building synthetic data pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap. Experience working on environments, evals or benchmarks. Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating remotely across time zones. Strong candidates may also be detail-oriented enough to catch subtle inconsistencies or edge cases in synthetic data; able to reason from first principles about task design, scoring and failure modes; and comfortable in unstructured problem spaces or early-stage environments. Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above. Why This Role Matters for You Build the synthetic data pipeline: You will design the tasks and systems that generate training data at scale, not only run experiments on someone else's pipeline. Research that has to work in production: Turn messy, domain-specific workflows into tasks that are realistic, measurable and usable for training agents. See what the data actually teaches: Analyse model and agent performance, and improve the tasks when they fail. High ownership, unstructured problems: You will build without a fully prescribed roadmap, from method design through tooling and metrics. San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70–80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. items.desc: Join us, be part of more. We’re so much more than an energy company. We’re a family of brands revolutionising how we power the planet. We're energisers. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels, whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it. We have an exciting opportunity for a Data Scientist to join our team, using relevant data to tackle complex business challenges and turn insight into measurable outcomes. You'll work across a varied portfolio of customer, commercial and operational problems, from understanding churn and retention to Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV), segmentation, propensity modelling and operational optimisation. This is more than a model-development role. You'll have the opportunity to build reusable, production-ready solutions, embed models into business processes and see the real-world impact of your work. Key Accountabilities: Design, build, test and deploy statistical and machine learning models to solve customer, commercial and operational challenges. Analyse large and complex datasets to identify patterns, opportunities and drivers of customer behaviour, translating your findings into clear, actionable recommendations. Partner with stakeholders to turn commercial questions and opportunities into well-defined data science problems. Develop solutions across areas including churn and retention, CLTV, segmentation, propensity modelling, customer targeting and optimisation. Build robust feature engineering, training and inference pipelines, using technologies such as Python, PySpark and Databricks. Help take models into production through automated workflows, testing, version control, CI/CD, monitoring and model lifecycle management. Collaborate with data engineers, platform teams and fellow data scientists to create scalable, reliable solutions while maintaining high standards of data quality, model governance and responsible AI. Here’s what we’re looking for: Experience applying statistical analysis and machine learning to real-world business problems. Strong programming skills in Python and SQL, with experience working with large and complex datasets. Experience with, or exposure to, PySpark and Databricks. A good understanding of machine learning techniques, which could include classification, regression, gradient boosting/XGBoost, segmentation, propensity modelling or survival analysis. Experience or knowledge of production ML practices such as Git, CI/CD, MLflow, automated testing, model deployment and monitoring. Strong analytical thinking, with the ability to take an ambiguous business question through exploration and modelling to an actionable recommendation. The ability to explain complex analytical approaches, assumptions and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. A collaborative and curious approach, with a willingness to learn, challenge existing thinking and share knowledge. Experience within customer analytics, energy, utilities, retention, pricing or commercial analytics would be beneficial, but isn't essential. Location: We operate a Flexible First approach, giving colleagues flexibility in how and where they work. This role can be predominantly home-based, although ideally you will be based within commutable distance of our Cardiff site and be flexible to travel across our sites as may be needed on occasion for team meetings. Why should you apply? We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Help us, help you. We would love for you to share any information about yourself throughout our recruitment process so that we can better understand you and help shape your journey.

items.desc:
Platform & Pipeline Engineering 
 Develop, automate, and maintain resilient data pipelines connecting on-premises 
 laboratory equipment, high throughput test benches, and edge systems to Microsoft Azure.
 Investigate, unpack, and parse complex, non-standard, binary, proprietary, and undocumented file formats where standard connectors do not exist.
 Implement parsers and normalization routines capable of ingesting diverse technical data streams, for example:
 High-frequency sensor streams, time series, and bus telemetry.
 Multi-dimensional scientific arrays, spatial grids, and spectral data.
 - Hierarchical, nested, and unstructured binary logs or custom ASCII exports.
 Event logs, operational metadata, and intermittent experimental batch runs.
 Clean, validate, and transform fragmented or schema-less raw data into optimized, partitioned Lakehouse tables (Delta Lake/Parquet) ready for analytics and ML model training.
 Deploy, monitor, and maintain pipeline resources on Azure using Terraform, Databricks, and containerized workflows following established team templates.
 Collaboration & Lab Support 
 Work directly alongside experimental scientists, lab engineers, and technicians to decipher raw measurement files, clarify domain-specific semantics, and automate recurring data uploads.
 Collaborate closely with solution architects and senior engineers to implement data ingestion patterns, cataloguing schemas, and governance standards.
 Maintain clear technical documentation, code comments, and onboarding walkthroughs to help research teams connect their equipment seamlessly.
 Support proof-of-concept initiatives exploring metadata integration with corporate AI assistants, data discovery catalogs, and modern data tools.
Education 
 BSc, MSc or Ph.D. in Data Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
 Experience 
 3+ years of professional experience in data engineering, building automated and reliable data pipelines.
 1–2 years of practical experience handling heterogeneous, non-standard, or binary data sources (e.g., physical sensor logs, laboratory exports, hardware telemetry, or raw byte streams).
 1+ years of hands-on experience utilizing Apache Spark (preferably Databricks) and Microsoft Azure in production environments.
 Demonstrated experience deciphering, parsing, or converting non-standard, legacy, or custom data formats into structured data structures.
 Technical Skills 
 Strong proficiency in Python for data manipulation (including binary data handling using modules like struct, byte manipulation, NumPy, Pandas, and PySpark) and Bash.
 Solid understanding of modern Lakehouse concepts (Delta Lake), distributed data processing, SQL, and NoSQL/document datastores.
 Proficient with Git, GNU/Linux environments, and working knowledge of Infrastructure as Code (Terraform).
 Practical experience with standard transport mechanisms (e.g., REST APIs, SFTP, Kafka/Event Hubs, or IoT/streaming protocols).
 Mindset & Soft Skills 
 Strong analytical mindset with a natural curiosity to open unfamiliar files, inspect headers, and solve data decoding puzzles.
 Friendly, empathetic communication style with the ability to bridge conversations between laboratory technicians, domain scientists, and software teams.
 C2 CEFR level in English, written and spoken.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience with scientific/hierarchical file formats (e.g., HDF5, NetCDF, Parquet, Protobuf).
 Familiarity with industrial telemetry or time-series historian protocols (e.g., OPC UA, MQTT).
 Exposure to Azure analytics tooling (Azure Data Factory, Azure Event Hubs, Azure Data Explorer).
 Experience with vectorial databases.
 Languages 
 Fluent in Portuguese.
 B2 CEFR level in English, written and spoken.
 B2 CEFR level in German, written and spoken is a plus

 Challenges in an international environment | career opportunities in one of the best companies in the world | flexible hours | medical services | discounts for employees | sports and health related activities | canteen | good access to public transports | space for creativity.

Pour dépasser les limites de notre calibrage physique actuel, nous explorons des approches basées sur l'apprentissage automatique. L'équipe de recherche a étudié le remplacement de ce calibrage linéaire par une formulation basée sur l'apprentissage automatique, utilisant des arbres de décision à gradient boosté. Cette approche permet d'exploiter un ensemble de variables dérivées de Starwave plus riche et plus expressif. Plusieurs modèles candidats ont été évalués, et un modèle a été sélectionné actuellement pour ses performances prédictives, sa robustesse face à l'hétérogénéité des variables et sa gestion efficace des variables catégorielles. Vos missions En tant que stagiaire, votre projet se déroulera en deux grandes étapes : Étape 1 : Vous commencerez par reprendre le code du modèle IA et le coupler à des bases de données géographiques. En s’appuyant sur des mesures terrains, vous devrez déterminer et évaluer, en fonction du type d’environnement géographique, les variables utiles qui permettent de mieux décrire la propagation radio. Étape 2 : Dans un deuxième temps, en collaboration avec un alternant en data-sciences, vous fusionnerez les variables explicatives que vous avez trouvées avec celles générées par le modèle historique afin d’évaluer les performances de l’inférence avec des mesures de test. Cadrage du besoin : Comprendre les questions métier et identifier les données géographiques pertinentes. Collecte et exploration des données : Repérer les sources disponibles, évaluer leur qualité, leur couverture et leurs limites Préparation des données : Nettoyage, harmonisation des formats et systèmes de coordonnées, traitement des valeurs manquantes et documentation. Analyse spatiale et statistique : Explorer les tendances, relations et répartitions géographiques à l’aide de méthodes adaptées. Modélisation : Définir et tester des approches de Data Science, puis évaluer leurs performances et leurs limites. Visualisation et restitution : Produire des cartes, tableaux de bord ou synthèses accessibles aux équipes métier. Industrialisation : Contribuer à des scripts ou pipelines reproductibles, éventuellement déployés dans un environnement cloud. Documentation et collaboration : Présenter les résultats, documenter les choix méthodologiques et échanger avec les équipes concernées. Votre formation : Vous préparez un diplôme d’ingénieur ou un Master 2 en Mathématiques Appliquées, Data Science, ou en Informatique/Développement. Vos compétences techniques (Hard Skills) : Une excellente maîtrise de Python et de son écosystème pour l'analyse de données (NumPy, Pandas). De solides bases théoriques et pratiques en Machine Learning (Scikit-Learn, TensorFlow ou PyTorch). Une appétence pour la manipulation de bases de données et de données géographiques est un vrai plus. Vous lisez et comprenez la documentation technique en anglais. Vos qualités (Soft Skills) : Rigueur scientifique et curiosité naturelle pour la recherche expérimentale et le prototypage rapide. Esprit d'équipe et aisance relationnelle pour échanger et co-construire avec d'autres profils. Esprit de synthèse pour restituer simplement des concepts techniques complexes. Ce stage est une opportunité de travailler sur une problématique de recherche avancée. Vous pourrez développer vos compétences en Data Science en travaillant en particulier sur le domaine de la propagation et de la prédictibilité des communications sans fil. L'indemnité mensuelle brute de stage proposée est comprise entre 1 000 et 1 500 euros selon votre niveau d'études en cours. A cela s'ajoutent l'accès aux Activités Sociales et Culturelles proposées par votre Comité Social et Economique, l'accès subventionné au restaurant d'entreprise ou aux titres restaurant, ainsi que la prise en charge à hauteur de 50% de votre abonnement aux transports en commun. items.desc: At IONOS, the leading European provider of cloud infrastructure, cloud services and hosting services, you will work together with a wide range of teams. We are characterized by open structures, a friendly working culture and flat hierarchies with a strong team spirit. We firmly believe that work and fun are compatible, and offer you the right environment for this. Our constant growth means that we are always looking for new colleagues. Become part of IONOS and grow with us. About the role Both halves of this role are about the same underlying question: which systems can reach our most sensitive infrastructure, and under what controls. You will own the security architecture for our provider-side infrastructure layer, and you will be the subject matter expert for the AI platforms and agents we operate internally, making sure they run in a secure, governed, auditable state rather than accumulating quietly as a new class of privileged access. This is a hands-on expert role. You set standards, pressure-test designs, and work directly with platform and engineering teams across our brands to get them implemented. Define and maintain security architecture standards and hardening baselines for provider-side infrastructure: virtualization and container platforms, control planes and provisioning systems, DNS, mail infrastructure, and backup and recovery systems. Assess and strengthen tenant isolation across shared hosting, virtualization, and container layers, and drive remediation with the responsible platform teams. Review infrastructure designs and major changes for security impact, and act as an escalation point for infrastructure security questions from platform, cloud, and brand engineering teams. Reduce blast radius on the paths that matter most: privileged access to customer-facing infrastructure, administrative segmentation, secrets handling, and recovery integrity — translated into workable per-brand implementation plans across our heterogeneous platforms. Support Cyber Defense, Vulnerability Management, and IT Emergency Management with infrastructure expertise during incidents and post-incident hardening. Own the security architecture and baseline standards for the AI platforms we run internally: model gateways and self-hosted models, agent frameworks, assistant integrations, connectors, and retrieval pipelines over internal data. Define and enforce how agents are identified, authenticated, and authorized: non-human identity handling, credential and token management, least-privilege tool and system access, and where autonomous action requires a human in the loop. Establish what data internal AI systems may access and index, and ensure agent activity is logged, attributable, and reviewable to the standard our regulatory and certification obligations require. Run pre-deployment security reviews for new internal AI platforms and agent use cases, at a pace that fits how fast these are being adopted, and keep a picture of where unsanctioned AI usage is emerging. Advise the security functions and internal engineering teams on adopting AI safely, including the guardrails that make that adoption defensible. Qualification Several years of hands-on experience in infrastructure or platform security, ideally at a hosting provider, cloud provider, telco, or comparably large-scale multi-tenant environment. Deep practical knowledge of Linux, virtualization and container platforms, networking, and the security properties of multi-tenant infrastructure. Strong background in identity and access: privileged access, machine and workload identity, secrets management, authorization models, and infrastructure-as-code security. Experience designing and enforcing security standards in a heterogeneous, partly legacy landscape, and getting them adopted by teams you do not manage. Working knowledge of how LLM and agent systems are built and operated, and of the risks specific to them: prompt injection through untrusted data, over-scoped tool access, data exposure via retrieval, unlogged autonomous action, model and provider dependency. Ability to make and defend risk-based decisions, including blocking a deployment with a clear rationale, and to explain technical risk to non-technical stakeholders. Fluent English; German is a strong advantage given our regulatory and public-sector environment. Advantegous Hands-on experience deploying or securing internal AI platforms, agent frameworks, or tool-calling integrations in production. Familiarity with NIS2 / BSIG or ISO 27001 Background in DNS, e-mail infrastructure, or abuse-adjacent platform security. Experience in a multi-brand or post-acquisition environment where the same control has to land in several different implementations. Security engineering or development background (automation, tooling, scripting). Encadré(e) par un Senior Data Scientist en charge de la modélisation mathématique et de la biologie des systèmes, vous contribuerez à un projet visant à évaluer et affiner des approches de Machine Learning pour guider la conception de formats d’anticorps multispécifiques (notamment des T-cell engagers). Pour pallier la complexité et le bruit des données expérimentales, votre projet se concentrera sur la création d'un environnement de test robuste basé sur des données synthétiques. Vos principales responsabilités incluront : Génération de données : Concevoir un générateur de données synthétiques reproduisant les caractéristiques clés de l'optimisation des formats d'anticorps (assemblage modulaire, relations structure-activité non linéaires, courbes dose-réponse, bruit de mesure) afin de fournir une vérité terrain contrôlée. Optimisation de l'espace latent : En vous appuyant sur un pipeline existant, réévaluer et affiner les méthodes de représentation numérique (embeddings) des architectures d'anticorps. L'objectif sera d'améliorer la structure de l'espace latent utilisé par les processus gaussiens pour prédire la relation dose-réponse et l'activité fonctionnelle. Benchmarking rigoureux : Évaluer systématiquement les performances des modèles sur les données synthétiques, en analysant leur robustesse, la qualité de l'estimation des incertitudes et leur capacité à généraliser à des formats moléculaires non observés. Simulation et communication : Utiliser cet environnement contrôlé pour simuler des stratégies de sélection de nouvelles architectures à tester, et communiquer vos résultats de manière pédagogique aux scientifiques de différentes disciplines. Votre profil : Nous recherchons un(e) étudiant(e) curieux(se), rigoureux(se) et motivé(e) par l’application du machine learning à des problématiques scientifiques concrètes en recherche pharmaceutique. Le stage se situe à l’interface entre data science, modélisation mathématique et biologie ; une expertise préalable en anticorps n’est pas indispensable. Compétences requises : Formation : Étudiant(e) en dernière année de Master (M2) ou d'école d'ingénieurs (Bac+5) à la recherche d'un stage de fin d'études, ou jeune diplômé(e) (Bac+5). Spécialisation en mathématiques appliquées, machine learning, data science, informatique scientifique, statistiques, bio-informatique ou domaine quantitatif proche. Hardskills : Maîtrise de Python et de l'écosystème d'analyse de données/ML. Solide compréhension théorique et pratique des algorithmes de machine learning et des statistiques. Une première expérience ou de solides connaissances en modèles probabilistes (processus gaussiens), deep learning (PyTorch/GPyTorch), optimisation ou apprentissage de représentations (embeddings) constituent un atout majeur. Anglais scientifique courant (lecture de publications et documentation). Softskills : Rigueur scientifique, capacité à s'approprier des concepts mathématiques avancés et forte autonomie. Goût pour la recherche algorithmique et la résolution de problèmes complexes. Excellente communication pour vulgariser et expliquer clairement ses résultats à une équipe interdisciplinaire (biologistes, modélisateurs, data scientists). items.desc: IONOS S.R.L. Cyber Security Engineer (f/m/d) Infrastructure & AI Platform Security (Hybrid) At IONOS, the leading European provider of cloud infrastructure, cloud services and hosting services, you will work together with a wide range of teams. We are characterized by open structures, a friendly working culture and flat hierarchies with a strong team spirit. We firmly believe that work and fun are compatible, and offer you the right environment for this. Our constant growth means that we are always looking for new colleagues. Become part of IONOS and grow with us. About the role Both halves of this role are about the same underlying question: which systems can reach our most sensitive infrastructure, and under what controls. You will own the security architecture for our provider-side infrastructure layer, and you will be the subject matter expert for the AI platforms and agents we operate internally, making sure they run in a secure, governed, auditable state rather than accumulating quietly as a new class of privileged access. This is a hands-on expert role. You set standards, pressure-test designs, and work directly with platform and engineering teams across our brands to get them implemented. Define and maintain security architecture standards and hardening baselines for provider-side infrastructure: virtualization and container platforms, control planes and provisioning systems, DNS, mail infrastructure, and backup and recovery systems. Assess and strengthen tenant isolation across shared hosting, virtualization, and container layers, and drive remediation with the responsible platform teams. Review infrastructure designs and major changes for security impact, and act as an escalation point for infrastructure security questions from platform, cloud, and brand engineering teams. Reduce blast radius on the paths that matter most: privileged access to customer-facing infrastructure, administrative segmentation, secrets handling, and recovery integrity — translated into workable per-brand implementation plans across our heterogeneous platforms. Support Cyber Defense, Vulnerability Management, and IT Emergency Management with infrastructure expertise during incidents and post-incident hardening. Own the security architecture and baseline standards for the AI platforms we run internally: model gateways and self-hosted models, agent frameworks, assistant integrations, connectors, and retrieval pipelines over internal data. Define and enforce how agents are identified, authenticated, and authorized: non-human identity handling, credential and token management, least-privilege tool and system access, and where autonomous action requires a human in the loop. Establish what data internal AI systems may access and index, and ensure agent activity is logged, attributable, and reviewable to the standard our regulatory and certification obligations require. Run pre-deployment security reviews for new internal AI platforms and agent use cases, at a pace that fits how fast these are being adopted, and keep a picture of where unsanctioned AI usage is emerging. Advise the security functions and internal engineering teams on adopting AI safely, including the guardrails that make that adoption defensible. Qualification Several years of hands-on experience in infrastructure or platform security, ideally at a hosting provider, cloud provider, telco, or comparably large-scale multi-tenant environment. items.desc: Konsert Strategy & IP is a leading consultancy at the intersection of business strategy, technology and intellectual property. Founded in Gothenburg in 2006, we work with some of the world's largest technology-intensive companies, close to the leaders who decide where to compete and how to win through technology and IP. Since 2024 we have been part of the international Rouse Group. Like every consultancy, we are adapting to an environment that AI is reshaping. Much of the research, analysis and preparation that used to fill a project team's weeks can now be done by machines. Our clients face the same shift from the other side. Their strategy, technology and IP functions are under a clear mandate to work faster and leaner with AI. But today's landscape of point tools depends on the user to supply the context, and without it the tools speed up the doing without improving the thinking. What clients still need is sound judgment, grounded in the right context. That is where the real value of AI lies: not in faster work, but in better, more reliable and more impactful decisions. So rather than defend the old consultancy model, we are rebuilding ours around that: consultants who work inside our clients' organizations, supported by an AI platform that holds the client's context. That platform is Sapivia. We are now growing our in-house tech team, to make sure we have the capabilities under our own roof to take Sapivia to the next level. What we are building: Sapivia Sapivia is Konsert's AI platform. At its core is the context layer: a client-specific knowledge graph that holds the context every decision depends on. How the business, its technology and its intellectual property connect, what depends on what, and the reasoning behind the decisions already made. We have built that picture for clients by hand for twenty years; Sapivia captures it, keeps it alive and makes it available to people and AI alike. Our consultants build the context layer together with the client. The client's own people, Konsert's forward-deployed strategists and the AI tools the client already uses can then reason and act on the same picture, one that grows richer over time. Sapivia is already in use with clients, starting in IP, where the need is sharpest. But the same picture answers the questions every technology company has to ask: which technologies matter, where to compete and how to turn knowledge into advantage. That is where we are taking it next. The Konsert tech core team We are building a small tech core team: a handful of engineers with complementary skills. The team is led by a Tech Lead and sits in Gothenburg, next to the consultants who deploy Sapivia with clients. Build work happens in close collaboration with those consultants, several of whom spend part of their time in the team, so the domain expertise and the client's reality are in the room when we build. We work in an agile way with shared ownership: everyone is close to the users, effort goes where it is needed, and the team ships several times a week and owns the result together. Development runs in close alignment with Konsert's leadership team, with short paths to user input and quick decisions. The tech core team has a central voice in how Sapivia is shaped. Around this core, we scale with external developers and the Rouse Group's technology organization. Questions we are working on right now Giving AI the right context is only the start. Turning that context into decisions that large companies can rely on raises questions that few teams have answered yet. These are some of the ones we are working on now. They are open questions, not tickets, and you will help answer them. How do we assure the quality of AI responses at scale, when the right answer is often a matter of judgment? How do we best combine deep domain knowledge with what the models already know? How do we make a rich, connected body of knowledge feel simple and intuitive to work with? How do we give large organizations precise control over who sees what, across regions, teams and many users? How do we shorten the path from prototype to production code, while keeping the freedom to experiment? The role: Applied AI engineer You bring the applied AI competence to the core team. Sapivia's AI features run on the client-specific knowledge graph as their context layer, and the hard problems are in the harness around the models: retrieval, context management, tools, guardrails, evaluation and feedback loops. You take LLM-based features from first prompt to production, set up the evaluation that assures their quality, and help the team decide where AI creates value and where it does not. You work closely with the consultants whose judgment the system is meant to support. Ditt uppdrag är att omvandla data till meningsfulla insikter som stärker verksamhetsutvecklingen, samt i din roll som AI-koordinator identifiera var AI-tillämpningar kan bidra till ökad kvalitet och förbättrad service för våra medborgare. Agerar AI-koordinator, kartlägger och etablerar AI-stöd: Du driver arbetet med att kartlägga, prioritera och införa AI-stöd i arbetsuppgifter inom socialförvaltningen där det förbättrar service till medborgaren, kvalitet och effektivitet i verksamheten. You will be expected to: Work directly with clients to understand their current objectives and establish new strategies Monitor and evaluate current performance across organic search and AI, identifying appropriate strategies to implement to improve overall performance. Covering: - Technical audits - Keyword research - Competitor analysis - Search intent research - AI visibility - Content strategy - Website user experience Coordinate with the wider team ensuring all objectives are aligned Test new ideas, tools and approaches and sharing what you learn with the team Report on leads, revenue, conversions and meaningful business outcomes What we’re looking for Someone who knows their way around SEO, but is also tuned into AI. You will need to be analytical, commercially aware and naturally curious to see where AI is heading. You’ll enjoy looking into why something is happening and taking responsibility for doing something about it. We are looking for someone with: A solid understanding of how search engines and AI works A good understanding of the various elements that make up a successful SEO/AI campaign Strong communication skills, written and verbal Good organisational skills, the ability to manage and prioritise multiple tasks Meticulous attention to detail The ability to take data and insights and think outside the box A willingness to learn, take on-board feedback and develop new skills A pro-active attitude You don’t need to arrive knowing everything. items.desc: Let’s transform society together We are Sweco. We are Europe’s leading design, engineering, environment and regulatory consultancy. We are future planners, city shapers, urban innovators, digital transformers, net zero chasers, community connectors, social enterprisers and lifestyle improvers. We are #DifferenceMakers. And we are now taking applications for the Autumn 2027 cohort of our Early Careers Graduate Scheme. Now recruiting: Graduate Geotechnical Engineer to join our Infrastructure and Environment Division. At Sweco, we recruit to role – meaning you’ll join a team where your skills, interests and ambitions align with the work you’ll be doing. Our Ground Engineering team delivers a diverse portfolio of projects across the UK, supporting clients in sectors including energy, national and local infrastructure, highways, water and commercial development. The recent work includes supporting the British Antarctic Survey’s £100 million Antarctic Infrastructure Modernisation Programme, as well as delivering the detailed geotechnical design for nationally significant projects such as A47 Improvement Programme and M25 Junction improvements, York Central regeneration and Comrie Flood Mitigation Scheme. We’re looking for graduates who share our values, are curious about the world around them and are motivated to help build a more sustainable and resilient future. What will you be doing? As a Graduate Geotechnical Engineer, you’ll: Work as an integral member of a close-knit team of geotechnical engineers and engineering geologists. Collaborate with multi-disciplinary project teams to deliver geotechnical design projects at every stage, from feasibility and desk studies through to ground investigation, detailed design and construction. Assist with the planning and supervision of ground investigations, including site visits, drilling, sampling, field testing and site surveys. Gather, interpret and analyse data and test results from field and laboratory investigations. Use engineering software to model geotechnical behaviour, assess ground stability and support the development of practical design solutions. Contribute to the preparation of technical reports and other project documentation, summarising investigation findings and providing recommendations for construction methods and design considerations. Assist with the design of geotechnical solutions, including earthworks, foundations, slopes, retaining structures and other ground engineering measures. Support the supervision of ground investigation and earthworks activities during construction. Develop your technical, commercial and professional skills through hand-on experience, mentoring and involvement in a wide range of projects. This is an excellent opportunity to begin your career in a supportive and forward-thinking team, working on projects that make a real difference to communities and the environment. Who are we looking for? Our unique, personalised programme is designed for passionate, forward-thinking graduates who want to change the world around them, who will thrive in a dynamic team environment, and who are hungry to collaborate not only with fellow graduates, but also with mentors and leaders across the business. What do you need to apply? We want to hear from you if you… Have a degree relevant to the role you’re applying for. Have less than 12 months of relevant work experience (excluding placements). Are confident using Microsoft Office and other relevant digital tools. Are driven, proactive, and solution-oriented. Can work in the UK without restrictions either now or in the future. This is a permanent role, and we’re looking for candidates who can grow their careers with Sweco without a time limit. What’s in it for you? Our Graduate Scheme offers a two-year blended learning experience, with a tailored programme delivered virtually and face-to-face. You’ll have the chance to network and grow with the 2027 cohort. Personal growth will be supported by our Early Careers team, mentors and subject matter experts from across the business. Structured masterclasses focus on Internal Insight, Skills Development, and Subject Matter Expertise, helping fast-track your development as you pursue professional accreditation. The programme builds your confidence early in your career and gives you a platform for genuine impact within Sweco. You’ll receive a permanent position with an industry-standard salary and benefits package, including 25 days holiday, a great pension and life assurance. Read what our previous graduates have to say about their experience on the careers section of our website. Please note, we will hold an assessment centre for this position in January / February 2027. All applicants will be contacted regardless of the outcome. We provide feedback to all attendees of interviews or assessment centres but are unable to offer personal feedback at the application stage. Ready to make a difference with us? Apply now, and let's transform society …

items.card: Responsibilities: You will join our Quantum firmware Team as a Cloud Engineer. You will build the layer through which the world reaches our quantum computers.
