items.desc: Help us turn complex data into clear, trusted insight. At Abri, our purpose is to help people have a place they’re proud to call home. Reliable data helps us make better decisions for our customers, our communities and our organisation. We’re looking for a hands-on Data & Business Intelligence Developer to help make that possible. You’ll design, develop and support data pipelines, Power BI models, dashboards and reports that support business performance, regulatory compliance and evidence-based decisions. Working to agreed technical standards and priorities, you’ll take responsibility for the quality of your own work. This is a technical role with no line-management responsibilities. You’ll develop and maintain Power BI solutions, from reusable semantic models and DAX measures to dashboards, reports and subscriptions. You’ll build and optimise Databricks ingestion and transformation pipelines within our medallion architecture, working across Bronze, Silver and Gold layers and applying agreed data quality checks. You’ll also use SQL Server/T-SQL and Databricks SQL to develop queries, views, transformations and analytical datasets, investigate performance and resolve data issues. Working with colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation, you’ll understand and document reporting needs, turn them into practical solutions, and explain what reports and dashboards can—and can’t—tell us. You’ll help people across our Directorates make effective use of Power BI, and create reporting that brings together information from different systems, with drill-down and timely or real-time insight where needed. You’ll assess data sources, support integration and transformation, and look for ways to improve data quality, traceability, reuse and performance. When issues arise, you’ll investigate and document causes and fixes, seeking support or escalating complex problems through the right channels. You’ll collaborate in peer reviews, share knowledge and documentation, and contribute practical technical input as we evaluate new systems and applications. You’ll also keep developing your skills and suggest ways to improve our tools, solutions and ways of working. You’ll bring hands-on experience designing, developing and supporting Power BI reporting and analytics in a customer-focused organisation. You’ll have practical experience with Databricks or Fabric pipelines, a good understanding of medallion architecture and data quality, and strong SQL skills across SQL Server/T-SQL and Databricks SQL. You’ll also have experience with Power BI semantic models, dimensional modelling, DAX, row-level security and performance optimisation, alongside a working knowledge of data architecture, governance, security and master data management. You’ll be comfortable translating business needs into effective solutions, managing your own workload and delivering agreed work to timescales. Clear communication, sound analytical and troubleshooting skills, and the ability to build relationships with technical and non-technical colleagues are important. You’ll be organised, self-motivated and collaborative, ready to raise risks and priorities, share what you know and keep learning in a changing technology environment. Most of all, you’ll bring our values and behaviours to your work through collaboration, innovation, customer focus and professional standards. Experience with Databricks Lakehouse and Bronze, Silver and Gold layers would be useful. We’d also welcome knowledge of Python, Spark, SQL Analytics, Delta Lake or Databricks orchestration; experience in housing, the public sector or a regulated setting; or exposure to advanced analytics, AI, machine learning, forecasting or self-service analytics. You'll be able to be based out of either our Eastleigh office (SO50 6AD), Bracknell office (RG12 1RF), Yeovil office (BA22 8WN) or London office (W10 8BN) a minimum of three days per week to connect and collaborate with colleagues and the other two days can be worked from at a place of your choosing whether that's at another of our offices, a cafe or at home. We’ll review applications and interview suitable people as they come in. If we receive enough applications, we’ll close the advert early, so please apply today so you don’t miss out. Abri is a large housing provider who own and manage more than 58,000 homes and various community assets, serving around 113,000 customers across the South of England. We believe everyone has the right to a good quality safe, warm and sustainable home in a community where they can belong, grow and thrive. What does that look like in real terms? We’re investing £689m over the next ten years in our existing homes to improve building safety and make them more energy efficient. items.desc: Specialist, Lifecycle Programs - CRM focused Do you want to build customer journeys that engage customers across their lifecycle? We are looking for a hands-on lifecycle professional to help Pandora build, maintain and optimise automated customer programs in Bloomreach. As Specialist, Lifecycle Programs, you will translate approved strategies, briefs and playbooks into reliable CRM customer journeys in Bloomreach. You will work closely with the Lifecycle team, markets, Analytics, Digital & Technology and external partners to deliver high-quality lifecycle programs consistently and at scale. What you will do Together with the team, you will help turn our lifecycle strategy into high-quality, scalable customer experiences in Bloomreach. Your focus will be hands-on CRM implementation, quality execution and continuous optimisation. Build and deliver lifecycle programs Translate approved briefs and playbooks into segmentation, targeting and Bloomreach scenario setups. Build, deploy and maintain automated lifecycle programs across email and other relevant CRM channels. Support the rollout and localisation of lifecycle initiatives across markets. Ensure quality and optimise performance Test scenarios end to end and ensure they follow agreed templates, QA standards, contact strategy and suppression rules. Monitor live programs, troubleshoot implementation issues and contribute to clear documentation and handovers. Use performance insights and test results to improve targeting, timing, messaging and journey logic. Collaborate and share expertise Work closely with Lifecycle colleagues, markets, Analytics, Digital & Technology and external partners to deliver programs effectively. Provide hands-on Bloomreach support and share reusable solutions and learnings across the team. Contribute to improving templates, documentation and ways of working. What success looks like Accurate and reliable lifecycle implementations. Consistent use of agreed standards, templates and QA controls. Faster and more efficient delivery across markets. Clear documentation and effective handovers. Improved customer engagement, conversion, lifecycle progression and repeat-purchase outcomes. To succeed in this role, you have Typically 2-4 years of experience in CRM, lifecycle marketing or marketing automation. Practical hands-on experience with Bloomreach Engagement or a comparable marketing automation platform. Experience building automated customer journeys and applying segmentation, targeting and audience logic. An understanding of testing, QA and lifecycle program optimisation. Strong attention to detail and a structured approach to documentation. The ability to collaborate effectively across business, technology, markets and external partners. The judgement to recognise and escalate complex implementation or governance questions. Fluency in English, written and spoken. Why join us? You will join Pandora’s global Customer Lifecycle & Membership team and help turn lifecycle strategy into customer experiences that can be scaled across markets. The role gives you the opportunity to develop deep hands-on Bloomreach expertise, contribute to global lifecycle programs and help improve the standards, templates and ways of working that support our continued growth. Additional information Global Career Band 5B Did we get your attention? If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores. Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025. items.desc: Veo is a global leader in AI-based sports camera technology. Our innovative, fully automatic camera solution enables sports teams to record matches and training sessions without a camera operator. We’re democratizing the world of sports by granting video analysis for teams on all levels—a privilege that used to be only for the few. More than 40,000 clubs in 90+ countries record their games every week. But what truly sets us apart? Our people . We’re a diverse group of innovative thinkers, creators, and problem-solvers who believe in delivering an incredible product—and having fun while doing it. The Opportunity Veo's Revenue Platform is the engine that drives the business. Each subscription, order, invoice, payment and shipment passes through the platform that our team built. We are looking for an engineer to join our team. The team owns the core revenue engine that sits between Veo's products and the systems that run the business: billing, payments, CRM, ERP and fulfillment. Other teams use our APIs to sell, quote, bill and provision. Finance relies on us to get the numbers right. The foundations are in place. The next chapter is about making the platform more robust, easier to build on, and ready for new markets, products and pricing models. You'll help model subscription lifecycles, amendments, quotes, tax and payment flows. You'll make workflows stay correct when a third-party API fails halfway through an order. You'll also work closely with Finance, Sales and Product so the business logic in code matches how the business actually works. What You Will Do Evolve and scale backend services in Rust that process real revenue: orders, subscriptions, invoicing, payments and provisioning. Strengthen our Temporal workflows so they are reliable, idempotent and safe to change, through versioning and replay. Shape the Revenue Platform API into a clear, OpenAPI-first product that internal teams can adopt with confidence. Improve our integrations with billing, payment, CRM, ERP and logistics providers, and handle their failure modes properly. Turn ambiguous commercial requirements (pricing changes, new markets, new payment methods) into correct, well-documented business logic. Own what you ship in production: observability, alerting, incident response, and data migrations that touch thousands of customer accounts. Incorporate modern AI development tools into your workflow to iterate quickly and build thoughtful software solutions. Set technical direction for the platform's next phase, and raise the bar through design reviews, code reviews and testing. What You Could Bring 2+ years as a software engineer, with significant backend experience. Backend experience using Python, Rust, or another comparable language. Experience in revenue-critical domains is a plus: billing, subscriptions, payments, e-commerce, or financial systems. Experience with API design and integrating with third-party APIs. Experience building distributed systems where correctness under failure matters. Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams. You've worked closely with product managers, designers, finance, data and commercial stakeholders. A product-oriented mindset. You care about the outcome, not just the code. Curiosity about modern AI development tools and how they can support everyday engineering workflows. Fluent English, written and spoken. Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community. Values we hold at Veo: Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work. Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing. Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills. Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger outcomes. Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally) We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to contribute meaningfully.

Du vil få mulighed for at sætte dit præg på den løbende videre udvikling af arbejdsområdet, herunder bidrage til automatisering og integration af database-systemer til brug for opgaveløsningen. Du vil være en integreret del af udviklingen i enheden. Da det er et nyoprettet team, søger vi efter forskelligartet kompetencer, der kan bidrage til etableringen, udviklingen og løsningen af opgaven. Derfor vil det være en differentieret opgaveportefølje du og dine nye kolleger kommer til at arbejde med, afhængigt af hvilken baggrund man kommer med. Din kontaktflade vil omfatte flere forskellige enheder og faggrupper i FE og i Forsvaret samt hos udenlandske partnere. Du skal forvente uddannelse og kurser af kortere varighed i både ind- og udland. Du og din baggrund er vigtig Vi forestiller os, at du har en relevant civil uddannelse på akademisk eller teknisk niveau. Det kan være du er ingeniør, data scientist, datamatiker, programmør, eller lignende. Du kan ligeledes have en militær baggrund, hvor du bl.a. har opbygget en lignende teknisk forståelse og erfaring. Det er en fordel, hvis du har opbygget teknisk viden og erfaring inden for it-programmering og dataforståelse samt interesse eller erfaring med analyse og bearbejdning af elektroniske signaler. Men tøv ikke med at søge, hvis du er nyuddannet. Derudover skal du kunne arbejde struktureret og selvstændigt, og trives i et til tider hektisk miljø, som kræver en fleksibel tilgang til opgaveløsningen. Du er kendetegnet ved at være en holdspiller, som er god til at udveksle idéer og sparre med dine kolleger. Du vil blive en del af en afdeling med spændende opgaver, og som vægter faglighed, fleksibilitet og stor frihed i opgaveløsningen højt. Vi kommer fra vidt forskellige baggrunde, men fælles for os er, at vi brænder for opgaven og for at gøre en forskel for Danmarks sikkerhed. Hvis du drømmer om at blive en del af dette team og møder mange - men ikke alle – af de nævnte kvalifikationer til stillingen, opfordrer vi dig til at sende en ansøgning. Din nye arbejdsplads Forsvarets Efterretningstjeneste (FE) er Danmarks udenrigsefterretningstjeneste og arbejder – hemmeligt og åbent – for at beskytte Danmark og danske interesser i en foranderlig verden. Du vil blive del af en helt særlig organisation, hvor vi står sammen om, at løse en vigtig opgave. Mange af dine kommende kolleger brænder for at gøre en forskel, og vi har et stærkt fagligt og socialt sammenhold. Da vi ikke kan tale særlig meget om vores arbejde med venner og familie, så skabes der et helt særligt bånd til dine kolleger. Hos os er det ikke så nemt at tage arbejdet med hjem, da vi arbejder med fortrolige oplysninger. Til gengæld tilbyder vi en høj grad af fleksibilitet i planlægningen af din arbejdstid, og når du ikke er på arbejde, har du helt fri. Vi har et stort fokus på det sociale sammenhold, som understøttes af forskellige arrangementer som for eksempel fredagsbar og brætspilscafé. Du har også mulighed for at tilmelde dig forskellige faglige fora, som går på tværs af organisationen. Vi har desuden en idrætsforening, hvor du kan dyrke forskellige typer motion i selskab med dine kollegaer. Som ansat i FE er du omfattet af nogle særlige vilkår. Det er et krav, at du kan sikkerhedsgodkendes og opretholde sikkerhedsgodkendelsen under hele din ansættelse. items.desc: Vil du være med i et kreativt, tværfagligt team? Interesserer du dig for historie, historiske kilder og arbejdet med historiske data? Er du omhyggelig, nysgerrig og god til at arbejde selvstændigt – og har du måske også interesse for digitale metoder, databaser eller programmering? Så har du nu chancen for at få et studenterjob i vores Data Science-enhed. Om Rigsarkivet Med næsten 1000 års analog og digital samfundsdokumentation er Rigsarkivet Danmarks hukommelse og videncenter for det danske samfunds udvikling. Vi indsamler, bevarer og leverer originale dokumenter og data, der understøtter videns- og retssamfundets behov og skaber nye indsigter og forståelser af vores samfund. I Rigsarkivet bliver du del af en ambitiøs og moderne organisation. I tæt samarbejde med vores brugere arbejder vi kontinuerligt på at være en vigtig spiller i den offentlige digitale infrastruktur, så vores store mængde data skaber størst mulig værdi for borgere, forskere, virksomheder og offentlige myndigheder. Jobbet Som studentermedhjælper vil du blive en del af et tværfagligt team, der arbejder med historiske data og forskningsinfrastrukturprojekter i Rigsarkivet. Du vil primært blive tilknyttet projekterne ChildHomes, Historisk Person Register (HisPeR), MiDiN-DatA og NordHistPop med arbejdsplads i Odense. Dine arbejdsopgaver vil blandt andet omfatte: Transskription og bearbejdning af historiske kilder Transskription, linkning, bearbejdning og beskrivelse af kilder Praktisk assistance til infrastruktur- og forskningsaktiviteter (arrangementer, formidling, m.m.) Ad hoc-opgaver relateret til arbejdet med historiske persondata og forskningsinfrastruktur (søgning af materiale, bestilling af materiale, scanning, kodning, osv.). Arbejdet kræver omhyggelighed og evnen til at arbejde struktureret med historiske kilder og data, som ofte er komplekse, ufuldstændige og ikke entydige. Stillingen kræver desuden en vis grad af selvstændighed samt evnen til at planlægge og prioritere opgaver i dialog med projektlederne. Du indgår i et dedikeret team i enheden Data Science, og der vil være tæt dialog og sparring med sammenlignelige projekter i Rigsarkivet. Om dig Vi forestiller os, at du er studerende inden for historie eller humaniora med en stærk historisk interesse, og at du interesserer dig for historiske kilder, historiske data og digitalt arbejde med arkivmateriale. Vi forudsætter, at du: har erfaring med transskription af historiske kilder fra 1800- og 1900-tallet har erfaring med brug af strukturerede data (f.eks. i Excel eller Access) har kendskab til dansk historie i 1800- og 1900-tallet har erfaring med praktiske støtteopgaver taler og skriver dansk og engelsk kan arbejde selvstændigt og tage ansvar for egne opgaver er aktiv studerende Det er en fordel, hvis du: har interesse for eller erfaring med databaser, digitale metoder eller programmering, herunder Transkribus har arbejdet med Link-Lives-data er interesseret i at anvende nye kilder og metoder i dine studier Om os Du bliver en del af enheden DATA SCIENCE, hvor vi har stor faglighed, engagement og godt humør. Du bliver en del af Team Linking Lab, hvor vi arbejder med fem tæt relaterede projekter (Historisk Person Register, Mapping Freedom, Childhomes, MiDiN-Data og WIDOWS, se https://www.rigsarkivet.dk/om-os/samarbejder-og-projekter/). Du vil arbejde sammen med seks medarbejdere med historiefaglig baggrund og forskellige niveauer af kompetencer inden for programmering og data management og tre data scientister fordelt på lokationerne i København og Odense. Vi tilbyder en spændende hverdag med flere forskellige opgaver og tæt kontakt med teamet, hvor vi hele tiden nørder med historiske datasæt og prøver at undgå i komme ned i alt for mange kaninhuller. Der er desuden andre studentermedhjælpere tilknyttet dataaktiviteter i huset, som du vil have mulighed for at sparre og udveksle erfaringer med. Vi har til huse centralt i Odense med banegården lige om hjørnet. Hos os betyder tilstedeværelse sammen med vores kollegaer meget, og vi mener, at samarbejde og videndeling på tværs af Rigsarkivet er afgørende for et godt arbejdsmiljø. Samtidig vil vi gerne sikre fleksibilitet for vores medarbejdere, og hjemmearbejde aftales løbende mellem chef og medarbejder, når det er foreneligt med opgavevaretagelsen. Det er vigtigt for os, at du får en god start i Rigsarkivet. De første uger er der lagt et introduktionsprogram, hvor du får rig mulighed for at lære dine nye kollegaer og organisationen at kende samt komme godt i gang med dine arbejdsopgaver. Løn og ansættelsesvilkår Du bliver ansat i henhold til den til enhver tid gældende overenskomst mellem Finansministeriet og OAO-S/HK som studerende. Arbejdstiden er gennemsnitlig op til 15 timer om ugen. Vi har fleksible arbejdstider og vægter, at arbejds- og privatliv hænger godt sammen. Stillingen er placeret i Rigsarkivets enhed Data Science, og arbejdsstedet er Rigsarkivet Odense, Jernbanegade 36, Odense. Jobbet ønskes besat 1. februar 2026 …

items.desc: Sorontar is a team of engineers and scientists working to rearm France and its allies. Backed by world-class defense investors and angels, we are building a universal weapon architecture where software, design and manufacturing come together to produce more, faster and at lower cost. A product like this calls for a different kind of company. In most large organizations, layers of management stand between people and their work: ownership fades, knowledge travels slowly and energy goes into coordination. We chose the opposite. We keep Sorontar flat and give that energy back to the work, which is why we look for people who need no management once the direction is set. If a lean team driven by its mission is where you do your best work, you will feel at home here. What you'll get to do At Sorontar, you will manage our relations with customers until the contract is signed. This includes pre-contract agreements, the structuring of contracts and the financing that goes with them, including the government financing tools used for defense purchases. Our technology relies on our production means and can therefore also be used in civilian markets. Most of your work will be in defense, but you will also develop this civilian activity. You will work with the CEO, the Chief of Staff and the Sentinels, who can support you in France and abroad. As the company grows, you will build the business development team. Your profile You have worked in defense and have already sold weapon systems or defense programs to governments. You know how a defense contract is negotiated, structured and financed. You work in French and English. What will set you apart Experience with export contracts is a real plus, as is experience selling industrial products in civilian markets. An existing network with defense customers in France or abroad also counts. We give priority to candidates with several years of professional experience, because this role requires a good knowledge of how defense contracts are won and structured. People who thrive at Sorontar also share four traits: You are an owner. You treat problems as your own and carry them through to the result without waiting to be asked. The mission stays with you. You keep thinking about the problem, because solving it matters to you. You are measured by what you deliver. The result counts more to you than how busy you look. You decide with facts. Evidence weighs more for you than opinions, including your own. What's critical to us We are looking for brilliant, fearless and good people, and we deeply believe that people do not fit into boxes. Yet while a person is a continuum of qualities, a hiring decision is a yes or a no. To make the best decision possible, we assess every candidate on six criteria, grouped in pairs in the matrices below. Make sure you see the graphs on our career page: here. Brilliant. Talent without responsibility leaves potential unused, and responsibility without talent reaches its limits quickly. We look for people who combine the ability to solve hard problems with the drive to see them through. Fearless. Courage without judgment leads to reckless decisions, and judgment without courage turns into commentary. We look for people who see clearly and act on what they see. Good. Integrity without warmth makes a team hard to work in, and warmth without integrity is charm that does not last. We look for people others can rely on and enjoy working with. Our commitment to you The best companies are the ones where you work alongside the best colleagues. Our first commitment is to surround you with people you learn from every day, which is why we hire with great care. Highly competitive salary. We offer €70,000 to €90,000 gross per year, positioned according to your experience. From there, your compensation follows a clear trajectory that rewards the scope and impact of your missions. Equity. Your salary rewards your time, and your equity gives you a share of what your work creates. Full ownership of your scope. You choose how to reach the results you are responsible for, and what counts is the outcome. Leverage. We give you software, automation and the right tools so that your impact grows faster than your workload. Judgment over seniority. Your influence grows with the quality of your decisions, not with your title or your age. The essentials. Days off, full life insurance, lunch covered, and more. items.desc: À propos de nous La Direction des Plateaux Médico-Techniques (DPMT) regroupe deux pôles d’activité médicale (PAM : le pôle imagerie et le pôle de biologie et anatomie pathologique (BAP). Le PAM BAP comprend des activités de biologie médicale, d’anatomie et cytologie pathologiques (ACP), de biotechnologies et des activités cliniques de consultation. Les différents services de biologie et ACP, constituent un laboratoire unique nommé Laboratoire de Biologie Médicale Multi-Sites (LBMMS) dont l'activité est articulée autour de 3 centres de biologie et pathologie (CBP) : Centre de Biologie et de Pathologie Nord (CBPN), Centre de Biologie et de Pathologie Sud (CBPS), Centre de Biologie et de Pathologie Est (CBPE). items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Mécanismes en sciences intégratives du vivant Type de Contrat IT en contrat CDD Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 69008 LYON 08 Durée du contrat 12 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration A partir de 3 175€ brut mensuel selon expérience Date limite de candidature : mercredi 2 décembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions Nous recrutons un(e) ingénieur(e) en analyses de données et approches computationnelles pour travailler sur un projet mêlant biologie du développement et cancérologue pédiatrique. Le poste s’inscrit dans un projet collaboratif européen (ERC SYNERGY), qui a pour but d’étudier le rôle du réseau d’interacteurs des récepteurs UNC5 dans le neuroblastome. La principale mission consistera à développer des modèles in silico du fonctionnement de l’interactome UNC5, à partir de données d’analyses transcriptomiques et protéomiques, et des comportements fonctionnels, générées sur un modèle embryonnaire de transplantation in vivo de cellules tumorales humaines dans leur territoire d’émergence. L'Activité Développement de modèles computationnels : Créer des modèles pour analyser des données de Single-nucleus RNA-seq liées au réseau UNC5. Mise en œuvre d'outils d'IA : Modéliser l'impact de perturbations d’expression des gènes du réseau UNC5 sur la biologie du neuroblastome. Collaboration avec des biologistes : Interpréter les résultats in silico et orienter la conception d'expériences in vivo. Votre Profil Compétences Formation : Formation initiale en mathématiques appliquées à la biologie et en intelligence artificielle. Une expérience confirmée dans l’application de ces expertises en cancérologie pédiatrique sera un atout fort. Une connaissance de l’inférence de réseaux de régulation génique (GRN) serait un autre avantage important. Compétences techniques : Maîtrise de R/Python et des outils d’analyse single-cell (Seurat, CellChat, GSEA…). Une connaissance des bases de données biologiques serait un avantage (UniProt, STRING, Alphafold…). La maîtrise de l’anglais (lu, écrit et parlé) est indispensable. Qualités personnelles : Rigueur, autonomie, prise d’initiative et capacité à travailler en équipe pluridisciplinaire. Un intérêt pour la biologie et la recherche translationnelle sont des atouts. Votre Environnement de Travail Le personnel recruté travaillera au sein d’une unite de recherches de 11 équipes, localisée sur le campus de Rockefeller, en proximité immédiate de plusieurs hôpitaux et autres centres de recherches. Il sera intégré dans un collectif de 5 personnes environ au sein d’une équipe de 15 personnes. L’équipe travaille sur l’étude du neuro-développement physiologique et ses dérégulations dans les tumeurs pédiatriques. items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Institut de Génétique Humaine Type de Contrat IT en contrat CDD Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 34396 MONTPELLIER Durée du contrat 12 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration à partir de 2521,95 euros brut mensuel ajustable en fonction de l'expérience professionnelle sur des postes de niveau équivalent Date limite de candidature : mercredi 2 décembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions La personne recrutée participera au développement et à l'optimisation de méthodes de microscopie de fluorescence pour étudier la dynamique des molécules impliquées dans la régulation de l'expression des gènes en cellules vivantes. Elle contribuera à la mise en œuvre d'approches d'imagerie à molécule unique ainsi qu'au développement d'outils d'analyse quantitative des images de microscopie. L'Activité Mettre en œuvre et optimiser des protocoles de microscopie de fluorescence, notamment pour l'imagerie de cellules vivantes et de molécules uniques. Préparer des échantillons biologiques pour les expériences d'imagerie, incluant la culture cellulaire et le marquage fluorescent. Réaliser des acquisitions d'images et optimiser les paramètres expérimentaux afin d'améliorer la qualité et la reproductibilité des données. Développer et adapter des outils d'analyse d'images, notamment pour la détection, le suivi et la quantification de signaux fluorescents. Participer au développement de méthodes automatisées d'analyse de données de microscopie. Contribuer à l'analyse, à l'interprétation et à la présentation des résultats expérimentaux. Assurer la documentation des protocoles expérimentaux et des outils d'analyse développés. Votre Profil Compétences Formation supérieure en biotechnologie, biologie cellulaire, biophysique, bio-imagerie ou dans un domaine connexe. Connaissances en microscopie de fluorescence et en techniques d'imagerie biologique. Expérience en acquisition et en analyse quantitative d'images de microscopie. Compétences en programmation et en traitement d'images, notamment avec Python et/ou Fiji/ImageJ. Des connaissances en microscopie de super-résolution, en suivi de particules uniques ou en méthodes d'apprentissage automatique seraient appréciées. Des compétences en culture cellulaire et en préparation d'échantillons biologiques seraient un atout. Rigueur scientifique, autonomie, sens de l'organisation et capacité à travailler en équipe. Capacité à communiquer en anglais dans un environnement scientifique international. Votre Environnement de Travail La personne recrutée intégrera l'équipe « Dynamique ARN-Protéines dans l'expression des gènes » à l'Institut de Génétique Humaine (IGH, CNRS et Université de Montpellier). L'équipe développe des approches interdisciplinaires combinant biologie moléculaire, biologie cellulaire et microscopie de fluorescence à molécule unique pour étudier la dynamique de la traduction et les mécanismes de contrôle qualité des ribosomes dans les cellules vivantes. La personne recrutée travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chercheurs et les autres membres de l'équipe et aura accès aux plateformes de microscopie et aux équipements de biologie cellulaire de l'institut. L' IGH est situé sur le campus Arnaud de Villeneuve, partie prenante du programme Objectif Employeur Pro-Vélo. Contraintes et risques Le poste implique l'utilisation de microscopes de fluorescence équipés de sources lumineuses intenses, notamment de lasers, ainsi que la manipulation de cultures cellulaires et de matériel biologique potentiellement génétiquement modifié. Les activités seront réalisées dans le respect des règles d'hygiène et de sécurité applicables. Une présence régulière au laboratoire est nécessaire pour la réalisation des expériences. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy. We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers. We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. Working in international teams alongside colleagues from our development centers in China and Spain, we create innovations for the efficient
items.desc: Who we are The Product Design Center of TK Elevator Innovation and Operations GmbH is responsible for the development of product features, harmonized global product platforms, as well as the conception and development of complete escalator and moving walk system types. Working in international teams alongside colleagues from our development centers in China and Spain, we create innovations for the efficient escalators and moving walks of the future. The international nature of our work is reflected in the close collaboration and regular exchange with experts from various engineering disciplines worldwide. In addition, our proximity to manufacturing at our Hamburg site ensures close integration between development and production, enabling us to support development projects directly on the production line and through their market launch. What we expect You translate elevator drive requirements into control architecture, algorithms, interfaces and acceptance criteria, considering motor–inverter dynamics. You design and tune current, torque and speed control for induction and permanent-magnet motors, including PWM, estimation and fault response. You model and simulate motors, inverters and control loops using MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS or equivalent, supporting MIL/SIL/HIL verification. You implement control firmware in embedded C/C++ or automatically generated code on real-time MCU/DSP platforms, ensuring deterministic execution. You integrate sensing, ADC/PWM synchronization, feedback, communications and protections, considering DC-link, regeneration, power-stage and thermal limits. You validate inverter–motor performance on test rigs and elevator prototypes, diagnose hardware/control issues and coordinate solutions with multidisciplinary teams. Who we are looking for Degree in Electrical, Industrial, Electronics, Automation or Control Engineering, or a comparable discipline. Strong foundations in control theory, signal processing, power electronics, electrical machines and motor-drive dynamics. Practical experience with motor-control algorithms (FOC, PWM, current/torque/speed regulation), modelling and real-time implementation. Knowledge of MATLAB/Simulink or PLECS, model-based development, automatic code generation and embedded C/C++. Experience with MCU/DSP platforms, ADC/PWM, interrupts, timing, numerical robustness and laboratory inverter–motor testing. Ability to work across hardware, controls and firmware teams and communicate in English; HIL, elevator drives, CAN or IEC 61800/EN 81 are valued. This position can be filled in Spain (Mostoles) or Germany (Esslingen). What we offer Health and Safety – Highest standards and a wide range of health promotion and healthcare activities Flexibility – We support, for example, through flexible yet regulated working hours and remote working options Compensation & pension – Fair working conditions, competitive compensation, following “Collective Agreements” and support with pension schemes Collaboration & diversity – Collegiality is of huge importance – we treat everyone with respect and appreciation Development – Individual support to help you get started in your new job as well as training and education programs to help you develop professionally and personally Creative leeway – We offer an environment in which you can try out new solutions in a no-blame-culture Sustainability – We act with responsibility and environmental awareness Attractive Location: Subsidized cafeteria, a convenient location in Hamburg with parking, and excellent access to public transportation. Contact Please apply online in English including your salary expectation and your notice period . items.card: Role Overview: As Quantum Error Correction Scientist (f/m/d), you will contribute to the development of QEC infrastructure, realistic circuit-level noise modelling, decoder benchmarking, logical-performance assessment, and hardware-aware quantum error-correction research. The role offers the opportunity to join at an early stage of eleQtron’s QEC effort, helping to establish the infrastructure that will be key for
items.desc: Full time Hamburg or Siegen eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Our approach combines laser schemes for cooling/initialization/readout, engineered magnetic-field gradient induced coupling (MAGIC) combined with microwave control for universal gate sets, and advanced quantum control techniques and dedicated firmware to work within the high-fidelity regime and below the error threshold of quantum error correction (QEC). A central objective of our technology roadmap is the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing. To achieve this goal, we combine the above high-fidelity quantum hardware with microscopic physics-based modelling, hardware–software co-design, advanced characterization and benchmarking techniques, and detailed numerical simulations to model system performance realistically and identify the optimal QEC strategy and the associated system requirements. As part of our initiative towards fault-tolerant quantum computing, we are expanding our Foundations & Concepts team and are looking for a Quantum Error Correction Scientist (f/m/d) to help establish and grow this strategic activity within the company. Role Overview: As Quantum Error Correction Scientist (f/m/d), you will contribute to the development of QEC infrastructure, realistic circuit-level noise modelling, decoder benchmarking, logical-performance assessment, and hardware-aware quantum error-correction research. The role offers the opportunity to join at an early stage of eleQtron’s QEC effort, helping to establish the infrastructure that will be key for realistic QEC studies and first logical-architecture demonstrations. Responsibilities: Build simulation and benchmarking infrastructure for realistic fault-tolerance studies based on hardware-derived noise models. Analyze logical performance, decoder strategies, resource requirements, and scaling behaviour of quantum error-correction architectures. Collaborate with system operators, architects, and application scientists to connect hardware characterization with logical-level performance assessments. Contribute to early logical-computing demonstrations and the development of eleQtron’s future fault-tolerance capabilities. Required Skills: MSc with an outstanding MSc thesis or PhD in Physics, Quantum Information, Computer Science, or a closely related field. Solid background in quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing (Experience with stabilizer formalisms, decoder frameworks, or realistic noise modelling) Excellent analytical skills in numerical simulations and performance modelling. Ability to work in an international and diverse team at the interface of theory, software, and hardware. Fluent communication in English What you can expect from eleQtron: Competitive salary: We value our team members and therefore provide remunerations that reflect this, additionally rewarding achievements. Flexible working hours: We offer personal freedom through a variety of flexible work schedules. Team spirit: In our international and diverse team, and with our regular team events, having fun at work is simply part of the game. Further development: We want to grow together and so we offer our team members’ needs-based, individualized further training as well as plenty of room for personal development. Wellness Package: We offer health-promoting benefits such as fitness programs like UrbanSportsClub to support your well-being. Moving Benefits: A warm welcome! We are happy to support employees who move for us with a bonus. At the forefront: Work at the forefront of technology, where academic research meets commercial applications. Modern workplace: We have a high-quality infrastructure with laboratory space, offices, and meeting rooms.

Inventory & Asset Management : Active management of inventory levels, prevention of excess stock, and coordination of scrapping and phase-out/clearance processes. Procurement Models & Supplier Integration: Support and continuous development of modern procurement models (consignment warehouses, Just-in-Time/JIT, EDI integrations) as well as monitoring of supplier performance. Escalation & Shortage Management: Proactive risk and shortage management to safeguard production within a globally diversified supplier network. Process Optimization & Digitalization : Participation in digitalization initiatives (e.g., automation of order confirmations, deployment of BI dashboards and modern supply chain tools). This is how you'll win us over: Successfully completed commercial apprenticeship with sound professional experience in operational procurement / MRP control (ideally within the manufacturing industry), ideally supplemented by relevant further education. Excellent understanding of ERP processes (SAP MM/PP) and supply chain KPIs (lead times, delivery reliability, stock cover). Solid knowledge in creating and utilizing BI dashboards (Power BI, DAX) as well as a strong affinity for digital automation solutions and AI-supported procurement tools. Excellent command of written and spoken German and English, combined with strong communication and assertiveness skills in international supplier relations. items.desc: Who we are The Product Design Center of TK Elevator Innovation and Operations GmbH is responsible for the development of product features, harmonized global product platforms, as well as the conception and development of complete escalator and moving walk system types. Working in international teams alongside colleagues from our development centers in China and Spain, we create innovations for the efficient escalators and moving walks of the future. The international nature of our work is reflected in the close collaboration and regular exchange with experts from various engineering disciplines worldwide. In addition, our proximity to manufacturing at our Hamburg site ensures close integration between development and production, enabling us to support development projects directly on the production line and through their market launch. What we expect You translate elevator drive requirements into control architecture, algorithms, interfaces and acceptance criteria, considering motor–inverter dynamics. You design and tune current, torque and speed control for induction and permanent-magnet motors, including PWM, estimation and fault response. You model and simulate motors, inverters and control loops using MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS or equivalent, supporting MIL/SIL/HIL verification. You implement control firmware in embedded C/C++ or automatically generated code on real-time MCU/DSP platforms, ensuring deterministic execution. You integrate sensing, ADC/PWM synchronization, feedback, communications and protections, considering DC-link, regeneration, power-stage and thermal limits. You validate inverter–motor performance on test rigs and elevator prototypes, diagnose hardware/control issues and coordinate solutions with multidisciplinary teams. Who we are looking for Degree in Electrical, Industrial, Electronics, Automation or Control Engineering, or a comparable discipline. Strong foundations in control theory, signal processing, power electronics, electrical machines and motor-drive dynamics. Practical experience with motor-control algorithms (FOC, PWM, current/torque/speed regulation), modelling and real-time implementation. Knowledge of MATLAB/Simulink or PLECS, model-based development, automatic code generation and embedded C/C++. Experience with MCU/DSP platforms, ADC/PWM, interrupts, timing, numerical robustness and laboratory inverter–motor testing. Ability to work across hardware, controls and firmware teams and communicate in English; HIL, elevator drives, CAN or IEC 61800/EN 81 are valued. This position can be filled in Spain (Mostoles) or Germany (Esslingen). Contact Please apply online in English including your salary expectation and your notice period . items.desc: The Kiel Institute for the World Economy is seeking Research Assistants in Economics of Populism (Berlin) . We are looking for up to two highly motivated research assistants to support a new research project on populist leaders in government. The positions are embedded in the research group of Prof. Christoph Trebesch and will be supervised by Dr. Max Deter. The project, “From Populist to Dictator”, builds an event-level database of illiberal actions taken by populist leaders since 1900 and studies how these actions unfold over time and how they relate to economic and financial-market outcomes. It is also part of the SCRIPTS Cluster of Excellence. In this role, you will work closely with postdoctoral scholars as well as more senior faculty of the Kiel Institute to support them in their research. Your Role: As a research assistant in the Research Group of Prof. Dr. Christoph Trebesch, you will play a key role in building the data foundation of the project. The research topics include: Economics of Populism Illiberal actions of populist leaders (e.g. against the judiciary, the media, elections, and state employees) Economic policies of populist leaders Financial market reactions to illiberal actions Economics of Autocracies Sequencing illiberal actions: how and when populists in government turn into autocrats Constraints on leaders and the role of institutions, civil society and international actors Business freedom and cronyism under populist and autocratic rule Your responsibilities will include: Research Assistance Providing research assistance for the project’s data work and for further projects of the group. These tasks include: AI-assisted event coding : using large language models and a structured codebook to extract events (action, date, outcome) on populist leaders from country reports, news archives and academic literature Source verification : checking coded events against the original document, recording verbatim quotes for action, date and outcome, and flagging events that cannot be confirmed Assist in compiling, cleaning and harmonizing the resulting dataset, including checks for duplicates, inconsistent dates and missing sources Assist with documenting research processes (codebook, coding decisions, source logs) and maintaining organized research files and datasets Assist with data visualization, tables, and figures for papers and presentations Conduct background research on populist leaders, country cases and their institutional context Support the preparation of research papers, reports and policy briefs Project Management Assist with day-to-day administrative and organizational tasks Help organize seminars, workshops, and other events (both online and in-person), including managing invitations and participants Your Profile We seek candidates who have the following qualifications and experience: Enrolled in a Master’s program in economics, political science or a closely related quantitative subject in a German University. Applicants should intend to remain enrolled as a student for at least one more year . An excellent academic record Attention to detail , also when working through long documents and large numbers of cases Careful and critical use of AI tools : willingness to check every AI-generated claim against the original source and to document how a result was obtained Strong interest in political economy , including topics such as populism, democratic backsliding, autocracy and political institutions; an interest in geoeconomics, international finance or sanctions is a plus Fluency in English (minimum C1 level). German skills are not required. Previous experience as a research assistant is a plus Reading knowledge of further languages (e.g. Spanish, Portuguese, Turkish, Russian) is a plus Programming skills in Stata or Python are a plus, as is familiarity with Overleaf (LaTeX) or Claude Code . Very good interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills as well as a proactive, solution-oriented mindset Strong organizational skills and the ability to meet deadlines Ability to work independently We are offering Flexible working arrangements; the primary work location is Berlin, with the possibility of remote work. Up to 37 hours/month Research assistant (with completed Bachelor’s degree): 16,20€/hour Fixed-term contract for one year (with the option of extension) Planned start : 1 December 2026. The Kiel Institute for the World Economy values diversity. We welcome applications regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion/belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. The Kiel Institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy. We promote the professional opportunities of women and strongly encourage them to apply. Women with equivalent qualifications, competence and expertise will be given preference. items.card: You will bridge our volumetric heating technology with real-world chemical and separation processes; validating industrial processes at small scale in our lab before rapidly scaling up to pilot and industrial plant size. Tasks & Key Responsibilities In-House Lab Setup: Set up, commission, and operate our small-scale process testing rig in Athens to replicate and validate key industrial process parameters at bench
items.desc: About Solidwatts Solidwatts is a pioneering deep-tech startup decarbonizing hard-to-abate industrial processes. By leveraging our proprietary high-power, solid-state Radio Frequency (RF) heating platform, we replace fossil-based combustion with direct, volumetric, and digitally controllable electrical energy. Our breakthrough approach unlocks step-change efficiencies across gas separations, carbon capture, heterogeneous catalysis, and thermochemical processes. The Opportunity While our core team develops the RF heating and power electronics platform, we are looking for an industrial Process Engineer to own the chemical process side of our systems in Athens. You will bridge our volumetric heating technology with real-world chemical and separation processes; validating industrial processes at small scale in our lab before rapidly scaling up to pilot and industrial plant size. Tasks & Key Responsibilities In-House Lab Setup: Set up, commission, and operate our small-scale process testing rig in Athens to replicate and validate key industrial process parameters at bench scale. Process & Material Adaptation for RF Heating: Investigate how operating conditions, reactor design, and material properties (sorbents, catalysts, supports) interact with volumetric heating, uncovering benefits and solving process challenges alongside our hardware team. Feasibility Testing: Proactively identify promising endothermic processes across chemical and separation industries, designing compact lab trials to demonstrate technology fit and build technical evidence for new verticals. Process Calculations: Perform heat and mass balances, preliminary equipment sizing, and comparative Techno-Economic Analyses (CAPEX, OPEX, energy efficiency, and TCO vs. conventional steam or fired systems). Customer Advisory: Partner with Business Development during technical discussions with industrial clients and process licensors, evaluating baselines, defining validation test plans, and presenting engineering results. External Partners: Define basic engineering requirements to transition validated processes from small-scale testing to industrial plant scale, coordinating with external research institutes and engineering partners. The musts: Industrial Track Record & Education: Degree (BSc or MSc) in Chemical or Process Engineering and a minimum of 4 years of hands-on industrial work experience in the chemical, petrochemical, gas processing, or cleantech industry. Separation Technologies and Catalytic Processes: Proven industrial background in separation technologies (TSA/PSA/VPSA) and/or fixed-bed catalytic reaction processes (Oxidation, WGS, SMR). Reactors & Process Design: Practical experience with test rigs, pilot units, or basic plant operations, translating process conditions into experimental setups, P&IDs, equipment sizing, and heat/mass balances. Industrial & Startup Mindset: A balanced mindset between strategic vision and rapid hands-on lab execution; the pragmatism to move fast on screenings while maintaining strict safety and precision. Planning, execution and communication: Fluent in English, with the ability to manage priorities and communicate effectively with international customers in a project-driven environment. The plus: Thermal & Heating Systems: Prior experience as a process engineer working with steam, hot-gas, or electric heating systems; familiarity with dielectric heating (RF or microwave) is a plus, though we train you on RF. Process Simulation & Modeling Tools: Familiarity with process simulation or engineering calculation tools (Python, MATLAB/Simulink, OpenModelica, structured spreadsheet models, or COMSOL/Ansys). Experimental Instrumentation: Practical familiarity with gas flow control, vacuum systems, temperature sensing, and gas analyzers. Commercial & R&D Project Exposure: Experience supporting customer commissioning, feasibility studies, IP/patents, or collaborative R&D projects. We offer: Large autonomy: work from home, with the needed technical support to fulfill the demanding targets we set. Interdisciplinary working environment and possibility to train for advancement of competences Regular travel to the Swiss office to work with the team directly Working close to the customers and in direct contact with the market reality Competitive salary conditions with the possibility to receive options for participations in the company Job Types: Full-time, Permanent Pay: 25,000.00€ - 28,000.00€ per year Work Location: Hybrid remote in Αθήνα

items.desc: We're rebuilding Cegeka's data foundation by migrating our legacy analytics platform to a modern cloud-based and domain-oriented architecture on Databricks. This shift requires engineers who can keep business-critical legacy workloads reliable while helping us redesign and migrate them into modern, cloud-based production systems. That’s why we are not looking for someone who only wants to build new solutions from a clean slate; we are looking for someone who understands established platforms, can navigate complex legacy logic and dependencies, and can turn that knowledge into stable, maintainable data and analytics solutions on our future cloud platform. This role is for someone who can demonstrate hands-on experience working with legacy data systems and migrating them to modern cloud-based production environments. Experience migrating SQL Server workloads, including data, pipelines, business logic, and operational processes, to Databricks will give you a clear edge over other candidates. If you are a pragmatic Data or Analytics Engineer who understands both legacy and modern data platforms, have experience working in an environment in transition and want to help shape a new cloud-based data foundation from the ground up, read on. What you will be working on As a Data or Analytics Engineer, you will initially own and maintain the data workloads within our SQL Server data warehouse that support Cegeka's critical business processes. You will keep the existing environment reliable by maintaining and enhancing jobs, resolving incidents, improving performance and quality, and supporting changes requested by stakeholders. At the same time, you will build a thorough understanding of its data, business logic, dependencies, and operational processes. Once the migration begins, you will contribute hands-on to implementing, validating, and transitioning these workloads to our new Databricks platform while safeguarding business continuity throughout the change. What you will do Concretely this means you will … Update SQL stored procedures, jobs, and SSIS packages to implement business logic changes requested by stakeholders Improve performance and quality by optimizing ingestion and transformation jobs to ensure data workloads complete on time and without errors Investigate failed jobs, identify root causes in the existing business logic, and implement appropriate solutions Support analysts and help architects define improvements to observability, quality, and performance Resolve incidents promptly and document improvements that strengthen platform stability Build deep knowledge of your team’s data domain to prepare workloads for an efficient migration to Databricks Rebuild SQL Server and SSIS workloads on Databricks, including ingestion, transformation, orchestration, testing, validation, deployment, and production transition Apply modern engineering standards to build, test, deploy, monitor, and support data workloads across the legacy environment and future cloud platform We are looking for someone with ... Professional experience with SQL Server, SSRS, SSAS, and SSIS Experience building and operating data workloads on Databricks using PySpark, Spark SQL, Delta Lake, Databricks Workflows, and Medallion architecture A strong understanding of data warehousing principles, ETL/ELT, and data modeling techniques Proficiency in performance tuning and query optimization through execution plans, indexes, and statistics management Experience reverse engineering complex legacy data systems and documenting undocumented business logic, data flows, dependencies, and operational processes Experience migrating data workloads between platforms and validating data quality, business logic, performance, and operational continuity Experience contributing or giving feedback on the design of new data products and data workloads, including architecture, data models and integration patterns

items.desc: Computer Systems Validation (CSV) Engineer Department: Quality / Validation Job Title: Computer Systems Validation (CSV) Engineer Role Overview Catalyx is seeking a Computer Systems Validation (CSV) Engineer to support the validation of software applications and computerised systems used in regulated pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device environments. The successful candidate will be responsible for authoring, reviewing and executing validation documentation and test protocols, ensuring software solutions meet defined requirements, regulatory expectations and quality standards. The role requires strong technical writing skills, practical CSV experience and the ability to collaborate with Software Development, Testing, Operations and Quality Assurance teams throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). Key Responsibilities Computer Systems Validation and Documentation Prepare, review and execute validation documentation, including Validation Plans, Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), Acceptance Test (AT) protocols and Validation Summary Reports. Independently author clear, accurate and technically sound validation protocols and test scripts, including test steps, expected results and acceptance criteria. Review software requirements and functional specifications to ensure appropriate validation coverage. Develop and maintain Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs). Execute validation protocols, document results and supporting evidence, and manage discrepancies and deviations. Apply risk-based validation principles in accordance with GAMP 5 and applicable regulatory requirements. Regulatory Compliance and SDLC Support Ensure validation activities comply with applicable GxP requirements, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 and internal quality procedures. Apply Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and ALCOA+ data integrity principles. Collaborate with Development, Testing and Quality Assurance teams to investigate and resolve issues identified during validation. Support software change control, impact assessments and release activities. Maintain accurate and traceable validation records to support customer audits and regulatory inspections. Contribute to the continual improvement of validation processes, templates and documentation standards. Qualifications and Experience Essential Requirements Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Science or a related technical discipline. Demonstrated experience in Computer Systems Validation (CSV) within a regulated GxP environment. Proven ability to independently author validation protocols, test scripts and validation reports. Strong technical writing skills, with excellent attention to detail and documentation accuracy. Working knowledge of GAMP 5, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 and risk-based validation principles. Experience reviewing software requirements and functional specifications and developing requirements traceability documentation. Understanding of Good Documentation Practices (GDP), data integrity principles and deviation management. Strong communication, analytical and problem-solving skills. Desirable Requirements Experience validating software used in pharmaceutical manufacturing, automation or machine vision systems. Familiarity with Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles. Experience working within an Agile software development environment. Familiarity with software change control, configuration management and release management processes. Experience using software testing or test management tools.

items.desc: Launch Your Cybersecurity Career with EKCO At EKCO , we’re on a mission to make businesses more secure, resilient, and ready for the future. As one of Europe’s fastest-growing cloud and cybersecurity specialists, we protect organizations against ever-evolving threats, and we’re looking for the next generation of security talent to join us. At Ekco, we believe great careers are built on the right opportunities at the right time. Following the success of our inaugural Graduate Cybersecurity Programme, we are excited to be launching our second programme in Ireland, designed to give you real exposure across seven key pillars: AI Automation, GRC, Security Architecture, Threat Detection & Response, Cyber Resiliency, Security Engineering and Pen Testing. Why Start Your Career at EKCO? Make a Real Impact From day one, you’ll play a part in safeguarding businesses across industries. The work you do won’t sit on the sidelines, it directly strengthens our clients’ defenses against real-world cyber threats. Learn & Grow Fast We know that stepping into the security industry can feel overwhelming. That’s why we provide hands-on training, mentorship, and opportunities to earn industry-recognized certifications. You’ll gain the practical skills you need to turn your studies into expertise. Work with Cutting-Edge Tech At EKCO, you won’t be limited to theory, you’ll get your hands on the latest tools and cloud-native security solutions. From security engineer and incident response to cloud security and compliance, you’ll experience it all. A Supportive Culture We believe in collaboration, not competition. Our teams are open, approachable, and always ready to share knowledge. You’ll be part of an environment where asking questions is encouraged and learning never stops. Clear Career Pathways Your journey with us doesn’t stop at graduate level. Whether you see yourself as a Pen Tester, Security Engineer, GRC Specialist, or Cloud Security Architect, EKCO’s growth means there are opportunities to specialize and progress quickly. What We’re Looking For At EKCO, we know graduates may not have all the answers yet and that’s okay. We’re more interested in your potential, passion, and willingness to grow. Here’s what will help you succeed: Education & Knowledge A degree (or equivalent qualification) in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Security, or related fields. A basic understanding of networking, operating systems, or cloud computing. Awareness of cybersecurity concepts like malware, phishing, vulnerabilities, and risk management Mindset & Attitude Curiosity, you love learning and want to stay ahead of evolving threats. Problem-solving, you see challenges as opportunities to innovate. Adaptability, comfortable with fast-paced environments and new technologies. Integrity & accountability, security is built on trust, and we value people who take responsibility. Collaboration & Communication Team player, willing to learn from colleagues and share knowledge. Clear communicator, able to explain technical findings in plain language to non-technical people. Proactive learner, ask questions, seek feedback, and take initiative. ️ Bonus Skills (Nice-to-Haves, Not Must-Haves) Familiarity with Microsoft, AWS, or Azure cloud platforms. Exposure to security tools (SIEM, firewalls, endpoint detection, vulnerability scanners). Any hands-on labs, projects, or certifications (e.g., CompTIA Security+, Cisco CCNA, Microsoft Fundamentals). Learning & development - Unlimited access to Pluralsight learning platform A lot of responsibilities & opportunities to grow (also internationally)

items.desc: UNIQLO Management Candidate (UMC) Graduate Programme Lead the Future of Retail At UNIQLO, we believe clothing should be simple, high-quality, functional, and built to last, in order to make everyone’s life better. That's the heart of LifeWear. The UMC Graduate Programme is a 12-month accelerated leadership journey designed for ambitious graduates ready to shape the future of one of the world's most dynamic global retailers. Expect a fast pace, a steep learning curve, and the chance to make a real impact in a business landscape that is always evolving, and where your contributions and ideas truly matter. What You'll Gain Throughout the year, you'll be supported by team members, managers and senior leaders who’ve been where you are and are determined to fast-track your career. Mentoring and direct communications with your COO Training in store operations, finance, people management and more Participation to the UNIQLO Europe Leadership Convention in London A network of diverse and supportive colleagues united by a shared purpose Programme Structure Months 1–4 | Discover the Business & Master the Foundations You'll begin by immersing yourself in the engine of UNIQLO: our stores. Your learning will happen directly on the shop floor rather than in an office setting. This is where you'll build a deep understanding of our customers, our products, and what makes our operations world-class. You'll learn and master: Customer service Product deliveries & replenishment Omni-channel & checkout operations Onboarding and training new starters Product category management Months 5-6 | Step into Leadership As a supervisor, you'll begin leading teams on the shop floor, influencing performance, and owning your first commercial responsibilities. This stage develops your leadership stance, building trust, driving results, and bringing out the best in the people around you. You'll take on: Team coordination & daily planning Developing the performance of your colleagues Operational excellence and customer satisfaction Ownership of a key subdivision, ensuring day to day performance Months 7–12 | Drive the Business In your final rotation, on top of maintaining a strong presence on the shop floor as an assistant manager, you'll work alongside the Store Manager to influence commercial decisions and operational strategy. You'll be responsible for: Sales analytics & KPI performance Inventory & commercial planning Layout optimisation & store standards Workforce planning aligned with sales forecasts Team development & succession planning What We Offer: €36600 annual salary, guaranteed bonus & group profit sharing CBA applied: CCNL Terziario Distribuzione e Servizi Full-time permanent contract 30% staff discount across all Fast-Retailing brands Two paid volunteer days per year Opportunities for fast career progression at the end of the programme (Eligibility for promotion every 6 months) Locations: Milan and Rome Minimum Requirements: Bachelor's or master's degree with permanent work authorisation in Italy (Student visa is not accepted) Ready to start full-time end of February or end of August 2027 Minimum B2 level in English and Italian Flexible to work varied shifts across five days per week, including weekends, opening, or closing shifts, and public holidays Open to relocation within Italy Selection Process: Step 1: Online Assessments (Including English and Italian proficiency tests) Step 2: In Person Group Assessment Centre (If you apply to multiple markets, you can only attend one assessment centre) Step 3: Online Individual Interview Step 4: Final Interview If you want to find out more what our UMCs do on a daily basis, click on the link below: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IOOMDphhzRg Commitment to Inclusion and Data Protection UNIQLO is an inclusive employer, and welcomes applications from all backgrounds regardless of age, race, gender, sexual orientation, disability or other characteristics. We are dedicated to safeguarding your privacy and personal information; please refer to our privacy policy for details on our recruitment process. The only exception is for roles advertised in Germany via the HeyJobs platform. UNIQLO takes recruitment security seriously and is committed to protecting the process from misuse. Stay alert and apply only through verified sources. #LI-POST

Medacta’s innovation, forged by close collaboration with surgeon leaders globally, began with minimally invasive surgical techniques and has evolved into personalized solutions for every patient. R&D Software Functional Analyst - Medacta Applied Solutions: Due to the high growth and commitment to technology, Medacta Applied Solutions, a Software Company of the Medacta International Group based in Milan, is seeking for a Functional Analyst / UX & Requirements Engineer to join our software development team. This team is responsible for creating preoperative planning software for orthopaedic surgeries. The selected candidate will work closely with Product Managers, software developers, QA, and other stakeholders to identify, formalize, and document software requirements, transforming user and clinical needs into clear functional specifications, wireframes, and logical flows. This role is key to ensuring that software features are well-defined, unambiguous, and verifiable, contributing to higher product quality, more accurate development estimates, and reduced rework during implementation. The Functional Analyst will also support verification activities, ensuring that implemented features meet the intended requirements. The candidate will be responsible for managing the following activities: collaborate with Product Managers and stakeholders to elicit, analyze, and refine software requirements based on user, clinical, and business needs; translate requirements into clear functional documentation, including: user stories and functional specifications; wireframes and UI mockups; logical flow diagrams and state diagrams. define and document edge cases, error scenarios, and exceptional conditions, with particular attention to usability and safety; act as a functional reference point for the development team, clarifying requirements during implementation; participate in verification and validation activities, reviewing implemented features to ensure alignment with documented requirements; support QA activities by contributing to acceptance criteria and test scenarios; maintain documentation consistency throughout the software lifecycle, managing updates and changes to requirements. Soft Skills excellent communication skills both written and oral; problem-solving mindset and proactive approach; ability to translate complex requirements into clear and structured documentation; proactive attitude and sense of ownership; awarness of the importance of teamwork and collaboration in multidisciplinary environments; ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a regulated and quality-driven context. items.desc: Byondis is an independent, fully integrated biopharmaceutical company in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. We are engineering antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) to tackle cancer and other difficult to treat diseases. Our teams combine expertise in disease biology, linker-drug technology and antibody-drug conjugation to design targeted cancer medicines. Our Nijmegen campus brings together preclinical and clinical development, in-house GMP manufacturing capabilities and regulatory affairs. As a Regulatory Affairs Specialist, you will work directly with the scientists and manufacturing colleagues whose data you use to write clinical trial dossiers. Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities As Regulatory Affairs Specialist, you will join a small and dedicated RA team supporting early development and clinical-stage programs. The team interprets regulatory requirements, prepares and maintains submission documentation, and coordinates Clinical Trial Applications (CTAs) across different regions. Your work will cover CMC, nonclinical and clinical topics for both biological products and small molecules. You will work in multidisciplinary project teams and interact with colleagues across the company, regulatory authorities and CROs. Your responsibilities include compiling and maintaining regulatory documentation, such as IMPDs, IBs, DMF/ASMF and API documentation, and supporting scientific advice activities. You will coordinate the timely availability of documents for CTA submissions and responses to questions from authorities. You will also keep up to date with relevant regulatory requirements and advise project teams on how to apply them. Desired Skills and Experience Your CV and motivation letter should show that you have: A Master’s or preferably PhD degree in life sciences, chemistry or a related discipline; At least five years of relevant experience in Regulatory Affairs, preferably in early clinical development; Experience with ADCs. We also welcome small-molecule experience combined with exposure to biologics during your studies or career. Hands-on experience writing CMC and nonclinical sections of clinical trial dossiers and familiarity with the EU Clinical Trials Regulation. CTIS training or experience is helpful. Experience with CTA submissions in other regions is a strong advantage; Strong organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize effectively, coordinate multiple activities and deliver high-quality work within challenging timelines; The ability to maintain a broad overview while also paying close attention to detail; A proactive, pragmatic, and hands-on approach, with the curiosity to learn new topics and the ability to work independently and take ownership of deliverables; The ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and communicate clearly with internal and external stakeholders; Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain regulatory topics clearly and translate regulatory requirements into practical recommendations; Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to learn new digital tools and systems. Why Join Byondis? On our Nijmegen campus, you’ll work directly with the scientists and manufacturing colleagues developing new cancer medicines. Having research, development and clinical manufacturing on one site means you can discuss the data with the people who generated them and see how your dossier supports a medicine’s move into clinical trials. You’ll take responsibility for the regulatory work on your own project and work closely with the Head of Regulatory Affairs. In a small team, you’ll have room to ask questions, contribute ideas and broaden your experience across the quality, nonclinical and clinical aspects of drug development.
